author: OAG
title: Picturing the bandits
content:
In June, the

Guardian

 published

“Brutal and Emboldened: How Nigeria’s Bandit Crisis Spun Out of Control,”

 a report from Katsina State in Nigeria’s northwest, where communities in local government areas such as Batsari have struck peace deals with the armed groups that have terrorized them for years. The photographs were taken by Terna Iwar, an Abuja-based photographer and artist who traveled with the

Guardian

’s West Africa correspondent, Eromo Egbejule, and a local stringer — without a security escort — to meet one of those groups under a neem tree near the border with Niger.

On the latest episode of the

Africa Is a Country

 podcast, the Nigerian Scam talks to Terna about that encounter: why he kept his camera in plain sight from the moment he arrived, how the group saw itself (as protectors of their communities, not bandits or terrorists), and what the peace deal actually gives them. Access to shops and medicine, and an end to their families’ shame, are on the table; disarmament is not, since other armed groups are still out there. Terna describes a landscape of abandoned towns and clinics, electricity poles without cables, and border posts that barely function. He also reflects on the central dilemma of conflict photography: how to portray people as more than one-dimensional without losing sight of the horrific acts they have committed.

Listen to the show below, and

subscribe

 on your favorite platform.

Sa’eed Husaini

Well, look, I guess we should talk banditry and photography, which are some of the key words for the day. So yeah, we’re talking about banditry and shooting the bandits, quote, unquote, today. And the conversation is with a longtime comrade, collaborator, or friend, Terna Iwar, who’s also a well-known photographer, artist, and creative. So, Terna, thanks for coming on the show, man.

Terna Iwar

Thank you for having me.

Sa’eed Husaini

Homecoming in some ways, right?

Terna Iwar

In many ways, yes.

Sa’eed Husaini

We hope. So feel free to raid the fridge. You don’t need to take your shoes off. The normal protocol. So, this is inspired by a recent article,

“Brutal and Emboldened,”

 a

Guardian

 article about how Nigeria’s bandit crisis is spinning out of control. We want to talk about banditry, but not necessarily only about the dynamics and history and stuff. We’ve had part of that conversation previously with James Barnett, and we’ll have more of that kind of more historical, if you will, conversation going forward. But I think part of what we want to dive into is a bit of the experience, right, of encountering this camp, going to the camp, and shooting, or photographing, the bandits — and then, of course, your assessment, based on that experience, of what the hell is going on with banditry in Nigeria. I’m sure there’ll be elements of the conversation maybe you don’t want to get into right now. We’ll respect that, but of course, as detailed or as granular as you want to get, there’s space for that. And so, just by way of a little bit more background, Terna was part of a team that went up to Katsina, if I’m not mistaken, and had an exclusive interview with at least one camp of AK-47-wielding bandits. Got their perspective, but also kind of hung out with them. They seem pretty relaxed in the photos, and I guess it’d be interesting to get your take on how you got them to be so chilled out in the photos, and what they thought of you as well, shooting at them from the camera. So I don’t know, man. Maybe by way of intro, you could just talk a little bit about how you got into this and what that was about, and how freaked out were your parents hearing that you. . . .  However you want to get into it.

Terna Iwar

Well, again, thank you for having me. Talking about the work I do is not something I often get to do, so I think this might even help me metabolize what that was like. So Eromo, the West Africa correspondent for the

Guardian

, reached out. We’d been talking back and forth for a while about potential stories and stuff that I was working on, what I was interested in doing, and when this came up, he thought that it would be a great fit, since a lot of the work that I’ve been doing in photojournalism revolves somehow around conflict. I just kind of found myself shooting a lot of conflict stuff, banditry, the aftermath of people’s lives changing in the most horrific, drastic ways. Initially, because of the nature of the story, it was very, very tightly kept. I didn’t even know …

author: Randi Beers
title: Expect office, road closures Wednesday for Remembrance Day
content:
Parts of downtown Iqaluit will be closed to traffic Wednesday morning to allow for a Remembrance Day ceremony and march to take place.


The closures will affect parts of Sivumugiaq Street and Mivvik Street starting at 9:30 a.m. until approximately 12 p.m., the City of Iqaluit announced Monday in a public service announcement.


“The closure is necessary to ensure the safety of participants and the public while the march is underway,” said the announcement.


The march, which starts at the RCMP detachment and ends at the cadet hall, is scheduled to start at 10:30 a.m.


Remembrance Day ceremonies are also planned in Rankin Inlet at the Singiituq Complex, from 10:30 a.m. to 11:30 a.m. and Cambridge Bay’s community hall at 10:30.


Government offices across the territory will also be closed to mark the day.


Remembrance Day is observed every year on Nov. 11 to honour armed forces members who have died in the line of duty.

title: C4SS Panelists on the Intellectual Legacy of Don Lavoie
content:
There will be a Molinari/C4SS presence at the 10th annual PPE Society meeting, 12-14 November 2026, at the Westin New Orleans (100 Iberville St.).


I’ve organised a panel on “The Intellectual Legacy of Don Lavoie.” We’re in the very first session of the conference: Thursday, 12 November 2026, 9:00-10:30 a.m. (Central time) in River Room II.


The panel features Cory Massimino (C4SS) on “National Economic Planning: What is Right?” and Nathan Goodman (Mercatus; co-authoring with Molly Rovinski and Karla Segovia) on “Immigration Restrictions as Non-Comprehensive Planning.” Zak Woodman was also scheduled to speak at the panel, on “Ratcheting Up State Power: The Knowledge Problem, the Power Problem, and Legibility,” but will probably not be able to make it.


(This is not to be confused with the panel on the same topic at last month’s Mercatus Markets & Society conference, organised by Nathan Goodman and featuring Jason Byas, Akiva Malamet, and again Cory Massimino.)


Jason Byas, currently in his first year as Assistant Professor in Philosophy and Political Economy at Tulane, is also on the program; he’ll be speaking in a panel on “Anarchism as a Practical Philosophy,” Friday, 13 November 2026, 9:00-10:30 a.m. (Central time) in the Salon Room. Jason’s fellow panelists are Jesse Spafford, Jessica Flanigan, and Billy Christmas.

author: Valerie Anne
title: You Oughta Know That Alanis Morissette Is Pansexual
content:
feature image photo by Credit: NBC / Contributor via Getty Images

It’s official: 90s icon and present-day superstar Alanis Morissette is pansexual. The singer was a guest on the Handsome podcast, which is co-hosted by queer comedians Tig Notaro, Fortune Feimster, and Mae Martin, and they were talking about Alanis’s penchant for a post-breakup rage anthem. Fortune Feimster jokingly asked her, “Did it make you want to be a lesbian at any point?” to which Alanis replied, “I’m pansexual, so yeah.”

The energy in the room was perfect. At first, everyone thought it was a joke (or perhaps that she was being…ironic), but when they clarified that Alanis was serious, they all joked that she should have led with that. You walk into a queer podcast with the queer announcement!!

Granted, this is not the first time Alanis has said she isn’t straight. She has been talking about exploring her sexuality and being attracted to women as far back as 2008, and it was apparently at least partly her idea for her character to kiss Sarah Jessica Parker’s Carrie during her Sex and the City guest spot. It’s just the first time she’s used a specific label out loud.

I considered riddling this intro with Alanis-related puns (like the joke my friend made: she’s got one pan in her pocket…) but I’ll save you the cringe. I’ll just say this news has made me even more head over feet for her.

God is a woman, and she’s also pansexual.

author: Stephen Lerner
title: Trump and technofascism took a hit — now we must act
content:
This article

Trump and technofascism took a hit — now we must act

 was originally published by

Waging Nonviolence

.


The midterm election was a repudiation of Trump and of his Silicon Valley billionaire enablers. This has created a huge opening that we should celebrate — yet we should be clear-headed about the challenges ahead. Victory over Trumpism and Silicon Valley technofascism is by no means assured. Trump’s

appointment of Stephen Miller, a white nationalist

, to chief of staff is a flashing warning sign. 


Trump and Miller have massive power to use the Justice Department, Immigration and Customs Enforcement, or ICE, and other tools of the federal government to target Trump’s opponents. And the Silicon Valley billionaires will use their extraordinary wealth and power to try to crush attempts to stop the build-out of massive data centers, which they desperately need to power their AI expansion. There are growing fears that AI investments have created a stock market bubble that is leaking and ready to burst. The $2.5 trillion sell-off of AI and tech stock on Nov. 5 is a terrifying illustration of how

AI speculation may crash the whole economy

. So while we should breathe in the hope the electoral results have delivered to us, we must also redouble our resolve and prepare for the battles ahead.


Over the past two years, many of us felt overwhelmed, strangled and suffocated by unrelenting attacks that came from every direction, from ICE kidnapping our neighbors, to the U.S. bombing and warring on other countries, to absurd conspiracy theories and racist ranting by Donald Trump, Elon Musk and their ilk. As we can now see, the increasingly vicious nature of their words and actions was also a sign of their weakness and growing desperation. 


Sign Up for our Newsletter


We’ll send you a weekly email with the latest articles.


But weakness and desperation should not be confused with surrender. As our history reminds us, the forces of entrenched power and wealth are nothing if not resilient. They will use every tool at their disposal to deflect or dilute reform, divide their opponents, and prepare countermoves that will roll back our gains. The Reconstruction of the post-Civil War years gave birth to the reactionary “Redeemers,” who succeeded in undoing efforts to advance racial equality. The forward thrust of the New Deal was blunted by the Red Scare. The civil rights gains of the 1960s were challenged by the Southern Strategy and the Reagan Revolution.   


So we should prepare ourselves for the reality that the forces that we have been fighting will not simply throw in the towel. We should not assume that the lawless ways of the Trump presidency will suddenly cease or that its billionaire backers will retreat to the comfort of their gated communities and private jets and cease their efforts to commandeer our future. Far from it. We must expect that they will use every bit of the considerable power they still hold to thwart real change.  


Silicon Valley AI billionaires have made clear that they aren’t content with just becoming billionaires and trillionaires. Their goal is far more expansive and scary. They want to eliminate democracy altogether and replace it with a CEO autocracy. Palantir co-founder Peter Thiel is worth $37 billion and publicly says, “I no longer believe that freedom and democracy are compatible.” 


Defunding AI


The election has shown that the popular mood is behind us. We have a unique window to thwart the Silicon Valley billionaires and to build and exercise power. None of us has a road map of how to do this, but there are some promising paths we can take. A central task is figuring out how we stop funding, bankrolling and purchasing from the technofascist billionaires. We need to stop financing our own destruction. 


There are a series of exciting campaigns already happening

that are trying to do exactly that, and each one offers opportunities for people to be involved individually and organizationally. These campaigns offer, if successful, a vehicle to organize and activate hundreds of thousands of new activists directly in the fight for democracy and against the Silicon Valley AI overlords. 


Previous Coverage


10 reasons to resist AI


The $6 trillion of public employee pension fund assets and $900 billion in university endowments are currently a key

source of capital

 for Musk and other oligarchs. We need to cut off, or at least limit, the massive flow of capital to …

author: Admin101
title: Seattle Event: Anarchists in the Labor Movement Panel and Discussion
content:
This event is co-sponsored by Black Rose/Rosa Negra

,

Seattle Organized Anarchists

, and the

Institute for Anarchist Studies

.


Anarchism emerged as a wing of the workers’ movements in the 19th century. What place do anarchists have in the contemporary labor movement?


Join us for a moderated panel and discussion with anarchists from around the Puget Sound currently engaged in the labor movement as rank-and-file workers, union staffers, and community organizers. 


How do anarchists organize in the workplace? What sets anarchists apart from other political tendencies in labor? How do anarchists relate to unions? And how can anarchists contribute to building workers power from below? 


When:

 Friday, December 4 • 6-8 PM


Where:

 Chinatown-International District, Seattle, WA (specific location details sent upon registration)


Registration is required to attend

!


Click here to register


About the Panelists


JOMO

 is a former healthcare worker and currently organizes with immigrant workers. They write at 

https://substack.com/@chinatowncommune1312


Jorge

 has been organizing in his workplaces for nearly 25 years. Across seven different industries, within four different unions, and in nonunion workplaces too. He has been an elected shop steward, served on contract negotiating committees, organized rank-and-file caucus efforts, and written for Labor Notes. He is a member of

Black Rose Anarchist Federation/Federación Anarquista Rosa Negra (BRRN)

.


Taylo

r is an anarchist organizer and started organizing with the Seattle Solidarity Network (SeaSol) in the middle 00s. In SeaSol (and alongside many talented organizers) she organized for repeated worker and tenant empowerment through dozens of successful direct action pressure campaigns for stolen wages and stolen deposits, including her own. She is a proud IWW member and currently works as a staff organizer for one of the biggest unions in Washington State. In her staff-work she organizes and advocates for continued rank-and-file worker empowerment by sharing with workers many of the same tactics and strategies acquired through her time in SeaSol and the IWW.

author: Frey Blake-Pijogge, Local Journalism Initiative Reporter
title: Attending the Arctic Circle Assembly as an Inuk Youth was transformative and inspiring
content:
Frey Blake-Pijogge helps facilitate a workshop about “the Arctic we are building” on Oct. 9 — part of the Arctic Indigenous Youth Cohort at the Arctic Circle Assembly in Reykjavík, Iceland.

Photo courtesy Oli Haukur Myrdal/Arctic Circle Assembly


The shaking of hands and small smiles welcome me to Reykjavík, Iceland. So does the rain. 


I meet the rest of the Arctic Indigenous Youth Cohort the evening before the annual Arctic Circle Assembly starts, all of us tired after journeying from our many time zones that tightly span the planet’s North. 


On the streets downtown, people are buzzing. Reykjavík feels alive. And everywhere in the city of nearly 150,000, I see signs about the global assembly, held from Oct. 8-10. 


Federal Foreign Minister Anita Anand addresses more than 2,500 participants representing Arctic nations at this year’s Arctic Circle Assembly in Iceland from Oct. 8-10.

Photo courtesy Oli Haukur Myrdal/Arctic Circle Assembly


Every October, the world’s northernmost capital city hosts the

event

, the largest annual gathering of its kind. Organizers

say

 more than 2,500 people from 75 countries attended this year.


Over three days, participants take in the event’s more-than-200 sessions — including panel discussions, round tables, forums, and workshops, their topics ranging from climate change to Arctic sovereignty, military defence, arts, and more. 


The Arctic Indigenous Youth Cohort program is run by the federal government’s

Global Arctic Leadership Initiative

.


Iceland hosted the three-day international assembly at Reykjavík’s Harpa Concert Hall and Conference Centre.

Photo by Frey Blake-Pijogge


The next morning, I arrive at Harpa Concert Hall and take in the ambiance of the crowd: the space is brimming with loud laughter and the steady, excited talking of delegates.


We meet in the designated Youth lounge — each of us bringing their own perspectives and skills from around the Arctic. Our cohort includes Indigenous Youth from “Canada,” the “U.S.,” Greenland, Norway, Finland, and Sweden.


Participants attend a session on at the annual Arctic Circle Assembly in Iceland on Oct. 9.

Photo courtesy Oli Haukur Myrdal/Arctic Circle Assembly


The first day of the assembly goes by in a blur, as I’m jet-lagged and still getting used to the three-hour time change.


I attend sessions on the geopolitics of

polar climate research

; one on why media coverage of the Arctic is the “

final frontier in public interest reporting

”; how the region today is seen through the eyes of Youth leaders; and short presentations by student researchers from fields of biology, law, language, children, and computer science. 


All three days’ sessions are unique, yet echo similar themes.


It’s clear that Indigenous peoples are at the forefront of many of the international discussions. 


An Oct. 9 session hosted by the Pulitzer Center brought media experts together to talk about ‘All eyes on the Arctic, the final frontier of public interest reporting.’

Photo courtesy

Darryl Lyon


Graduate students from around the world present their Arctic research across academic disciplines.

Photo courtesy Oli Haukur Myrdal/ACA


“Indigenous peoples have so much richness to offer,”

said

 the Inuit Circumpolar Council’s international chair Aluki Kotierk, former president of Nunavut Tunngavik. “I think states realize that.


“Many Indigenous peoples from the Arctic … have been very instrumental in Arctic diplomacy, and even globally.”


For the rest of the assembly, whether meeting people outside of panels or at the Youth lounge, I feel a huge sense of awe to see how us Inuit from all around Inuit Nunangat are at the forefront of these urgent global discussions. 


Youth at the Arctic Circle Assembly hold a discussion during the events.

Photo courtesy Oli Haukur Myrdal/Arctic Circle Assembly


Another thing I notice is how powerfully Inuit are showing up at the event — representing our culture through our voices, leadership and perspectives, adorned with our beaded earrings, our silapak (pull-over top), our furs, and our kakiniit (tattoos) and tunniit. 


Throughout the assembly, I meet people who are Sámi, Iñupiaq, Métis, Inuvialuk, Gwich’in — and from many other nations.


READ MORE:


Indigenous leaders give the UN a roadmap for protecting their peoples


They fill me with a powerful sense of shared kinship I’ve not experienced anywhere else, except with other Indigenous people.


Simply put, I hold this kinship …

author: Marcelle Edenlord
title: Idaho’s OB/GYN Crisis was on the Ballot: Despite Idaho Voting No, the Nation Voted Yes
content:
Following the overturning of Roe, Idaho state law criminalizes abortion at all stages, except in the context of rape or incest that has been formally reported to law enforcement or to prevent the death of the mother. Within fifteen months of the ban’s enactment, 60 OB/GYN physicians stopped practicing obstetrics in Idaho.

As of 2024, 43% of obstetricians have stopped practicing, left the state, closed their practices within the state, or retired in response to harsh legislation. This has left over half of Idaho’s 44 counties without obstetricians, leaving the 23 practicing OB/GYN’s to serve 569,000 Idahoans.

This flight of providers is not a coincidence but rather a clear response to legislation that poses major threats to individuals seeking obstetrician services and physicians. The law’s narrow exceptions and criminal penalties can leave providers concerned about whether an abortion is legally permitted when a patient’s health is at risk. Physicians can be subject to two to five years in prison and risk losing their medical license and being sued for up to $20,000 per family member who chooses to file a lawsuit. This said, the ban’s language is unclear and has left many doctors unsure how to legally interpret the state’s policies and limitations, despite the significant consequences that can follow misinterpretation.

Additionally, this legislation specifically targets women in rural areas, as it causes them to travel significantly more to reach care. One doctor shared, “I have definitely seen people arrive to our hospital much sicker than they should be, and that’s all due to the time that they have to travel.”

This is specifically dangerous for pregnant women, as they are uniquely vulnerable to life-risking complications. Reports state several instances of hemorrhaging pregnant women being airlifted out of state to receive urgent, life-saving abortion care. Given that rural areas have already been reported to struggle to retain and recruit doctors, policies that cause massive flights of physicians are detrimental to women in rural areas and across the state.

As tragic as this is, it is in no way surprising, as 90% of the US has better maternal pregnancy outcomes than Idaho. Since these restrictive policies have been enacted, three labor and delivery wings have closed. Additionally, doctors of all specialties are seven times less likely to apply to work in states with restrictive abortion policies for their residency training.

The effects of Idaho’s abortion laws were also at the center of the state’s November 3 election. Idahoans had the opportunity to vote for safety and health through the Reproductive Freedom and Privacy Act. Tragically, the proposition failed. This said, it lost by 82,807 votes, with 385,716 voters sharing support. This act would have enabled reproductive healthcare decisions to be made between a doctor and patient without the state’s influence until a fetus is viable. It would additionally have freed providers and patients alike from the threat of punitive consequences.

As devastating as this loss is, abortion was on the ballot across the nation and Idaho’s loss is the minority. In Nevada, Missouri and Virginia, abortion rights have been defended or established. Idahoans deserve to have the opportunity to make private decisions with their providers about their healthcare. Providers should not have to choose between their professional obligations and state law. Nationally, the country is reckoning with the heartbreaking consequences anti-choice legislation has caused. Idaho will see justice prevail; it’s just a matter of time.

author: Victoria Valenzuela
title: Incarcerated Los Angeles Youth Fought for the Right to Hug Their Parents — and Won
content:
This story was co-published with


Truthout

.


Mercedes Maradiaga sat across from her 19-year-old son in the Los Padrinos Juvenile Hall in Los Angeles in complete devastation. Her son had at that point been incarcerated at the prison for two years and she had visited him every weekend. But that day in September 2024 was especially hard because it was their first visit since he had been beaten by officers earlier that week in a space in the jail where there were no cameras. The guards had jumped on and kicked him, and he needed surgery for a torn ACL. All she wanted was to give him a hug and reassure him that she was there. However, because of the no-contact visit policies at Los Padrinos, she was unable to give him that comfort.


Even during birthdays and holidays, they weren’t allowed to embrace. The boy endured the jail’s horrible living conditions — including rat infestations and flooded toilets — but couldn’t hug his mom for a moment of escape.


“I couldn’t even let him know I’m here just with the little hug,” Maradiaga said. “It would have meant everything to him. It was sad, and I did that for four years.”


Los Padrinos had

reopened a year earlier

 in 2023, after being shut down in 2019 due to conditions that violated the Board of State and Community Corrections (BSCC) standards, including abuses by staff. Six officers were criminally charged with

assault and child abuse

 for using pepper spray on several teenage girls. Reports

also cited a decreasing youth population

 as a factor for closure, yet staff

claimed to feel “outnumbered.”

 When Los Padrinos closed, youth were shuffled to another facility called Central Juvenile Hall — and then in 2023, that facility was closed down due to similar issues. Los Padrinos reopened, and just months later, the abuses restarted. In 2025,

30 officers were criminally charged

 by the California Attorney General with child endangerment and abuse, conspiracy, and battery for encouraging “gladiator fights” that pit youth against each other.


Olivia Shields, a justice transformation policy coordinator at Urban Peace Institute, described the constant closing and reopening of BSCC facilities as a “cycle of noncompliance.” Shields said the Los Angeles County Probation Department has ultimately failed with these maneuvers to address the core issue: unmet youth needs — which won’t be addressed through incarceration but through coordinated care in the form of individualized, robust support systems and resources.


“Rather than decarcerate these populations of young people and find community-based alternatives or step-downs for as many of them as possible, they basically shift the youth around from facility to facility to avoid noncompliance,” Shields said.


Long before the closing of Los Padrinos in 2019, the facility had a bad reputation among Angelenos. Maradiaga recalled hearing disturbing stories about the facility in the ’80s when she was a kid.


“I think it needs to be shut down,” Maradiaga said. “I think that there needs to be a better way for the youth. I don’t think locking them away from their family is the answer.”


The Appeal in Your Inbox


Subscribe to our newsletters for regular updates, analysis and context straight to your email.


          Sign Up


Barred From Basic Human Contact


When Ilana Parach, executive director and co-founder of

Hoops 4 Justice

, went inside Los Padrinos with a basketball and mentorship program, she quickly learned about what youth were facing inside. She felt it was important to give them a platform to express their needs directly, so she pivoted to working with them on legislation.


“They made a list of specific programs they wanted — resources for their families, reentry support,” Parach said. “At the bottom of that list, they wrote, ‘We want to hug our moms.’”


Incarcerated youth directly told her that one parent who hugged her son during a visit on his birthday then had her visit terminated and future visits suspended for two weeks. She said another youth was incarcerated for three years and had no choice but to watch his mother cry during the visits because she couldn’t hug him.


Contact visitation policies vary across California and are often left at the discretion of correctional officers. Parach said youth and staff both told her that Los Padrinos stopped allowing contact visits after the pandemic. Parach said that during meetings of the board of supervisors, she heard officers citing staffing shortages …

title: In the Crosshairs of the Far-Right Advance : An Update on Anti-Fascists and Anarchists in Greece
content:
Anarchist graffiti from Athens, Greece (2026)


The anarchist movement in Greece faces a new wave of repression. Urged on by the US and its obsession with combatting “far-left extremism,” the Greek state has targeted anti-authoritarians with new legal charges and attacked demonstrations, while fascists carry out street attacks and plot their return to the halls of power. Amidst a landscape of ongoing austerity, terrorism designations, lethal prisons, and ferocious wildfires, anarchists nonetheless continue to forge a combative culture of revolutionary solidarity.


In this article, we present an interview with an anarchist comrade in Athens assessing the current situation among anarchists and anti-fascists in Greece, along with analysis of the US’s role in advancing state repression and fantasies of Western supremacy.


The US and Greece: A Right-Wing Alliance to Defend “The West”


Earlier this month, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio delivered a speech at the Pnyx in Athens. With the historic Acropolis and the Parthenon—that ancient symbol of Western democracy, constructed with slave labor—in the background, he delivered a warning message to Greece’s political and business elite.


“The course we take will determine whether the West maintains its place at the head of the world or resigns itself to a future of atrophy and servitude and decline,” Rubio cautioned. “We will either choose to act now or lose the choice to act at all.” Lamenting how “nationalism became a dirty word,” he called for renewed militarism, praised Christian faith and martyrdom, and announced a new counterterrorism information-sharing program between the two countries. His statements were calculated to reinforce the colonial legacy of Western dominance over the rest of the world, while urging the worst of Greek society to imitate America’s current political trajectory.


US Secretary of State Marco Rubio constructs an elaborate photo op for his defense of nationalism, militarism, and “the West” (October 7, 2026).


The speech came in the wake of a conference Rubio convened in July that aimed to coordinate intensified repression against “far-left extremism.” The following month, the US government imposed a “global terrorist” designation on the Italy-based

Autistici/Inventati (A/I) tech collective

, which operated the free publishing platform NoBlogs.org.


Greece’s right-wing politicians and business leaders benefiting from the country’s endless austerity measures are heeding Rubio’s call to preserve the hubris of the so-called West. Meanwhile, governments are collaborating to escalate repression against any truly revolutionary movements that challenge the world’s current status quo.


Greece’s strategic importance to Western powers is rooted in its symbolic status as the birthplace of “Western Civilization,” as well as its strategic location in the world today. The country offers the US access to four military sites, including a dedicated Navy base in Crete’s Souda Bay. Those with a longer memory have not forgotten how the US supplied napalm to Greece’s fascist forces, who worked with the Nazis during World War II and later with the British and US in a Cold War anti-communist alliance. Fascists dropped American napalm on Greek partisan resistance fighters during the civil war from 1946 to 1949, scorching bodies and charring forests, leaving the countryside scarred to this day.


More recently, the Greek people were pummeled by the 2008 global economic crisis, brought on in part by Wall Street firms such as Goldman Sachs that raked in immense profits while destabilizing the world’s economy and immiserating millions. The US then contributed to the austerity measures imposed on Greece in 2010 by the International Monetary Fund (IMF), leading to years of ferocious resistance to neoliberal capitalism and government complicity.


Today, Greece’s current New Democracy regime upholds

the legacy of the brutal military junta

 of 1967-1974, promoting the image of Greece as a symbol European supremacy as invoked by Rubio. Despite its nationalist rhetoric, the government continues to lick the boots of the US, crushing opposition in the streets and enforcing a never-ending precarity on the majority of Greece’s increasingly exhausted and numb population.

title: Enzo Traverso: “La revuelta juvenil tiene una dimensión política evidente”
content:
Paris 2026: «siamo tutti antifacisti»


https://www.facebook.com/reel/1145355668017795


.


Enzo Traverso: “La revuelta juvenil tiene una dimensión política evidente”


Enzo Traverso

 


06/11/2026


En “Supervivencias de la revuelta”, el historiador pone de relieve la “vida póstuma” de las experiencias emancipadoras, a contracorriente de los relatos nacionales. En una entrevista con Mathieu Dejean para Mediapart, descifra los vínculos subterráneos que unen esta memoria rebelde y el movimiento social actual.


Contra la despolitización y la anestesia del pasado, el historiador Enzo Traverso, profesor de la Universidad de Cornell (Ithaca, Nueva York), revive las memorias rebeldes. Después de 

La melancolía de izquierda 

(2016) y 

Revolución 

(2022), su nuevo libro, 

Supervivencias de la revuelta. Ensayo sobre la dialéctica de la memoria 

(2026) -en francés en las ediciones La Découverte- cierra esta trilogía advirtiendo a los ciudadanos contra las políticas de memoria regidas por las instituciones e invitándolos a apropiarse de la tradición de los oprimidos.


“Esta memoria de las revueltas es subterránea, discreta, pero surge de forma imprevista”, 

escribe. El 17 de octubre de 2026 es una demostración de ello: varias capas de memorias rebeldes se entrecruzaron, desde el 17 de octubre de 1961 en la Comuna de París en 1871. Vuelve, en una entrevista con 

Mediapart

, sobre lo que el movimiento social actual lleva de recuerdos y sobre sus potencialidades, a pesar de la incertidumbre, para finalmente 

“dejar la época contemporánea”.


“Mediapart”: Un alto funcionario de la policía dijo, sobre el 

17 de octubre

: “Era la Comuna de París el día del Black Friday. ¿No es la memoria anti Comuna la que se manifiesta con fuerza desde esa fecha?


Enzo Traverso: 

Hay algo asombroso en la posteridad de la Comuna de París, que tiene tanto el estatus de paradigma para las memorias rebeldes -resurge constantemente, no solo en Francia, sino a escala global- como para el pensamiento reaccionario. Ha proporcionado un repertorio de figuras, referencias, símbolos, imágenes en la cultura reaccionaria, que se ha reactivado constantemente durante un siglo y medio.


De hecho, este es el caso desde el 17 de octubre, no solo en Francia sino también en Italia, donde se invocan los mismos motivos -la civilización amenazada por la barbarie, los salvajes que se apoderan de los centros de las ciudades-, con una dimensión xenófoba y racista particularmente importante. La juventud de los suburbios postcoloniales actúa como un nuevo chivo expiatorio. Un imaginario reaccionario global está tomando forma.


¿Cuáles son las referencias adoptadas precisamente de la memoria anti Comuna?


Si pensamos en la literatura anti Comuna, Théophile Gautier calificó a los protagonistas de la Comuna de París de 

“bestias”, 

“animales apestosos” 

y 

“venenosos” 

escapadas de un zoológico, que hacen estragos en la ciudad porque el guardián se olvidó de cerrar la jaula. Son los mismos clichés que se propagan hoy.


Una gran figura del pensamiento reaccionario de la época, Alphonse Daudet, dijo al día siguiente de la Comuna: 

«¡París estaba en manos de los negros!

 Es una racialización y una animalización de la revuelta y los rebeldes que, en una continuidad asombrosa, perduran hasta nuestros días.


En ambos casos, podemos destacar la negativa de los gobernantes -en este caso Emmanuel Macron, Sébastien Lecornu y Laurent Nuñez- a 

cuestionar las causas sociales y políticas de la revuelta

. Como en la Comuna de París, la revuelta es para ellos un fenómeno mucho más biológico que social. Lo que explica la revuelta es la naturaleza racial o religiosa de los rebeldes, aunque muchos jóvenes blancos fueron muy activos el 17 de octubre. En su imaginación, hay que ver al rebelde como un cuerpo ajeno a la nación.


En términos más generales, parece que el pueblo ha permanecido, en la mente de las élites gobernantes, una “multitud vil”, como dijo Adolphe Thiers.


Esta es una observación interesante, porque lo que también llama la atención es el relativo silencio de la extrema derecha, que a menudo se califica de “populista”. A menudo ha reivindicado la ira legítima de las clases populares contra el 

establishment

, del pueblo virtuoso contra las élites corruptas. Pero a diferencia de 2017 y 2022, Emmanuel Macron se encuentra en tal estado de derrota que Rassemblement national (RN) se ha ganado la confianza de las élites dominantes, de las que se ha …

title: Juzgado de Loncoche confirma propiedad indígena a favor de mujer mapuche y en contra de Forestal Mininco
content:
En 1991 la Forestal Mininco se apropió de 28.5 hectáreas de tierras indígena del sector Molul Pidenco, que doña Marcelina Curin Neculpan heredó a su hija Reineria Briseño Curin, mujer mapuche de 70 años. Una sentencia del Juzgado civil de Loncoche redactada el 26 de octubre, resolvió


que los demandantes “son dueños del inmueble rural” y ordenó “la cancelación de la inscripción” que favorecía a la empresa.


Por Morín Ortiz.


Aliviada y contenta se encuentran Reineria Briseño Curin y su familia, al conocer la resolución del Juzgado de Garantía de Loncoche, que reconoce el dominio legítimo de las tierras que heredó, tras la muerte de su madre Marcelina en 1987. Lo que desacredita judicialmente la versión de la Forestal Mininco, empresa que en diciembre de 1991 inscribió a su nombre las 28.5 hectáreas en el Conservador de Bienes Raíces de Loncoche. 


Sustentados en un contrato de compraventa que realizó la empresa con Luisa Curiqueo Curin, luego de que esta aprovechara una prolongada hospitalización de su hermanastra y heredera, Reineria Briseño Curin, para sacar de su casa el documento de propiedad y vender el terreno. Sin comunicarse con la familia Briseño Curin, ni entregarles parte del dinero recibido. 


Hechos que doña Reineria y su abogado, Mauricio Reidenbach del Centro de Investigación y Defensa Sur, denunciaron como fraudulentos. Debido a que la Forestal Mininco regularizó este predio mediante el Decreto Ley N° 2.695, promulgado en 1979 por el Ministerio de Bienes Nacionales, “vulnerando la protección que merecen las tierras indígenas a través de nuestra legislación”, lo cual se confirmó con la sentencia dada a conocer el 26 de octubre.

Para este juicio, abogados y antropólogos reconstruyeron la historia de esta tierra ubicada en la reserva indígena Huemal Curín, desde los registros más antiguos hasta el actual título de dominio. “Evidenciando que el predio se lo adjudicó la madre de la demandada, mediante Ley de Propiedad Austral, y luego se transfirió el dominio a sus herederos”, explicó el abogado Reidenbach. 


Una de las pruebas presentadas por la defensa, fue el Documento de Concesión de título del Fisco a nombre de la madre de Reineria. Resguardando que, según lo informado por la Dirección General de Tierras y Colonización “en virtud de lo dispuesto en los art. 12 y 14 de la Ley de Propiedad Austral. Concédese a doña Marcelina Curin Neculpan, título gratuito de dominio de un predio de 28 hectáreas 50 áreas, ubicado en Pidenco, comuna de Loncoche”, firmado en Temuco en 1956, como copia del documento original de 1939. 


Lo que fue considerado en la sentencia firmada por Renán Latin Quezada, Juez titular del Juzgado de garantía de Loncoche, señalando que, si bien la empresa “cuenta con un título inscrito, éste es una inscripción de papel, mientras que la actora ha adquirido los derechos en la sucesión de su madre por lo que ésta procede de dicho justo título”, refiriéndose a la figura de dominio por sucesión a causa de muerte que indica el artículo 722 del Código Civil. 


Judicialización y hostigamiento 


En las lomas de este predio, la familia Briseño Curin cosechaba 300 sacos de avellanas, más de mil kilos de trigo, y producía su propia harina. Cultivaban arvejas, habas y papas. Recolectaban hongos como la lengua de vaca, el loyo, el pique, los digüeñes, el gargal, se oía canta a las chicharras, se podían avistar tordos y pidenes. Recuerda Reineria de sus años en Molul Pidenco, donde nació, aprendió a ser campesina, se casó y formó familia.

“Hoy apenas nacen digüeñes, y si salen, están sucios porque el pino bota basura y químicos. ¿Cuántos pájaros se perdieron por consecuencia de las forestales? ¿Cuánta vida se ha perdido en estos 40 años?”, observa doña Reineria, señalando que “la forestal hizo el camino por encima de la casa de mi mamá. Con esto me destruyeron en vida”. 


A sus 33 años, Reineria salió del campo para educar a sus cuatro hijas. Dos años antes de tomar esta decisión, enfermó de gravedad y debió vivir largas hospitalizaciones. En esta ausencia fue que su hermanastra Luisa viajó desde Puerto Aysén, donde vive, para vender el terreno a la Forestal Mininco. Ante esta situación, las dirigencias de AdMapu, Ana Llao y José Santos Millao, recomendaron iniciar acciones legales contra la forestal para obtener su título de dominio y restaurar el imperio del derecho.

Estas tres décadas de hostigamiento empresarial y policial han desgastado la salud física y mental de Reineria, según …

author: anred
title: Los testimonios que la Iglesia no escuchó: víctimas del Opus Dei y Próvolo reclaman justicia y una respuesta del papa León XIV
content:
Mónica Zambrano (i), Claudia Carrero (c), y Tita Villamayor participan durante la primera cumbre internacional de ECA (Ending Clergy Abuse) sobre ‘Los Abusos del Opus Dei en Argentina’, en Buenos Aires (Argentina). Imagen: archivo EFE/ Matías Martin Campaya.


Este martes 10 de noviembre, a las 15, se realizará en Buenos Aires una conferencia de prensa de Ending Clergy Abuse (ECA) para llevarle un mensaje al Papa León XIV ante la falta de respuesta a las 43 mujeres que denunciaron haber sido sometidas a explotación por el Opus Dei y a los sobrevivientes de abuso sexual del Instituto Próvolo. La convocatoria fue difundida por la periodista y escritora Paula Bistagnino, quien sigue el caso de las 43 mujeres y publicó un libro sobre sus denuncias. La presentación estará encabezada por las autoridades de ECA.

La actividad se produce luego de que el Pontífice mantuviera un encuentro con cinco víctimas de abusos cometidos por integrantes del clero y de instituciones eclesiásticas, seleccionadas por la Iglesia local. Entre quienes no fueron recibidas se encuentran las mujeres denunciantes del Opus Dei y sobrevivientes del Próvolo. ECA cuestionó que la jerarquía eclesiástica argentina haya quedado a cargo de decidir quiénes podían acceder a esa reunión y reclamó transparencia, reconocimiento y reparación. Por ANRed.


“

Hoy a las 15 en Buenos Aires habrá una conferencia de prensa para dar un mensaje al Papa León XIV ante la falta de respuesta a las mujeres sometidas por el Opus Dei y a los chicos y chicas del Instituto Próvolo

. Estará encabezada por las autoridades de Ending Clergy Abuse (ECA)”. Así lo anunció la periodista

Paula Bistagnino

, quien investigó y publicó sobre las denuncias de 43 mujeres que acusaron al Opus Dei de trata de personas y explotación laboral.


 


Ver esta publicación en Instagram


 


Una publicación compartida por Agencia de Noticias Red Acción (@anredaccion)


La convocatoria se produce después de que

León XIV mantuviera un encuentro privado con cinco personas víctimas de abusos cometidos por integrantes del clero y de instituciones eclesiásticas del país

. Según informó la Oficina de Prensa de la Santa Sede, las cinco personas fueron presentadas por la Iglesia local y el encuentro duró más de una hora. Sin embargo,

entre quienes no fueron recibidas se encuentran las 43 mujeres que denunciaron al Opus Dei y los sobrevivientes del Instituto Próvolo

. La noticia generó cuestionamientos por parte de organizaciones que reclamaban una audiencia para trasladarle al Pontífice sus denuncias y demandas.


Desde ECA cuestionaron que la selección de las personas que accedieron al encuentro haya quedado en manos de las autoridades eclesiásticas argentinas, sin que se informaran los criterios utilizados ni los casos a los que pertenecían las víctimas recibidas. “Respetamos profundamente a las cinco personas y lo que cada una de ellas fue a decirle.

Nuestro reclamo es con un mecanismo que dejó en manos de la jerarquía eclesiástica argentina la decisión de a quién escucha el Papa. Esa jerarquía es justamente la institución cuya respuesta frente a los abusos está en discusión

”, expresó

Sergio Salinas Giordano

, abogado de víctimas del Próvolo y director de ECA Global. También sostuvo: “

Un comunicado así no genera esperanza en la Iglesia: genera desconfianza

”.


El testimonio de las mujeres que sufrieron la servidumbre del Opus Dei


Uno de los casos que estará en el centro de la conferencia es el de las

43 mujeres que denunciaron haber sido captadas durante su infancia o adolescencia por el Opus Dei y sometidas a explotación laboral

. Según sus testimonios,

fueron incorporadas bajo promesas de educación, alojamiento y formación, pero terminaron realizando durante años tareas domésticas sin remuneración, con jornadas extensas, restricciones a su libertad y situaciones de encierro y violencia psicológica

. En septiembre de 2024 presentaron una denuncia formal ante la Justicia argentina. La Procuraduría de Trata y Explotación de Personas (PROTEX) impulsó medidas judiciales contra integrantes de la organización por presunta trata de personas y explotación laboral.

El Opus Dei niega las acusaciones

.


También reclamarán por

los niños y niñas que sufrieron abusos sexuales en el Instituto Antonio Próvolo de Mendoza

. Las víctimas eran personas sordas e hipoacúsicas que asistían al establecimiento religioso de Carrodilla, en Luján de Cuyo.

author: Agência Mural
title: Construção: filhos de pedreiros que migraram para São Paulo buscam novas profissões
content:
Antônio Pedro de Lima, 54, e Naldo José Leite Lima, 50, têm algumas coisas em comum. Moradores de

Paraisópolis

, na zona sul de São Paulo, os dois chegaram à capital vindos do Nordeste em busca de trabalho e de uma vida melhor.


Começaram na construção civil como ajudantes de pedreiro, não concluíram o ensino fundamental e passaram boa parte da vida em uma profissão marcada pelo esforço físico. Ambos também são pais: Naldo tem três filhos e Antônio, quatro. Nenhum dos filhos, porém, quis seguir o mesmo caminho profissional.


A diferença está nas oportunidades. Quando chegaram a São Paulo, Antônio e Naldo encontraram na construção civil uma das poucas possibilidades de trabalho. Os filhos cresceram com acesso à educação, cursos e projetos sociais que ampliaram as opções de profissão.


Breno ao lado do pai, Antônio, que trabalhou na construção civil para sustentar a família


O tema virou polêmica este ano, quando um empresário da construção civil reclamou da

falta de mão de obra

.


Antônio veio de Murici, em Alagoas, em 1994, aos 22 anos. Chegou à cidade com uma promessa de trabalho que o irmão havia conseguido para ele. Na República, região central, começou fazendo manutenção em um hotel, lixando paredes e pintando. Depois, foi trabalhar em

Itaquera

 como ajudante de pedreiro. Foi ali que aprendeu o ofício que marcaria sua trajetória.


Com seis meses eu já sabia de muita coisa. Foi quando comecei a pegar esses conhecimentos e a levantar minha casa em Paraisópolis”


Antônio


pedreiro


Foi com o trabalho de pedreiro que Antônio sustentou os quatro filhos, entre eles Breno Tenório, 26, publicitário. Ainda criança, Breno percebia os efeitos da rotina do pai.


“Quando a gente é criança, não consegue traduzir muito essas coisas. Mas sempre senti a ausência dele em casa. Via meu pai chegando cansado e via meu pai saindo de madrugada, ainda escuro. Eu pensava: ‘Imagina como é difícil sair de casa às quatro ou cinco da manhã’”, lembra o publicitário.


A mesma realidade atravessou a trajetória de Naldo. Paraibano, ele chegou a São Paulo em 1995, aos 19 anos, para trabalhar na construção civil, em um emprego conseguido por primos. Iniciou a jornada como ajudante e aprendeu o ofício na prática. Foram mais de dez anos dedicados às obras, período em que também aprendeu pintura, encanamento e elétrica.


Gustavo Lira e o pai, Naldo, que trabalhou como pedreiro e atualmente é eletricista


“Quando comecei, não entendia de nada, mas fui aprendendo como ajudante. Era muito puxado. Porque a maioria das pessoas que vieram do Nordeste na minha época não tinha serviço além de coisas pesadas. Lá também é pesado o serviço, só que era diferente. Era agricultura, na roça”, relembra.


Durante os anos de obra, tijolos, concreto, pedras e sacos de materiais fizeram parte da rotina.


Carreguei muito tijolo, concreto, encher laje na mão. Você carrega pedra, carrega cimento, saco de 50 quilos praticamente. Não é fácil, exige muito do corpo da gente”


Naldo


eletricista


O filho, Gustavo Lira, 26, diretor de fotografia, cresceu vendo os efeitos dessa rotina.


“Meu pai chegava cansado, só tinha tempo de tomar banho, jantar e dormir para acordar cedo de novo. Durante anos, sempre vivi essa cena”, compartilha o jovem.


Outros caminhos


Breno acompanhou o pai levantar cada cômodo da casa da família. Mesmo assim, nunca se interessou pelo ofício. Quando criança, chegou a ajudar algumas vezes a carregar tijolos, mas logo corria para longe do trabalho pesado.


“Sempre corri, nunca quis ficar carregando peso não”, recorda, aos risos, enquanto conversa com o pai.


Com o tempo, Breno passou a enxergar que a escolha profissional também estava ligada às oportunidades que cada geração teve. Para ele, trabalhos essenciais para o funcionamento das cidades continuam concentrados entre populações mais pobres e migrantes, enquanto outros grupos têm mais possibilidades de escolha.


Breno, publicitário, afirma que busca oferecer uma vida melhor ao pai


Ele encontrou outro caminho por meio da educação. Antes de chegar à faculdade de publicidade, participou de cursos gratuitos de teatro e informática e de diferentes projetos sociais, que considera fundamentais para ampliar suas oportunidades.


Hoje, formado e trabalhando na comunicação, olha para a trajetória do pai, que continua atuando de forma autônoma na construção civil. Antônio teve carteira assinada apenas uma vez, em 1999. Para Breno, o custo desse trabalho não pode ser medido apenas …

author: Darío Aranda
title: Día de la Maestra y el Maestro Rural: sembrar el derecho a la educación en cerros, llanuras y bosques
content:
Por Marcela Isaías


El primer día de su trabajo Leila quedó largas horas empantanada en el camino hacia la escuela. Ese fue su bautismo como maestra rural en el norte santafesino. Sandra enseña arte en secundarias rurales de Entre Ríos; todo el tiempo denuncia el mal estado de las rutas y la fumigación de los campos con agrotóxicos. El femicidio de la directora correntina Nancy Godoy le llegó muy de cerca. Adolfo da clases en un pueblo jujeño cercano a La Quiaca, en sus tareas diarias incluye la huerta escolar como un espacio de encuentro con las familias.


Ni heroínas ni apóstoles. Historias que hablan de cómo trabajan maestras y maestros rurales para garantizar el derecho a la educación.


Norte de Santa Fe


Leila Díaz vive en Tostado, cabecera del departamento 9 de Julio, bien al norte de la provincia de Santa Fe. Desde el año pasado es maestra reemplazante, siempre en la ruralidad. Su primera suplencia la hizo en una escuela rural ubicada a unos 44 kilómetros de Tostado. Una buena parte del trayecto hasta ese establecimiento es por un camino de tierra, y sí o sí lo tiene que hacer en un vehículo propio. “La primera vez que fui me llevó mi papá. Hacía dos días había llovido y en el primer charco nos quedamos”, repasa ese recuerdo que atesora.


Con ella viajaba la cocinera de la escuela. Llevaban las provisiones de comida para la semana, la garrafa, agua, además de los materiales y útiles para las clases. Debieron caminar varios kilómetros hasta el cruce con la ruta para buscar ayuda.


Leila había soñado con ese primer día de trabajo como maestra, “nunca con algo parecido” a lo que pasó. Igual siguió adelante y se enamoró de la enseñanza rural: “Lo maravilloso fue cuando llegamos a la escuela, conectamos el wi-fiy mandé un mensaje al grupo de las familias para que sepan que iba a haber clases. A los dos o tres minutos empezaron a llegar todos los niños y las niñas. Ahí entendí lo importantes que somos”.


Foto: Gentileza Leila Díaz


Vivir la semana en el lugar donde enseña es parte de su trabajo. Por lo general, quienes permanecen en estas experiencias son la docente, que hace también tareas de dirección al ser personal único, la portera o cocinera y la maestra de nivel inicial. “Las tres solitas en el medio de la nada”, dice recordando una noche de tormenta en la que además se cortó la luz.


Leila se explaya en la charla sobre su vida familiar, su hija pequeña, su marido. Del intercambio que tiene con sus alumnas y alumnos, que enriquecen la experiencia pedagógica y remiten al legado freiriano: “Siento que me escuchan, que se llevan algo de mí, como yo me llevo de ellos, porque siempre me están enseñando”.


En ese ir y venir de relatos, reconoce que no puede dejar de pensar en lo que le pasó a Nancy Godoy, la docente correntina víctima de un atroz femicidio. “Pude haber sido yo o cualquiera de mis compañeras. Todas nos sentimos identificadas con ella”, comenta ese sentimiento de espanto colectivo.


“Después de lo que pasó con Nancy —continúa— te preguntás hasta qué punto te podés exponer. Más cuando, en Santa Fe, un reemplazo lo cobrás a los 60 días”.


Las condiciones laborales, en particular la movilidad, se vuelve un tema ineludible, atraviesa todo el tiempo la conversación con quienes ejercen en la ruralidad. Si hay que hacer dedo “siempre tratamos de ser dos o más, ir en grupo”. Pide más empatía a quienes tienen a su cargo las escuelas y exigen llegar sí o sí a dar clases, “sin importar a costa de qué”.


Cierta vez viajaba en auto junto a otras maestras a dar clases a la localidad de Esteban Rams, a 77 kilómetros de Tostado. Por la imprudencia de otro conductor estuvieron a poco de un accidente: “Nos salvamos de milagro”. Es ineludible la mención a la tragedia del 27 de mayo de 2013, ocurrida en el norte santafesino y en la que perdieron la vida diez personas, entre ellas siete maestras. Pasaron más de diez años y el reclamo para que se atienda el traslado cuidadoso de la docencia rural sigue pendiente.


Daniela Spárvoli fue víctima de femicidio en 2003 - Foto: Amsafe Delegación Iriondo


Nancy y Daniela


El femicidio de Nancy Godoy puso en la agenda pública otra vez el trabajo de las docentes rurales. Nancy era de Esquina (Corrientes) y desde agosto pasado ejercía como directora suplente en la Escuela Rural N° 626, en el Paraje El Malezal. Un lugar al que le demandaba horas llegar por distintos medios, incluso a caballo. A poco de asumir su cargo denunció el abandono en el que encontró la …

author: La Zarzamora
title: Lanzamiento de Black Onions, un listado de sitios web anarquistas y antiautoritarios con extensión .onion
content:
Publicado originalmente en Montréal Contre-information

Nos complace anunciar el lanzamiento de Black Onions, una nueva iniciativa que tiene como objetivo ofrecer una lista estable y actualizada periódicamente de sitios anarquistas y antiautoritarios con extensión .onion. Los sitios .onion son sitios web accesibles a través del navegador Tor mediante direcciones que terminan en «.onion».

En los últimos meses, algunos gobiernos han atacado las infraestructuras de comunicación de nuestros movimientos con renovado vigor; buena prueba de ello son la conferencia internacional sobre el «terrorismo de extrema izquierda» celebrada en Estados Unidos en julio, así como la inclusión del proveedor de servicios de alojamiento militante italiano Autistici/Inventati en una lista de sanciones relacionadas con el terrorismo a finales de agosto.

Para bien o para mal, la comunicación pública de nuestros movimientos tiene lugar en gran medida en Internet, lo que la hace vulnerable a los mecanismos tecnológicos de censura. A diferencia de los sitios web convencionales, los sitios .onion son menos vulnerables a la censura, ya que no utilizan nombres de dominio y permiten ocultar la ubicación del servidor, del mismo modo que el navegador Tor oculta tu propia ubicación al visitar el sitio. Consideramos que los sitios .onion son nuestra mejor baza para seguir comunicándonos en línea dentro del movimiento anarquista, especialmente si los intentos de censura se intensifican en el futuro.

El problema recurrente de los sitios .onion es que sus direcciones, compuestas por 56 caracteres aleatorios, son imposibles de memorizar. Black Onions tiene como objetivo resolver este problema. Te recomendamos guardar en los marcadores del navegador Tor, o en un archivo en tu ordenador, las direcciones .onion que utilizas habitualmente; pero si necesitas una dirección que aún no has guardado, ¡encuéntrala en Black Onions!

Accede a Black Onions a través de cualquiera de las siguientes direcciones:

– blackonions.gd – blackonions.li – blackonions.st – (próximamente, una dirección .onion)

Para establecer una base de confianza en esta nueva iniciativa, los siguientes proyectos anarquistas han avalado nuestra propuesta mediante declaraciones firmadas con PGP: Act For Freedom Now!, un proyecto de contrainformación activo desde 2008 , y el No Trace Project, un proyecto contra la represión activo desde 2021.

¡Utiliza sitios .onion! ¡Resiste a la censura!

author: Administrador
title: A QUÉ VAMOS. QUÉ SÍ Y QUÉ NO
content:
Atención Familias Buscadoras, sin o con colectivo: Atención quienes acompañan a familias buscadoras:

Éste es el primero de varios textos donde iremos aclarando algunas dudas que hemos recibido, responder a algunas ofensas e insultos, e irles dando a conocer poco a poco parte de la agenda de la delegación. Por favor les pedimos estar pendientes de éste y los siguientes escritos.

A.- Hemos detectado una serie de confusiones, malhabladas e intentos de manipulación sobre los objetivos, fechas, lugares y actividades de la delegación de la Comisión Sexta Zapatista para estos meses de diciembre, y la primera semana de enero del 2027.

Se habla y se malinforma de una supuesta reunión nacional entre familias buscadoras y la delegación zapatista en la llamada “Glorieta de los Desaparecidos” el 6 de diciembre, y de otras actividades públicas de la Comisión Sexta Zapatista en otros lugares y fechas.

Esto es falso, compañeras y hermanas buscadoras. Tal vez sí tengan una su reunión quienes se convocan en ése o en otros sitios como referentes a su justa lucha, pero nosotros no participaremos ahí.

No sólo porque la “invitación” que recibimos de ahí refleja ignorancia, mala fe y grosería. A nadie se le invita insultándolo. En su oportunidad explicaremos más sobre eso. También porque no vamos a reuniones masivas con familias buscadoras.

Los grupos, colectivos, colectivas y familias buscadoras que se reúnen en las glorietas o donde sea, pueden reunirse EN PRIVADO con nosotros, grupo por grupo, en la sede de la delegación en la Ciudad de México y en las sedes que se harán públicas, registrándose vía el Frayba, en la fecha y hora que les convenga, si así lo desean.

B.- Miren, ustedes y nosotros, los pueblos zapatistas, sabemos que tienen no sólo diferencias sino francas rivalidades y disputas, mismo entre colectivos de buscadoras, entre redes y movimientos. Incluso hasta llegar a tratar de vetar a ciertos colectivos y a decretar quién sí y quién no se reúne con la delegación zapatista. Tal vez por eso crece el número de familias buscadoras que no están en ningún grupo o colectivo, y que nos contactan directamente.

Nosotros no vamos a juzgar a nadie. No vamos a decir cuál estrategia es correcta o errónea, cuál es legítima y cuál no, cuál es buena y cuál es mala.

Consideramos que, quien busca verdad y justicia y tiene el objetivo de encontrar a quien le hace falta a causa de una desaparición forzada, puede y debe recorrer todos los caminos y tocar todas las puertas para aliviar su dolor.

Sea que hacen búsqueda de campo con pico y pala; sea que recurren a las instancias judiciales locales, estatales y federales; sea que quieren reunirse con la titular del ejecutivo federal o con su pirámide de funcionarios; sea que hacen campañas internacionales y nacionales; sea que sólo alcanzan a pegar las fotos de sus ausentes en sus calles y barrios, sea que recurren a Organizaciones No Gubernamentales de Derechos Humanos; sea que solicitan el apoyo de especialistas en búsqueda de desaparecidos y análisis de restos humanos; sea que recurren a marchas, mítines, plantones, tomas de edificios y bloqueos de calles y carreteras; sea rezar; sea maldecir; sea todo lo anterior.

Y siempre con la memoria como motor.

Sea lo que sea que decidan y hagan, es una decisión de ustedes, de quienes cargan ese dolor y sufren esa angustia, y de nadie más.

Entonces no vamos a decirles qué hacer ni a hacerlo por ustedes. Vamos a conocerlas, a escucharlas, a abrazarlas.

Ni vamos a decir cuál red o colectivo es mejor que el otro.

C.- Por eso nuestro viaje no privilegia actos de masas, ni mediáticos, ni asambleas generales ni creación de alianzas, frentes o cosas parecidas, ni una nueva organización que englobe o incluya a todos los colectivos y familias buscadoras, o a parte de ellas.

Tampoco vamos a discutir o a debatir el número de personas desaparecidas, si son 135 mil o son más o son menos, porque esos números tienen un nombre, una historia, una tragedia, un dolor, y un deber: el de buscar a quien se ama, a quien hace falta y, no pocas veces, a quien es sangre de su sangre.

D.- La principal intención de esta iniciativa es escuchar a cada familia o grupo de familias buscadoras que quiera contarnos su historia y, sobre todo, la historia de su ausente.

Porque nosotros hemos visto y escuchado su caminar, sus esfuerzos, sus sacrificios, si no rendirse en la búsqueda, su no vender a su ser ausente, su no claudicar en la memoria.

Y les pedimos, si es que …

author: Unknown
title: YPG internationalist Konstantin Gedig remembered in Kiel
content:
This Saturday, the seventh annual commemoration of Konstantin Gedig – Şehîd Andok Cotkar was held in Kiel. Andok was martyred on October 16, 2019, in an attack by the Turkish Air Force on the western Kurdish border city of Serêkaniyê (Ras al-Ain), in violation of international law. Since 2016, he had fought against the Islamic State (ISIS) as a member of the People’s Protection Units (YPG). To this day, Andok’s killing has had no political consequences for Turkey, a NATO member, and there is still no information about the whereabouts of Konstantin’s body.


Shortly after 3 p.m., the Kurdish Community Center in Kiel was filled to capacity. More than 100 friends, comrades and family members gathered in the hall, lovingly decorated with flowers, flags and photographs, to commemorate Konstantin Gedig – Şehîd Andok Cotkar and remember his struggle. They came to remember Konstantin, the humorous and lively person, the son, the friend, the brother, the farmer, the student of Kurdish, the medic and the fighter for justice. They also came to remember the struggle for freedom waged against ISIS and Turkey’s war of aggression. In this struggle, Andok and 11,000 other fighters lost their lives, while 19,000 were wounded, in an effort to protect the lives of countless others.


“When you lose your child, every memory is sacred”


In a moving speech, Konstantin’s mother, Ute Ruß, once again described how the family had experienced his journey to Rojava. On September 1, 2019, Konstantin contacted his family to say that he was on his way to Sulaymaniyah to join the fight against ISIS. From that moment on, time took on a different meaning for the family: researching the political situation in North and East Syria, searching for photographs of Andok and hoping for signs that he was alive.


Since his killing seven years ago, their daily lives have been shaped by efforts to reconstruct Andok’s final moments, the search for his body and the struggle for justice. Even today, new information about Andok, a fighter and frontline medic, continues to emerge: small mementos handed over to the family, stories shared by fellow fighters and photographs brought to them. This year’s invitation to the commemoration, for example, features a photograph of Andok taken in the summer of 2017, which filmmaker Pedro Brito da Fonseca gave to the family.


The struggle for justice is directed against what the family describes as deliberate attempts by the Turkish and German governments to erase the memory of Andok. Ute Ruß spoke in harrowing terms: “Nothing terrible is impossible. The Turkish state’s treatment of fallen enemies is profoundly degrading. Graves and bodies are desecrated on an unimaginable scale. Families have to beg for the return of their loved ones’ remains. A dead person is no longer treated as a human being; they are degraded, regarded as dirt in the eyes of the Turkish state.”


The search for Andok’s body has been made more difficult, according to the family, by the German government’s lack of interest and its unwillingness to confront Erdoğan. As a result, even seven years after Andok’s death, there is still no grave where his family can mourn him with dignity.


A special form of remembrance is the Konstantin Andok Literature Prize. Awarded since 2023, the prize is supported by Konstantin’s parents and was initiated by the Soli-Netz solidarity network, with contributors including Dario Azzellini, Yossi Bartal, Christian Baron, Jörn Boewe and Kerem Schamberger. Nearly 500 entries were submitted for the third edition of the competition, held under the motto “Speak. Write. Break the silence.”


During the commemoration, an excerpt was also shown from a laudatory speech delivered by Christian Baron at the most recent award ceremony. Baron emphasized that, under capitalism, literature and art must always take a stand against the existing order, exploitation, oppression and NATO wars waged in the name of Germany’s

raison d’état

.


The flower of Heval Andok


Musical performances accompanied the commemoration. As has almost become a tradition at these gatherings, 

Zana û Andok

 was sung, a tragic song about comrades Zana and Andok, who symbolize the pain and resistance of the Kurdish resistance movement. Following performances of 

Ez Nisêbin Tu Qamişlo

 and 

Çû

, everyone joined together to sing 

Bella Ciao

, including a verse rewritten in honor of Heval Andok.


Thus ended a deeply emotional, yet beautiful and defiant Saturday …

title: দুনিয়া কাঁপানো শরৎকাল
content:
এরকম এক শরৎকাল প্রত্যক্ষ করার পর এক রকমের আশা জাগে – বসন্ত আসতে হয়তো বেশি দেরী হবে না।


 


দেবারতি


গুপ্ত

  


 


এ এক অন্য শরৎকাল এসে হাজির হয়েছে দুনিয়া জুড়ে। লেট ক্যাপিটালিজমের নখ দাঁত যেভাবে প্রকট হয়ে উঠেছে গত দুই দশকে তাতে সাধারণ মানুষের নাভিশ্বাস উঠতে শুরু করেছে। মিলেনিয়াল প্রজন্ম এই পরিস্থিতি একভাবে মোকাবিলা করেছে। তাদের যৌবনে তবু কিছু চাকরি ছিল মন ভোলানোর উপাদান ছিল। কোভিড পরবর্তী কালে যে প্রজন্ম যৌবনে পা দিয়েছে তারা পেয়েছে এক অবাক পৃথিবী। একদিকে সমাজ মাধ্যমের বিভ্রান্তিকর দুনিয়া আরেকদিকে নতুন হাজির হওয়া কৃত্রিম বুদ্ধিমত্তা। এইসবের মধ্যে দুনিয়াজোরা সরকারি শিক্ষা ব্যবস্থা, স্বাস্থ্য পরিষেবা আর কর্মসংস্থানের চূড়ান্ত বেহাল অবস্থা।


 


বছর দুই আগে থেকেই সার্বিয়ার ছাত্ররা বিক্ষোভ শুরু করেছিল। নোভি সাদ রেইল স্টেশনের ছাত ভেঙে ১৬ জনের মৃত্যু হওয়ায় ছাত্রদের বিরোধিতা শুরু হয়। ওই কান্ড নিছক দুর্ঘটনা বলে চাপা দেবার চক্রান্ত সহজে মেনে নেয় নি সার্বিয়ার ছাত্ররা। তারা আন্দোলন শুরু করে। সেই আন্দোলন দীর্ঘ ১৪ বছর ধরে ক্ষমতায় থাকা আলেক্সান্ডার ভুচিচকে সম্প্রতি গদিচ্যুত করেছে।


 


২৬ অক্টোবর, অর্থাৎ সার্বিয়ার ওই ঐতিহাসিক দিনে বেলগ্রেড থেকে এক সফটওয়্যার ইঞ্জিনিয়ার লাজার পেত্রোভিচ ‘কফি হাউস এক্সপেরিয়েন্স’ এর লাইভ পডকাস্টে এসেছিলেন। এই মুহূর্তে কলকাতা শহরে যেখানে প্রতিদিন ফ্যাসিজমের উপস্থিতি হাড়ে হাড়ে টের পাচ্ছি সেইখানে বসে সার্বিয়ার পার্লামেন্টের সামনে দাঁড়িয়ে উচ্ছ্বসিত লাজারকে দেখতে পাওয়া, নিঃসন্দেহে খুব আশাব্যঞ্জক ঘটনা। মজার কথা হল দক্ষিণপন্থী ভুচিচের এস এন এস (সার্বিয়ান প্রগ্রেসিভ পার্টি) দলের বিরোধী যে রাজনৈতিক দলগুলো – গ্রিন লেফট পার্টি বা ডেমক্রেটিক পার্টি এরাও ছাত্রদের দলের কাছে পাত্তা পায় নি। ক্ষমতাসীন বা তথাকথিত বিরোধী দুই পক্ষের প্রতিই গভীর অনাস্থা থেকে Student List বা Students Are Winning দলটি তৈরি হয়েছিল। লাজারকে জিগ্যেস করেছিলাম যে ছাত্র আর সার্বিয়ার সুশীল সমাজের যে প্রতিনিধিদের নিয়ে ওরা ক্ষমতায় এল তাদের রাজনৈতিক আদর্শ কি? লাজার জানালো ওদের গত দু বছরের লড়াই কোন নির্দিষ্ট রাজনৈতিক আদর্শের ভিত্তিতে গড়ে ওঠে নি। তাদের দেশের সংকট যেখানে পৌঁছেছিল তাতে শিক্ষা, স্বাস্থ্য আর নিরাপত্তার মতো মৌলিক অধিকার নিয়ে তাদের লড়াই করতে হয়েছে। লাজারের দেশের শাসনব্যবস্থা তথা রাজনীতি কোনদিকে এগোয় তা বোঝার জন্য আমরা নিশ্চই অধীর আগ্রহে তাকিয়ে থাকবো সার্বিয়ার দিকে।


 


এবার মুখ ফেরানো যাক বিপ্লবের পীঠস্থান ফ্রান্সের দিকে। সেখানেও ছাত্রদের নেতৃত্বে বিরোধিতা শুরু হয়েছে।


 


প্রায় দু’মাস হতে চলল ফ্রান্সে ছাত্র আন্দোলন চলছে। প্রাথমিক ভাবে যেটা শুরু হয়েছিল প্যারিসের এক শহরতলি এলাকার উচ্চ বিদ্যালয় বা Lycée-র ছাত্র-ছাত্রীদের মাধ্যমে, তা পরে আরও ব্যাপক ভূমিকা গ্রহণ করেছিল। শিক্ষক-শিক্ষিকারা, অধ্যাপক-অধ্যাপিকারা, স্কুল ছাড়াও কলেজ-বিশ্ববিদ্যালয়ের ছাত্র-ছাত্রীরা, তাদের অভিভাবকেরাও মিছিলে নিয়মিত সক্রিয় অংশ নিচ্ছিলেন। হাই স্কুল ছাত্র-ছাত্রীদের মূল দাবী ছিল সরকারি স্কুল গুলোর পরিকাঠামোর উন্নতি,  কারণ সরকারি স্কুলগুলোয় যথেষ্ট শিক্ষক নেই, ফলে একেকটা ক্লাসে একজন শিক্ষকের দায়িত্বে অনেক বেশি ছাত্র। স্কুল বিল্ডিং এর অবস্থা ক্রমশ খারাপ হয়ে পড়ছে। অতিরিক্ত গরমে বা অতিরিক্ত ঠান্ডায় সেই সব ঘরে ক্লাস করা খুব মুশকিল হয়ে পড়ছে। গত বাজেট সেশনে শিক্ষা ক্ষেত্রে বাজেট অনেক কমানো হয়েছে। ফলে এই সবকিছু নিয়েই ছাত্ররা বিক্ষুব্ধ। সম্প্রতি সরকার এদের কিছু কিছু দাবি মেনে নিয়েছে কিন্তু তবুও আন্দোলন থামেনি। কারণ ছাত্ররা বলছে এটা যথেষ্ট নয়। যা সমস্যা রয়েছে আরও গভীরে গিয়ে তার সমাধান করতে হবে। ফলে স্কুল কলেজ ব্লক করা অব্যাহত রয়েছেl এই ব্লক করার একটা নাম তারা দিয়েছে – ব্লকাস (Blocus)


 


কথা হচ্ছিল ফ্রান্সে বসবাসকারী অধ্যাপক সোমঋতা ভট্টাচার্যর সঙ্গে। সোমঋতা কঁ-নর্ম্যান্ডি ইউনিভার্সিটিতে (Université de Caen-Normandie) ইংরিজি পড়ান। অকে জিগ্যেস করেছিলাম, ম‍্যাক্রোঁর সেন্ট্রিস্ট সরকারের বিরুদ্ধে যদি আন্দোলন জারি থাকে তাহলে কি তা লা পেনের দক্ষিণপন্থী দলকে জোরদার করবে? না কি বামপন্থী জাঁ লুক মেলেশঁদলেরও সম্ভাবনা তৈরি করতে পারে?


 


সোমঋতা আন্দোলনের বিস্তারের কথা জানালো। প্রতিবাদী ছাত্র-ছাত্রীদের সঙ্গে শ্রমিকশ্রেণী যাঁরা ইয়েলো ভেস্ট (gillet jaune) মুভমেন্টে অংশ নিয়েছিলেন, অবসর প্রাপ্ত মানুষ যাঁরা কিছু দিন আগে অবস্র গ্রহণের বয়স বৃদ্ধির বিরুদ্ধে প্রতিবাদে অংশ নিয়েছিলেন, তাঁরা সকলে একে একে জড়ো হচ্ছেন। কারণ দ্রব্যমূল্য বৃদ্ধি, মানুষের ক্রয়ক্ষমতা কমে যাওয়ার সঙ্কট একটা ভয়াবহ আকার নিয়েছে। তবে আশার কথা এই যে, ছাত্র আন্দোলনে কিন্তু মেলেশঁর সমর্থক বেশি দেখা যাচ্ছে। নিয়মিত ছাত্রদের পাশে থেকেছেন মেলেশঁ, তাদের প্রতিবাদে অংশ নিয়েছেন। অন্যদিকে ছাত্রেরা স্পষ্ট ভাবে মারিন লো পেন এবং তাঁর অতি-দক্ষিণপন্থী দলের সমালোচনা করছে এবং প্রতিবাদী ছাত্ররা তাদের বিরোধী মিছিলে এমন কিছু পোস্টার নিয়েও এসেছে যেখানে পরিষ্কার লেখা রয়েছে, দক্ষিণপন্থী দলদের তারা কোনও ভাবেই সমর্থন করছে না এবং অতি-দক্ষিণপন্থীদের বিভেদ, বৈষম্যমূলক কার্যকলাপের সম্পূর্ণ বিরোধিতা করছে এবং ভবিষ্যতেও করে যাবে। অর্থাৎ সার্বিয়ার মতো ছাত্র বিক্ষোভ থেকে বিদ্রোহ ছড়িয়ে পড়েছে নানান ক্ষেত্রে। তবে ফ্রান্সে রাজনৈতিক আদর্শ …

title: Natatanging Gawad honors journalist RJ Ledesma
content:
by

 Reachelyn Esona


Journalist RJ Nichole Ledesma’s pen was for the oppressed. He never left the side of the marginalized.


On the 9th Gawad Bayani ng Kalikasan, Ledesma’s work was conferred the Natatanging Gawad on October 24 for his exemplary dedication and service to farmers and indigenous people in their struggle for their right to land.


Ledesma was among the Negros 19 who was killed in Toboso, Negros Occidental on April 19. He was 30 years old. 


Read:

Bullets rained down in Toboso, residents tell fact-finding team

 


Ledesma was on assignment on that fateful day. He was looking into the situation of peasant communities where solar farm expansion and wind-energy developments. 


In a press conference before the ceremony, AlterMidya Chairperson Raymund Villanueva narrated Ledesma’s bravery who immersed with the community not just to report or write but to  take part in the people’s collective struggle to protect the environment and the rights of the farmers, fisherfolk, indigenous people, and other underrepresented groups.


“This recognition for RJ is part of a significant contribution to our call for justice for him, for his fellow martyrs in the Toboso 19, and justice for all slain environmental defenders.” Villanueva said.


Ledesma was recognized for his coverage on land disputes, renewable energy projects, palm oil expansion and reclamation. He also documented life stories of sugar workers, landless farmers, and communities facing possible displacement. 


Among his notable works was an investigative report on the proposed 6,000 hectare palm-oil plantation in

Candoni, Negros Occidental

 where he documented farmers and Indigenous People’s problem regarding land, livelihood, and the project’s social and environmental impacts.


Beyond community journalism, Ledesma established his own platform for creative writing and literary expression. He founded

SPIT zines

 in 2017 where he promoted literature. He was also chosen to join

Silliman

 University National Writers Workshop and

9th Amelia Lapeña-Bonifacio

 Writers Workshop as a poetry fellow.


In 2020, he led Paghimutad-Negros where he took roles as a writer and editor of a publication that focuses on human rights reporting and grassroots storytelling. Later on, he became a regional coordinator of AlterMidya Network in Negros Island.


Aside from Ledesma, Gawad Bayani ng Kalikasan also honored other organizations and individuals for their commitment to environmental defense.


The Gawad sa Organisasyon was received by Barikada ng Mamamayan ng Sibuyan represented by Elizabeth Ibanez, Alyansa ng Novo Vizcayano Para sa Kalikasan led by Fr. Vicente Tiam, and Jalaur River for the People’s Movement led by John Alenciaga.


Former ACT Teachers Partylist Rep. Francisca “Teacher France” Castro of Talaingod 13 Network Makabayan, Caritas Philippines President Most Rev. Gerardo “Gerry” Alminaza, and Dr. Ana Marie “Doc Ana” Rilloraza-Leung received the Gawad sa Indibidwal for their contributions to community protection. (

AMU, DAA)

author: Kodao Productions
title: Makabayan rejects Trump’s visit; Bayan condemns Imeldific welcome for US president
content:
The Makabayan Coalition filed a resolution at the House of Representatives (HOR) opposing US President Donald Trump’s visit to the Philippines to attend the upcoming 2026 ASEAN (Association of South East Asian Nations) Summit.


The anti-imperialist bloc filed House Resolution No. 1593 on Tuesday “expressing the sense of the [HOR] to oppose the welcoming of…Trump” who they said is expected to sign the Pax Silica Initiative, “among other lopsided agreements between the US and the Philippines.”


House Assistant Minority Leader and Kabataan Partylist Rep. Atty. Renee Co said: “A convicted warmongering racist, rapist, pedophile loser should not at all be welcome to step foot on our lands.”


“The American people have themselves rejected Trump. Why should we be forced to accept him here? This administration has no reason to welcome the primary imperialist oppressor of our nation,” Co said.


Co added that because of Trump, hundreds of thousands of people are being killed in various countries and oil prices are skyrocketing worldwide, including the Philippines. Because of Trump, the Filipino people are suffering even more under the mounting burdens he has imposed, she said.


Makabayan condemned Philippine government’s “all-out on spending and preparations” for Trump’s visit.


Imeldific welcome


Meanwhile, Bagong Alyansang Makabayan (Bayan) condemned Ferdinand Marcos Jr. government’s “Imeldific” cleanup drive to hide poverty from foreigners during the ASEAN summit.


Bayan said government’s cosmetic “cleanup drive” to drive out street vendors and urban poor residents from areas where ASEAN Summit dignitaries will pass through is a whitewash meant to hide the Filipino people’s deepening poverty.


“No amount of fresh paint, swept sidewalks, or hidden human beings can erase the hunger, joblessness, and misery that this government has failed to address,” Bayan said.


“We condemn the Marcos Jr. administration’s shameless attempt to prettify Manila for the cameras of foreign leaders while the poor are treated as eyesores to be swept away. The poverty of the people cannot be hidden by a cleanup drive,” the group added.


Bayan secretary general Raymond Palatino called on affected vendors and the urban poor to join the protest actions being organized for Trump’s visit. #

(Raymund B. Villanueva)

author: Mekong Review 2
title: The death of a scammer Tonggo Simangunsong
content:
Poipet, near the Thailand–Cambodia border. Credit: wattana / Shutterstock.com I t was the end of 2024. Almost five months after losing his job at a food and beverage company, thirty-nine-year-old Rasdy Fawzi told his wife, Kiki Tresia Ginting, that he was going to accept a job in Cambodia. Kiki was concerned, and for good reason. The man who’d offered him the job was part of a scam syndicate; the recruitment agency was unregistered and the work Fawzi would be undertaking was illegal. She’d heard stories of young Indonesians trapped in Cambodia, tortured and forced to work as scammers. “I worried and asked my husband about his safety if he worked there, but he said, ‘That’s okay, it’s fine, don’t worry’,” she recalls. Fawzi reassured her many times that his friend had been there, too, and he trusted him. He believed that he was too old for any company in Indonesia to want to hire him for the same role he’d had in mobile sales marketing with his previous employer. While going to Cambodia was risky, the salary offered would be more than enough to support their small family. It was an opportunity he didn’t want to pass up. In the end, there was nothing Kiki could do but let him go and pray for his safety. To read the rest of this article, and to access all Mekong Review content, please subscribe .
