Rollen sind die wiederholbare Aufführung einer bestimmten Reihe von Machtbeziehungen. Der Anreiz dazu, eine Rolle zu spielen ist ein Stückchen Macht; selbst wenn man eine unterwürfige Rolle spielt muss es dafür irgendeine Art von Anreiz geben, selbst wenn es nur ein negativer Anreiz ist, die Vermeidung eines schlimmeren Schicksals. Zu sagen, dass Rollen Aufführungen sind, macht sie nicht unreal, Rollen sind reale Akte, Akte, die wiederholt werden, bis sie sich zu Gewohnheiten verfestigen. Rollen tauchen nicht einfach aus dem Nichts auf, sondern werden von Institutionen, wie der Familie, dem Arbeitsplatz, Unternehmen, Bürokratien, Schulen aufrechterhalten und halten im Gegenzug die Machtstrukturen diese Institutionen aufrecht. Es gibt objektive soziale Strukturen und Institutionen, die Rollen aufrechterhalten, was nicht bedeutet, dass diese in Stein gemeißelt wären. Es gibt subjektive Sehnsüchte diese Rollen zu unterlaufen und zu zerstören, was nicht bedeutet, dass dies einfach wäre oder dass die Subversion Erfolg haben wird. In der Spannung zwischen den Machtstrukturen und dem Verlangen zu rebellieren findet das Spiel der Subversion statt.

Ethnizität, Geschlecht und Klasse existierten schon vor dem Kapitalismus, allerdings in sehr unterschiedlicher Form. Ethnizität wurde vom Aufkommen des Nationalstaats drastisch verändert, Geschlechterrollen haben sich durch die Proletarisierung von Frauen verändert und es ist recht offensichtlich, dass der Aufstieg des Kapitalismus die Klassenstruktur verändert hat. Nichtsdestotrotz wurden Rollen, die auf Geschlecht, Ethnizität und Klasse basierten sowohl vor dem Aufstieg des Kapitalismus, wie auch danach von den Machtstrukturen dazu genutzt, um die Machtbeziehungen aufrechtzuerhalten. Nationalismus ist etwas, das die Menschen oft nicht historisieren, sie begreifen schlicht nicht, wie jung der Nationalstaat ist und dass dieser die bloße Vorstellung von kultureller Identität beeinträchtigt hat. Unser derzeitiges Konzept von Ethnizität (dieses Wort stammt von dem griechischen Wort für Nation) ist vom Nationalstaat geprägt. Einige glauben, dass Nationalismus in seiner derzeitigen Form schon lange vor dem Aufkommen des Nationalstaats existierte und andere glauben, dass das Patriarchat in der Vergangenheit in einer stärkeren Form existierte, die sich heute langsam auflöst. Patriarchat ist eines der offensichtlicheren Beispiele eines Prozesses, der die Rollen der Herrschaft und Unterwerfung schon lange vor dem Kapitalismus aufrecht erhielt. Ich würde argumentieren, dass einige Formen von Patriarchat tatsächlich abgenommen haben, aber das das Patriarchat im allgemeinen nicht verschwindet, sondern vielmehr vom Kapital in eine andere Form umgewandelt wurde, diejenigen Aspekte, die den Kapitalfluss und die Proletarisierung der Frauen einschränkten, wurden verändert. Patriarchat ist keine einzelne, globale monolithische Struktur; es ist kulturell und hat verschiedene Formen. Es beginnt in der Familie, breitet sich auf andere Institutionen aus und wird folglich in der gesamten Gesellschaft reproduziert. Kapitalismus reproduziert neue, mutierte Formen des Patriarchats, er bedient sich der Geschlechterunterschiede, ebenso wie er sich der Klassenunterschiede und ethnischen/rassischen Unterschieden bedient, um die Arbeitskraft im größtmöglichen Maße auszubeuten.

Wie können wir die Kategorien der Identität dazu nutzen, die Gesellschaft in der wir leben zu verstehen, ohne genau die Rollen zu reproduzieren, die wir überwinden wollen? Das ist trickreich, denn wenn wir die Kategorien, die Geschlecht, Rasse und Ethnizität beschreiben, einfach verwerfen, verlieren wir wichtige Werkzeuge, die wir benötigen, um zu verstehen, wie diese Gesellschaft funktioniert, wie diese Kategorien unsere Beziehungen beeinträchtigen und strukturieren. Auf der anderen Seite verfällt man leicht dazu, genau die Rollen aufrechtzuerhalten, die wir überwinden wollen. Das ist ein Problem, das oft in der Identitätspolitik auftaucht, die von einer identitären Kategorie ausgeht. Da solche Politiken auf identitären Kategorien basieren, die im Wesentlichen an Rollen gebunden sind, verfestigt man diese, wenn man nicht bewusst versucht, diese Rollen zu unterlaufen. Kürzlich bezog sich der Artikel „Stick it to the Manarchy“ auf Frauen und People of Color auf die selbe Weise wie auf Kategorien wie die …

 Στο όνομα της «αυτοδιάθεσης των λαών», του «αντιφασισμού» και της «αποτροπής μέσω της ισχύος», ποτάμια αίματος και καμένη σάρκα στη γραμμή του μετώπου ορίζουν τα νέα σύνορα μεταξύ «Ανατολής» και «Δύσης». Το εργαστήριο θανάτου που λέγεται ουκρανία προωθεί την στρατιωτικοποίηση εντός των ευρωπαϊκών κοινωνιών. Φακέλωμα, αξιολόγηση, έλεγχος της κυκλοφορίας, ψηφιακά μητρώα, αυστηροποίηση του Ι5 και περαιτέρω ποινικοποίηση της ολικής άρνησης στράτευσης. Ο (έμφυλος) καταμερισμός εργασίας στην υπηρεσία της βιομηχανίας του πολέμου: Το Υπουργείο Πολέμου θέλει γυναίκες στα χακί, θητεία στα δεκαοκτώ. Οι ευρωπαϊκές πολιτικές άρνησης ασύλου και η αναβάθμιση των συνοριοφυλακών φιλτράρουν τους «απ’ έξω» και μαντρώνουν τους «από μέσα» σε εμπόλεμες ζώνες.


Τα μπάσταρδα της μαμάς-πατρίδας απαντούν με όξυνση του ταξικού ανταγωνισμού. Τα κινήματα λιποταξίας και ανυποταξίας υπονομεύουν την εθνική ενότητα και την ικανότητα των κρατών για διαρκή επιστράτευση των πληθυσμών. Γι’ αυτό το αντιπολεμικό κίνημα στηρίζει την εκτεταμένη ανυπακοή και λιποταξία, τους 300.000 λιποτάκτες και τους 2.000.000 φυγόστρατους στην ουκρανία και τους πάνω από 75.000 λιποτάκτες και 260.000 φυγόστρατους στη ρωσία.


Στη ρωσία οι αυθόρμητες απεργίες επιμένουν και οι αντιμιλιταρίστ(ρι)ες αντιστέκονται, ακόμα κι αν πετάγονται στις φυλακές. Στην ουκρανία τα μπάχαλα και τα πεσίματα στους καραβανάδες από όσους αρνούνται να πάνε να σκοτώσουν και να σκοτωθούν πληθαίνουν.


Αλληλεγγύη στους αντιμιλιταριστές/στριες κρατούμενους/ες στη ρωσία και τους φυγόστρατους στην ουκρανία. Να μην αφήσουμε μόνες όσες αντιστέκονται στον πόλεμο.


Ενάντια στη στρατιωτικοποίηση, τα σύνορα, τους επανεξοπλισμούς και την πολεμική οικονομία.

author: Publicación Abierta
title: El capitalismo cree en el crecimiento infinito. El planeta, no.
content:
Un sistema sin freno en un planeta con fin.


El capitalismo está diseñado para crecer sin límite: fabricar más, consumir más, extraer más. Pero nada, absolutamente nada, es infinito. Se atribuye a Einstein aquello de que solo hay dos cosas infinitas: el universo y la estupidez humana, aunque de la primera no estaba tan seguro. Los recursos energéticos y materiales de nuestro planeta, desde luego, tienen un límite. Y un sistema que exige crecer cada año choca de frente con esa realidad.


El futuro de nuestros hijos, hipotecado.


Al capital le da igual el futuro de nuestros hijos, el de nuestros nietos e incluso nuestro propio presente. Aquí solo importa crecer, acaparar riqueza y ganar cada vez más. Se parece demasiado a un cáncer: una enfermedad que lo devora todo hasta que no queda nada y el cuerpo muere. Ese será el destino del planeta si seguimos por este camino.


Einstein y la necesidad del socialismo.


Einstein se declaró socialista y, en su ensayo «¿Por qué el socialismo?», denunció la anarquía económica del capitalismo y la concentración del poder en pocas manos. Su advertencia sigue vigente: necesitamos un sistema que piense en el futuro y no solo en la acumulación de riqueza por parte de unos pocos.


El mono que acapara plátanos.


Cuando un mono acapara más plátanos de los que necesita, los científicos lo estudian porque ese comportamiento no es normal. En el capitalismo, a quien hace lo mismo lo llamamos multimillonario y lo respetamos. Gente como Elon Musk, que ha llegado a ser el hombre más rico del mundo en más de una ocasión, o los dos o tres multimillonarios que siempre se alternan en esa lista, viven de acaparar.


Riqueza que se convierte en poder.Y no les basta con tener más y más. También quieren más poder: influir en las democracias e injerirse en otros países para imponer su forma de ver el mundo. Y esa forma de ver el mundo, si no la frenamos, será la que acabe con la humanidad.


Hay alternativa, y se llama organización, conciencia de clase y un sistema que ponga la vida por delante del beneficio.


¡Até á vitoria sempre!


André Abeledo Fernández

title: Peter Gelderloos: Breathing Room
content:
Woodcut by Frans Masereel


from Peter Gelderloos’ substack page,

Suviving Leviathan

, 05/11/2026


Breathing Room


from the apocalyptic, fascistic Right to the insufficient, hypocritical, quietly genocidal Left


In the recent elections in Brasil, one of the largest countries in the Global South, leftwing darling Lula beat Flavio Bolsonaro, the fascistic dynast supported by the country’s plantation owner class. In Israel, the extreme Right lost the elections to the far Right (not a typo). And in the US, a “blue wave” has given the Democrats an ample margin of control in both chambers of Congress as well as a strong majority of governorships (for non-US readers, for whatever weird-ass reason related to our especially amnesiac, isolationist culture, in the US blue is the color of the Left and red is the color of the Right). In once Republican-held or toss-up states like Texas, North Carolina, and New Jersey, Democratic candidates won by double digits while conservatives won in what were, until yesterday, solidly Republican states like Florida or Louisiana by only 1 or 2%.


A high level Republican operative connected to Trump admitted to the press that these elections were just “too big to rig,” casually acknowledging how common it is to redraw electoral maps or send the precise vote-counting machines to the friendly districts and low quality, high-failure-rate machines to the unfriendly districts, in order to win an extra percentage point and tip elections.


Brasil


In Brasil, where former far Right president Jair Bolsonaro serves a sentence of house arrest in his mansion for launching a failed coup attempt after he lost the 2022 elections, his son Flavio Bolsonaro carried the first round of the elections in early October but failed to attain a majority. In the second round, held October 25

th

, voters turned to the Left and re-elected the incumbent, Lula, off the Workers’ Party. Wealthy investors punished the country for their vote, with the Brasilian stock market taking a plunge after the election even though Lula is a very business-friendly politician who has overseen a large deal of growth and “development” in the Brasilian economy. In practice that means he promotes oil drilling and mining in the Amazon, he subsidizes the intertwined beef-soy industry causing so much destruction in the south and west of the country, and he also supports manufacture and higher tech industry.


Brasil’s stock market index, with the big crash on the right-hand side occurring on October 25.


If Bolsonaro’s son Flavio had won this past 25

th

 of October, the death squads that work for the ranchers, soy plantation owners, miners, loggers, or directly for the state, would have had free rein. Several of my friends and many of the

Indigenous

,

African diasporic

, and lower class mestizo or white people

I met last year

, people at the forefront of

rural

 and

urban struggles

 against the ongoing violence of colonial capitalism and

for a better world

, would have been at greater risk of getting murdered for their resistance. For sure, a lot of people are breathing a very valid sigh of relief. But they’re not naïve about the meaning of the leftwing victory.

As one friend put it, “

If Bolsonaro wins, they kill us; if Lula wins, they let us die.

Another friend described the following:


“Bolsonarismo already won. I don’t say that just because the Congress and Senate are controlled by fascists, I’m referring to Lula’s campaign replicating the methods of communication that are very close to fascism (including the name “Lula’s Army”). author: Unknown
title: Midterm USA: come sta la seggiola di Trump?
content:
A due anni dall’inizio del secondo mandato di Trump il tempo delle elezioni del Midterm è stato raggiunto in modo da rinnovare il Congresso intero e un terzo del Senato, come indicato dalla Costituzione statunitense. Trump è stato sconfitto in entrambi i casi, con i Dem vincitori in 22 Stati, di cui 5 precedentemente in mano repubblicana, e che ora contano 228 seggi alla Camera e 54 al Senato (dati parziali allo stato della scrittura dell’articolo).


Due anni passati anche troppo velocemente: intensificazione delle operazioni dell’ICE (con i conseguenti sommovimenti come a

Minneapolis

), stati di emergenza di carattere politico emanati in diversi Stati, guerra (persa) all’Iran, ruolo di principale sponsor del genocidio in Palestina, richiesta agli Stati Nato di aumentare la spesa militare senza sborsare un centesimo, guerra commerciale alla Cina (e non solo), aumento vertiginoso del debito, ma anche corruzione e aumento dei profitti per la famiglia di Trump, lo scandalo di Epstein… In poche parole, una fattuale caduta del soft power americano.


STRATEGIE 


Entrambi i partiti hanno messo in atto delle strategie per giocarsi la riconferma o il ribaltamento dei rapporti governativi tra Camere (in particolare il Senato) e la Casa Bianca. Il rischio di un ribaltamento in favore dei Dem era nell’aria e in questo senso la priorità da parte del GOP era quella di concentrarsi sul mantenere il controllo sul Senato, in particolare sul difendere i seggi contesi e cruciali in Stati come Texas, Ohio, Kansas, Maine e Alaska per garantire l’approvazione delle nomine giudiziarie e dei funzionari federali anche in caso di governo diviso. Ma non è andata come sperato, infatti alcuni di questi Stati hanno visto una vittoria Dem inaspettata come nel caso del Kansas che non eleggeva un democratico dal 1932.  D’altro canto la strategia del Partito Democratico ha puntato ad affermarsi come l’unico contrappeso istituzionale e di controllo nei confronti del secondo mandato di Trump. Il tema centrale ruota intorno all’economia domestica: i Democratici imputano direttamente alla Casa Bianca l’aumento del costo della vita, del carburante e dell’inflazione, dipingendo i dazi protezionistici come “tasse sui consumatori” e denunciando i tagli ai servizi sanitari (medicina di base e sussidi ACA). Sul piano internazionale, attaccano i rischi di escalation bellica nei conflitti esteri ed evidenziano presunti conflitti di interesse dell’amministrazione, promettendo di usare la maggioranza al Congresso per avviare commissioni di inchiesta e vigilanza.


L’ultimo elemento da considerare è un andamento particolare degli ultimi anni relativo ai Democratic Socialists of America (DSA) che si sono trasformati da movimento di nicchia a forza capace di influenzare gli equilibri della sinistra americana. Sfruttando il malcontento della cosiddetta Gen Z e Millennials su disuguaglianze e costo della vita, i DSA hanno canalizzato l’attivismo giovanile portando istanze radicali nelle istituzioni. I risultati di ciò si sono visti: nel macro l’elezione a sindaco di Mamdani a New York, seguito da oltre 250 membri dei DSA in diverse altre posizioni (minori) in più di 40 Stati.


Fino ad ora i DSA sono stati forti principalmente nei grandi centri urbani abitati, tuttavia dalla campagna elettorale emerge un altro fenomeno: la retorica alternativa all’establishment, impostata sulle condizioni di vita e di riproduzione delle persone, sta permettendo le prime penetrazioni nelle zone

rurals

 più prossime alle città; forse ancora in minoranza, ma tuttavia rimane un fenomeno interessante. 


La loro strategia per le

Midterms

 si è basata sul condizionamento interno al Partito Democratico: sfidando i candidati moderati alle primarie nei collegi urbani, l’organizzazione impone temi chiave come sanità pubblica, diritto alla casa e tutela dei lavoratori. Questo spinge l’agenda dem verso sinistra, garantendo altresì un’alta affluenza di elettori militanti. Questo soggetto introduce un discorso che significa la dialettica alto-basso non più nei termini di establishment-popolo, bensì con fattori nuovi più prossimi ad una dialettica di classe. Si tratta di una formazione con istanze social democratiche e improntate alla redistribuzione della ricchezza con particolare attenzione al tema delle “minoranze” e di soggettività che intendono essere protagonisti di un nuovo scenario politico statunitense a venire.

author: ROAPE
title: What does Zambia’s Hakainde Hichilema tell us about democracy in Africa today?
content:
Perhaps the strongest hangover from colonialism is the relative lack of consent garnered by the ruling parties: the notion of them gaining “hegemony on a

shoestring

” in a context where rulers’ goals are to keep labour costs as low as possible in order to expand profits of exports. The strategy depended upon indirect rulers defined by “traditions” (flexible and changing) and regions and required brokerage among shifting alliances. Lacking the ideological means of gaining consent via domination of media and civil society institutions, rulers resort to state violence and intimidation.


In 2021 Hichilema inherited a state structure that had, according to

Amnesty International

, over the previous decade undertaken a “systematic crackdown on the right to freedom of expression”, criminalizing peaceful dissent and forcing the closure of independent media outlets. One consequence is that there are no reliable sources of information on the current political crisis. What fails to make international news is any analysis of the prominent regional and ethnolinguistic divisions that animate street-level politics. There is also no analysis of the striking absence of any clear differences in ideological or policy orientations between parties. The currently jailed opposition leader Brian Mundubile heads a coalition formed for the sole purpose of getting UPND out of power while contestation rests largely on respective judgements of character and regional and ethno-linguistic criteria. Questions revolved around

who

 gets to govern – rather than

why

 they should govern. Youtube and Facebook searches for elections information do not yield much more than pastors and self-appointed “prophets”, prophesizing elections results rather than actual political analysis.


The campaign period leading up to the national election on August 13

th

 was marred by street violence among

political supporters

, backed up with intimidation of opposition supporters by police and military. International observers have documented instances of voter intimidation, assaults, abductions, and arrest of hundreds of opposition supporters. Even worse has been the loss of life. A day after the election, security forces killed opposition member,Mutotwe Kafwaya, a former cabinet minister, and Lovemore Chishima, a polling agent. The UN Special Rapporteur, Gina Romero, has called for immediate international scrutiny. The EU parliament passed a near

unanimous resolution

 condemning the killings and the increase in political repression since the election and calling for an independent and impartial investigation. Hichilema has also cancelled the passports of at least six critics of his government, who include a

prominent academic

. When he was in opposition, Hichilema was a victim of the same repression he is inflicting on those who oppose his government.


For Tonga, Ila and Lenje ethnic groups (collectively referred to as ‘Bantu Botatwe’),  a stronghold of the ruling UPND, and where Hakainde and the rest of Southern Province belong, his election victory in 2021 was the culmination of a 75-year struggle of supporting opposition candidates who called for liberal nationalism. This dates back to 1951 when Hakainde’s fellow southerner, Harry Nkumbula launched the Northern Rhodesian African Congress (later renamed as African National Congress). With Nkumbula being eclipsed by Kenneth Kaunda and the United National Independence Party (UNIP) throughout the independence struggle, he remained the primary opposition figure until the banning of the opposition parties in 1973. Since then, Southern and Western regions had maintained deep grievances. With the UPND in power, today these grievances find expression through periodical street battles involving loyal cadres, most of who are lumpenproletarian, against their opposition counterparts. Unemployed and in poverty, these cadres hope for hand-outs in exchange for political support. Ruling party cadres are often the ones who kickstart the political disturbances targeting the opposition, which include disrupting campaign rallies. Thereafter, the police and military, join in, ostensibly to restore order by cancelling the opposition rallies altogether, which ultimately benefit the party in power. This dynamic also led to the suspension of the 2026 election ballot counting in some areas.

biography

 by Giacomo Macola that dispels much of the …

content:
By

Jordan


Jardine

. Original article:

Review: African Anarchism – The History of a Movement

, published on June 3, 2023. Translated into Burmese by Hein Htet Kyaw.


မင်းမဲ့ဝါဒီတစ်ယောက်အနေနဲ့ အမေရိကတင်မကဘေး၊ ကမ္ဘာတစ်ဝှမ်းလုံးမှာရှိတဲ့ မင်းမဲ့ဝါဒ လှုပ်ရှားမှုတွေကို သုတေသနလုပ်ဖို့ စိတ်အားထက်သန်မိတာ သဘာဝပါပဲ။ ဥပမာ – စာရေးသူဟာ လာအိုဇူး (Lao Tzu) ကို တော်တော်လေး သဘောကျမိပြီး၊ Tao Te Ching စာအုပ်ရေးသားသူဟာ ပီတာ ကရိုပေါ့ကင် (Peter Kropotkin) နဲ့ ရူးဒေါ့ဖ် ရော့ကာ (Rudolf Rocker) လိုမျိုး ထင်ရှားတဲ့ မင်းမဲ့ဝါဒီတွေပေါ် အများကြီး လွှမ်းမိုးမှုရှိခဲ့တာပါ။ ဒါကြောင့် တရုတ်နဲ့ အာရှအခြားဒေသတွေက မင်းမဲ့ဝါဒ လှုပ်ရှားမှုအကြောင်း တချို့ကို လေ့လာခဲ့ဖူးပါတယ်။ ဒါပေမဲ့ အာဖရိက ယဉ်ကျေးမှုကိုလည်း သဘောကျတဲ့သူတစ်ယောက်အနေနဲ့ အာဖရိကက မင်းမဲ့ဝါဒ လှုပ်ရှားမှုတွေကိုပါ လေ့လာချင်စိတ် မကြာသေးမီက ပေါ်လာခဲ့ပါတယ်။ ကံကောင်းစွာနဲ့ဘဲ ဒီသမိုင်းကြောင်း (တစ်ခါတစ်ရံ သမိုင်းကင်းမဲ့နေတာတွေကိုပါ) မှတ်တမ်းတင်ထားတဲ့ မရှိမဖြစ် စာအုပ်တစ်အုပ် ရှိနေပါတယ်၊ အဲဒါကတော့ ၁၉၉၇ ခုနှစ်မှာ နိုက်ဂျီးရီးယား မင်းမဲ့ဝါဒီ တက်ကြွလှုပ်ရှားသူ ဆမ်အမ်ဘား (Sam Mbah) နဲ့ ပူးတွဲစာရေးသူ အိုင်အီး အီဂါရီဝေ (I.E. Igariwey) တို့ရေးသားခဲ့တဲ့ African Anarchism: The History of a Movement ဆိုတဲ့ စာအုပ်ပါပဲ။


အကျဉ်းချုပ် –


အခန်း (၁)


အာဖရိက ယဉ်ကျေးမှုနဲ့ ရိုးရာအစဉ်အလာရဲ့ အစိတ်အပိုင်းတော်တော်များများဟာ မင်းမဲ့ဝါဒ စံတန်ဖိုးတွေနဲ့ ကိုက်ညီနေပေမဲ့ အာဖရိကမှာ မင်းမဲ့ဝါဒဆီ ဦးတည်တဲ့ အောင်မြင်တဲ့ လှုပ်ရှားမှုကြီးကြီးမားမား မရှိခဲ့ရတာဟာ ပြည်သူတွေအနေနဲ့ မင်းမဲ့ဝါဒဆိုတဲ့ အတွေးအခေါ်မျိုး ရှိမှန်းတောင် မသိကြလို့ဖြစ်တယ်ဆိုတာကို ရေးသားရင်း စာအုပ်ကို စတင်ထားပါတယ်။ ပင်မရေစီးကြောင်း ယဉ်ကျေးမှုမှာ ပုံဖော်လေ့ရှိသလို မင်းမဲ့ဝါဒဆိုတာ “ရှုပ်ထွေးပရမ်းပတာဖြစ်မှု” နဲ့ “စနစ်မရှိမှု” မျိုး မဟုတ်ပါဘူးဆိုတာကို အမ်ဘားနဲ့ အီဂါရီဝေတို့က ဆက်လက် ရှင်းပြထားပါတယ်။ မင်းမဲ့ဝါဒဆိုတာ အင်အားသုံးတာကို ငြင်းပယ်တာဖြစ်ပြီး၊ လူတစ်ယောက် ဒါမှမဟုတ် အဖွဲ့အစည်းတစ်ခုရဲ့ ဆန္ဒကို အခြားသူတစ်ယောက်ပေါ် အတင်းအကျပ် ဖိအားပေးတာကို တော်လှန်တာဖြစ်ပါတယ်။ စာရေးသူတွေက ပီတာ ကရိုပေါ့ကင်၊ မီးခေးလ် ဘားကူးနင်း (Mihail Bakunin) နဲ့ ပီယဲ ဂျိုးဇက် ပရူးဒွန် (Pierre-Joseph Proudhon) လိုမျိုး ထင်ရှားတဲ့ မင်းမဲ့ဝါဒီ အတွေးအခေါ်ပညာရှင် နမူနာအချို့ကို ပေးထားပြီး၊ မင်းမဲ့ဝါဒအတွင်းက အနာခို-ဆင်ဒီကယ်လစ်ဇင် (anarcho-syndicalism) နဲ့ မူတူဝယ်လစ်ဇင်/အညမည (mutualism) လို အတွေးအခေါ် ဂိုဏ်းဂဏတွေကိုလည်း ဆွေးနွေးထားပါတယ်။


အခန်း (၂)


ဒီအခန်းမှာတော့ ၁၉ ရာစုအလယ်ပိုင်းက စတင်ခဲ့တဲ့ ခေတ်သစ် မင်းမဲ့ဝါဒ လှုပ်ရှားမှုရဲ့ အထွေထွေသမိုင်းကြောင်းကို သင့်တော်သလို အကျဉ်းချုပ် ဖော်ပြပေးထားပါတယ်။


အခန်း (၃)


African Anarchism စာအုပ်ထဲမှာ အရှည်ဆုံးဖြစ်တဲ့ ဒီအခန်းမှာတော့ အမ်ဘားနဲ့ အီဂါရီဝေတို့က အာဖရိကလူမျိုးတွေ ကိုယ်တိုင် သတိမထားမိဘဲ အာဖရိက လူ့အဖွဲ့အစည်းရဲ့ အစိတ်အပိုင်းတွေမှာ မင်းမဲ့ဝါဒ စံတန်ဖိုးတွေနဲ့ ကိုက်ညီတဲ့ အချက်တွေ အမြဲတမ်း ပါဝင်နေခဲ့ကြောင်း တင်ပြထားပါတယ်။ အာဖရိက သမိုင်းတစ်လျှောက်က အသိုင်းအဝိုင်း အတော်များများဟာ အမှီအခိုကင်းပြီး ကိုယ်ပိုင်အုပ်ချုပ်တဲ့ “ဘုံဝါဒ” (communalist) အဖွဲ့အစည်းတွေအဖြစ် လည်ပတ်ခဲ့ကြတာကြောင့် အသိုင်းအဝိုင်းထဲက လူတိုင်းဟာ မိမိတို့ကိစ္စတွေနဲ့ အသိုင်းအဝိုင်းတစ်ခုလုံးရဲ့ ကိစ္စတွေမှာ ပါဝင်ပြောဆိုခွင့် ရှိခဲ့ကြပါတယ်။ အာဖရိက မျိုးနွယ်စု တော်တော်များများမှာ ဘာသာရေးက အရေးပါတဲ့ အခန်းကဏ္ဍက ပါဝင်ခဲ့ပေမဲ့ ဗဟိုချုပ်ကိုင်မှု မရှိခဲ့ပါဘူး။ ဒါကြောင့် ဘာသာရေး သို့မဟုတ် နိုင်ငံရေး အရာရှိတွေရဲ့ အုပ်ချုပ်မှုကို ခံရတာမျိုး မဟုတ်ဘဲ အသိုင်းအဝိုင်းတစ်ခုလုံး တန်းတူညီမျှ စုစည်းနိုင်ခဲ့ကြတာပါ။ အသိုင်းအဝိုင်းထဲက လူကြီးတိုင်း (အထူးသဖြင့် အမျိုးသားတွေ) ဟာ အခြေခံ လူမှုရေး လုပ်ငန်းဆောင်တာတွေကို ဆောင်ရွက်ဖို့နဲ့ သူတို့ရဲ့ အငြင်းပွားမှုတွေကို ကိုယ်တိုင် ဖြေရှင်းဖို့ တာဝန်ရှိခဲ့ကြပါတယ်။


ဒီလို လူ့အဖွဲ့အစည်းတွေဟာ အာဖရိကမှာ ရာစုနှစ်ပေါင်းများစွာ တည်ရှိခဲ့ပေမဲ့ ၁၅ ရာစု အစပိုင်းမှာတော့ လူတန်းစားခွဲခြားမှုနဲ့ လုပ်အားခွဲဝေမှုတွေက တိုက်ကြီးအတွင်းကို ဖြည်းဖြည်းချင်း ဝင်ရောက်လာခဲ့ပါတယ်။ ကျေးရွာစတိုင် ဘုံစနစ်ရဲ့ အစိတ်အပိုင်းအချို့ ကျန်ရှိနေသေးသော်လည်း နောက်ပိုင်းမှာ အာဖရိကဟာ ပဒေသာရာဇ်စနစ်နဲ့ ပရိုတို-ကက်ပီတယ်လစ်ဇင် (proto-capitalism) စနစ်တွေ လွှမ်းမိုးသွားခဲ့ပါတယ်။ စိတ်ဝင်စားစရာ အချက်တစ်ခုအနေနဲ့ အာဖရိကက ရှေးဟောင်း ဘုံဝါဒ ကျေးရွာ လူ့အဖွဲ့အစည်းတွေဟာလည်း ပြီးပြည့်စုံမှုနဲ့ အဝေးကြီး လိုနေသေးကြောင်း အမ်ဘားနဲ့ အီဂါရီဝေတို့က ဖြည့်စွက်ပြောထားပါတယ်။ အနာဂတ် လူ့အဖွဲ့အစည်း စာဖွဲ့ပုံတွေထက် ပိုမိုတန်းတူညီမျှမှု ရှိခဲ့တာ မှန်ပေမဲ့ ရွာတွေနဲ့ မျိုးနွယ်စုတွေမှာ အမျိုးသမီးတွေကို တန်းတူညီမျှ မဆက်ဆံခဲ့ကြသလို ကျေးပုလွေစနစ်ကိုလည်း အတိုင်းအတာတစ်ခုအထိ ကျင့်သုံးခဲ့ကြပါတယ်။


ဒါပေမဲ့လည်း စာရေးသူတွေက လွန်ခဲ့တဲ့ ရာစုနှစ်များစွာက အာဖရိကမှာ တည်ရှိခဲ့တဲ့ “နိုင်ငံမဲ့ လူ့အဖွဲ့အစည်း” အတော်များများကို ဆက်လက် စာရင်းပြုစုပြထားပါတယ်။ အတိတ်က အဆင့်အတန်း ခွဲခြားမှုမရှိဘဲ အလျားလိုက် ဖွဲ့စည်းခဲ့ကြတဲ့ တိုင်းရင်းသား အုပ်စုသုံးခု ဖြစ်တဲ့ နိုက်ဂျီးရီးယားက အစ်ဂဘို (Igbo)၊ နိုက်ဂျာ မြစ်ဝကျွန်းပေါ် ဒေသခံများနဲ့ ဂါနာက တာလန်စီ (Tallensi) လူမျိုးတို့အကြောင်း အသေးစိတ် …

Given that we live in a society that promotes ignorance and superficiality, perhaps it shouldn’t be all that surprising that current day anarchist discussions of historic inter-anarchist debates usually miss the point when it comes to colonialism (and imperialism more generally.)

Anarchists do not somehow become immune to colonial society’s influence simply by making abstract and hollow declarations of opinion. Knowledge and comprehension require actual commitment and curiosity, and these are sadly rare qualities among the European, Euro-American and Euro-Canadian anarchists of today.

This article is an attempt at a brief analysis of what’s been missing in recent anarchist discussions of three historic inter-anarchist debates. The term “debates” is used here in the widest sense of a general disagreement rather than some formally-held event or correspondence. Specifically, I refer to the debates between Luigi Galleani and Ricardo Flores Magón over the Mexican Revolution, between Peter Kropotkin and Errico Malatesta on the First World War, and between Emma Goldman and Reginald Reynolds on Palestine.

In the case of Reynolds, we should note that he considered himself a fellow traveler and sympathizer of anarchism, wrote regularly for the anarchist periodicals edited by Vernon Richards, and married the socialist-turned-anarchist Ethel Mannin, but did not self-identify as an anarchist, so my phrase “inter-anarchist debate” must also be understood in the broadest sense.

The anarchist periodical Tinderbox and the anarchist website The Transmetropolitan Review (TTR) have recently invoked the Galleani-Magón debate, though without even being aware of it in the former case.

The individual who writes articles at the TTR website claimed in May of this year that the historic anarchist Partido Liberal Mexicano (PLM) made a “fateful alliance with Pascual Orozco,” the latter being a bourgeois revolutionary who, with the help of Pancho Villa, took control of Ciudad Juárez in 1911. The author makes no distinction between the on-the-ground forces of the PLM and the Junta (leadership board) of that organization, which, from Los Angeles obviously could not directly control the actions of every individual on the frontlines in Mexico, even if they had wanted to.

TTR goes on to sell the lie that at the time, “the PLM was willing to work with anyone against Madero, and they took positions in Orozco’s rebel government alongside oligarchs and hacienda owners, something which further isolated the PLM from anarchists.”

In reality, Magón and the rest of the Junta, in their periodical, Regeneración, called for violent resistance to Orozco once he took control of Juárez, denouncing him as bourgeois and openly accusing him of being on the wrong side of the revolution, specifically because he was trying to disarm other revolutionaries and was friendly with the rich.

To be clear where TTR wasn’t, the anarchists they claim the PLM isolated …

Это письмо я пишу сегодня, тринадцатого июня тысяча девятьсот восьмого года, дорогие братья Пракседис и Энрике, чтобы сообщить вам дело, которое, на мой взгляд, имеет капитальное значение. Идею, которую я сейчас изложу вам, я уже высказал нашему товарищу Либрадо, и он с ней согласен. Перейдём к сути.

Вы знаете так же хорошо, как и я, что ни одна революция не достигает после победы того, чтобы восторжествовали и стали практическими идеалы, которые её воодушевляли, и это происходит потому, что полагаются на то, что новое правительство сделает то, что должен был сделать народ во время революции.

Так всегда и происходило. Повсюду поднимается знамя с более или менее важными реформами; вокруг него группируются скромные люди; идёт борьба; проливается более или менее обильно кровь, и, если революция побеждает, собирается Конгресс, которому поручено облечь в законы идеалы, заставившие народ взяться за оружие и сражаться. В Конгресс идут люди всевозможных идеалов: одни передовые, другие отсталые, третьи умеренные, и в борьбе всех этих тенденций чаяния революции увядают, искажаются, и после долгих месяцев, а то и долгих лет, начинают приниматься законы, в которых даже не угадываются идеалы, за которые пролил свою кровь несчастный народ. Но допустим, произошло чудо и были приняты законы, в которых во всей своей чистоте сияют идеалы революции, – вещь, которой, конечно, никогда не бывало, потому что очень немногие депутаты имеют те же идеалы, что и народ, взявшийся за оружие; допустим, чудо совершилось и что в особом случае нашей борьбы Конгресс предпишет раздел земель, восьмичасовой рабочий день и зарплату не ниже одного песо. Можем ли мы ожидать, что землевладельцы сложат руки и позволят ускользнуть тому, что делает их могущественными и позволяет им жить в праздности? Разве владельцы всевозможных предприятий, где используются наёмные руки, не закроют свои предприятия или, по крайней мере, не сократят число нанимаемых рабочих, чтобы заставить правительство отменить закон под угрозой всеобщего голода, делая вид, что им материально невозможно платить больше за меньшее количество часов работы?

Когда ресурсы для революции иссякнут, народ окажется в положении более тяжёлом, чем то, из-за которого он был вынужден восстать. Народ, без хлеба, прислушается к речам буржуазии, которая скажет, что его обманули, и возглавит его, чтобы свергнуть новое правительство, – и тем спасутся одни от потери своих земель, а другие – от уступок рабочим.

Богатые восстанут, когда речь пойдёт о том, чтобы осуществить на практике программу либеральной партии, – в случае если чудом, истинным и единственным в истории революций народов, идеалы революции после её победы сохранились бы нетронутыми.

Как анархисты мы хорошо всё это знаем. Мы хорошо знаем, чего следует ожидать от наилучшего правительства, какое только может тяготеть над каким-либо народом, и, как анархисты, мы должны сделать всё, что в наших силах, чтобы революция, которая вот-вот разразится, дала народу все блага, какие возможно завоевать.

Чтобы достичь великих благ для народа, благ действительных, нужно действовать как анархисты, которых легко раздавить даже тем, кто считает нас вождями. Всё сводится к простому вопросу тактики. Если бы с самого начала мы называли себя анархистами, никто, кроме немногих, не стал бы нас слушать. Не называя себя анархистами, мы постепенно зажигаем в умах идеи ненависти против имущего класса и против правительственной касты. Ни одна либеральная партия в мире не имеет антикапиталистических стремлений той партии, что вот-вот совершит революцию в Мексике, и этого мы добились, не говоря о том, что мы анархисты, мы не добились бы этого, даже если бы называли себя не анархистами, какими являемся, а просто …

author: Unknown
title: Франция против власти капитала: от массовых протестов к борьбе за свободное общество
content:
Статья российского анархиста Владислава Маджары, участвующего во французских протестах с мая 2026 года.

Есть особенное ощущение, которое трудно передать человеку, никогда не участвовавшему в массовых протестах. Ты стоишь посреди многотысячной толпы, вокруг звучат лозунги, люди спорят, смеются, обнимаются, незнакомые помогают друг другу. На какое-то время исчезает привычное чувство одиночества перед огромной государственной машиной.

Ты вдруг понимаешь: общество — это не правительство, не парламент, не полиция и не чиновники. Это люди вокруг тебя. И именно они способны изменить существующий порядок.

Ещё несколько минут назад улица была наполнена музыкой и разговорами. Теперь воздух пропитан слезоточивым газом. Люди закрывают лица, ищут воду, помогают тем, кому стало плохо. Где-то впереди слышны крики, а над толпой движутся подразделения CRS.

И перед тобой возникает вопрос, который невозможно отделить от происходящего: почему государство, называющее себя демократическим, отвечает насилием на стремление людей самостоятельно отстаивать свои интересы?

С этими противоречиями я сталкиваюсь во Франции уже несколько месяцев. Я участвую во французских протестах с мая 2026 года, когда нынешняя волна общественного недовольства только начинала формироваться. Вместе с французскими товарищами мы старались распространять информацию о протестах, привлекать людей и поддерживать развитие движения.

Сейчас я состою в бордоском объединении анархистов Envol Bordeaux, вместе с товарищами из которого участвовал в манифестациях. Кроме того, сотрудничаю с Fédération anarchiste — Федерацией анархистов Франции.

Для меня это не просто возможность оказаться среди идейно близких людей. Это непосредственное участие в борьбе, которая заставляет вновь задуматься о природе государства, капитализма, общественной солидарности и самой свободы.

Я приехал во Францию в марте 2026 года, получил здесь статус беженца и постоянный вид на жительство. И чем дольше живу здесь, тем отчётливее понимаю: наличие демократических институтов и социальных гарантий ещё не означает отсутствия эксплуатации, политического господства и государственного насилия.

Франция, безусловно, не Россия. Возможности для независимой политической деятельности здесь несопоставимо шире. Но именно поэтому особенно интересно наблюдать, как даже в обществе с сильными традициями социального сопротивления государство пытается ограничивать самостоятельную инициативу снизу.

И речь далеко не только о Макроне, очередном правительстве или конкретном государственном бюджете. Речь о системе, в которой человеческие потребности вновь и вновь оказываются вторичными по отношению к интересам капитала.

Чтобы понять нынешние протесты, нужно отказаться от представления, будто французы выходят на улицы исключительно потому, что им не нравятся отдельные политические решения. Конфликт гораздо глубже.

Французское государство долгое время воспринималось как одно из наиболее развитых в Европе. Доступная медицина, почти полностью бесплатное государственное образование, трудовые гарантии, социальное страхование, пенсионная система. Однако важно помнить: эти достижения не были подарком просвещённых правителей. За ними стоят десятилетия рабочего движения, массовых забастовок, социальных конфликтов и упорной борьбы.

То, что сегодня представляется естественной обязанностью государства, вчера приходилось буквально отвоёвывать у государства и собственников.

И теперь значительная часть этих завоеваний снова оказывается под давлением. Стоимость жизни растёт. Жильё становится всё менее доступным. Продукты, транспорт, коммунальные услуги поглощают значительную часть доходов. Пенсионный возраст повышается. Молодёжь всё чаще сталкивается с безработицей, а люди с низкими доходами вынуждены постоянно выбирать, какие минимальные базовые потребности удовлетворить сейчас, а какие отложить.

При этом правительство предлагает очередную программу бюджетного сокращения. Предлагаются ограничения роста некоторых социальных выплат, замораживание отдельных параметров жилищной помощи, сдерживание государственных расходов, ограничения финансирования общественных служб. Независимые экономические оценки показывают, что предлагаемые меры способны существенно сократить располагаемые доходы домохозяйств.

Решение бюджетных проблем снова предполагает ограничения для тех, кто и без того несёт на себе основную тяжесть экономической нестабильности. Политическая дискуссия почти всех французских политиков начинается с того, сколько общество …

author: Freedom Editor
title: The Whistles of Minneapolis
content:
How blowing a whistle to stop ICE raids opens up a challenge to the techno-fascists

The tools of state authoritarianism are changing fast. Swarms of drones levelling Gaza and mapping European airports; “flock” street cameras and cyber surveillance webs cataloguing everyone that moves through the major cities or uses a cell phone; state-directed bot armies using deep fake video and memes to alter people’s interior psyches.

A large part of the USA’s economic growth over the last few years has been the ever-larger digital surveillance and weapons industries, with Palantir and Amazon Web Services allowing governments to create vast databases of citizens’ lives, with ominous results. Digital and AI technologies have well-begun acting as accelerants of the domination and exhaustion of workers and the Earth’s ecologies. Commentators and scholars increasingly warn of geopolitical parallels with the twentieth century’s most wicked son, fascism.

Only this time the fash are equipped with expansive digital technologies of war, policing, surveillance, and propaganda.

But anti-fascist movements have begun to adapt, inventing organic technologies as new forms of counter-power. For example, when Trump sent Immigration Control and Enforcement (ICE), newly formed as a MAGA federal militia, to Minnesota to abduct, detain, and deport people of colour, organisers responded by mass 3-D printing a simple but effective technology: whistles. In Minneapolis, a longstanding hub of leftist organising, protesters wear these whistles as they take to the streets to disrupt ICE operations.

For more than a year, these same organisers and protestors have watched ICE agents on their city raids. Using encrypted cell phones to communicate to each other in Signal loops, they try to warn neighbours before the agents arrive. Thousands monitor the Signal loops for word of a raid, waiting for the moment to run out of their homes, blowing their anti-ICE whistles, so that all within earshot can try to flee the raids if they feel at risk. They are joined as community self-defence councils and more underground crews, with memberships in the tens of thousands. With some undocumented families hesitant to even leave their homes for fear of being disappeared by a federal sweep at the bus stops and outside of schools, mutual aid networks organise transportation networks to help their neighbours arrive at their workplaces and schools undetected.

The community councils have innovated on the road blockade to create what they call “filter blockades” across their neighbourhood streets, designed to allow neighbours to pass freely but prevent the passage of federal agents. Community defence crews counter-surveil federal authorities, setting up outside ICE’s headquarters at the Fort Snelling, a federal compound at the confluence of the Mississippi and Minnesota rivers that flow down through the North Woods and Western prairies. One hundred and fifty years ago, the United States Army forcibly marched thousands of Dakota Peoples into a concentration camp at the fort. Hundreds of Dakota prisoners died their first winter there, murdered, frozen to death, and starved. Now, federal forces carry out new forms of domination from the fort, part of what the federal government claims as their “unorganised territory” – lands never incorporated into any state or Native American government and thus under the direct control of the presidency through the Department of the Interior.

In Minneapolis’ Whittier neighbourhood, dissenters briefly raised an autonomous zone blockade at the site of the ICE murder of Alex Pretti, a nurse turned community defender. This is the same patch of concrete that, during the George Floyd uprisings, nurtured an epicenter of intense Black Lives Matter anti-police organising. From May 2020 until more than a year later, liberationists controlled a block of the neighbourhood as a police-free zone. Along the edge of Fort Snelling, an infrastructure that was and remains, as Nick Estes has called it, an infrastructure of U.S. power to genocide Indigenous people and Dakota people, organisers with First Nations United have started a Land Back protest and prayer camp on the land that was taken from their families more than a century ago. For these liberationists, only re-territorialising the land as Indigenous Land can end the cycles of history of white nationalist federal state detention and murder that have been perpetrated on the site.

Viele fallen auf den Versuch herein »Anarchafeminismus« lediglich als eine gelungene Mischung zu begreifen. Dieser »Eintopf« liegt all denen schwer im Magen, die spüren, daß auf solchem Wege Aufbruchsversuche von Frauen in eine eigene, selbstbestimmte Zukunft nur wieder für eine vorgegebene Männerbewegung nutzbar gemacht werden könnten.

Anarchismus – stellt die Frage nach der Herrschaft in der Gesellschaft und muß die feministische Herausforderung annehmen, diese Herrschaft auch als sexistische zu begreifen – als Einschränkung und Festlegung von Frauen auf bestimmte herrschaftsfunktionale weibliche Rollen.

Feministinnen – müssen begreifen, daß diese Herrschaft auch von ihnen selbst, in ihren eigenen Köpfen aufrechterhalten wird und nicht durch vordergründige Kampagnen beseitigt werden kann, wie z.B. die für Quotierung der Teilnahmemöglichkeiten an der patriarchalischen Macht. Feministinnen fallen sich da in den Rücken, wo sie die patriarchalische Bedingtheit ihrer eigenen Entwürfe nicht erkennen.

Ich gehe an mein Thema also von drei Richtungen heran:

vom Anarchafeminismus her, als einer irgendwie gearteten Symbiose, um der Konkretisierung und Neufassung es mir letzten Endes überhaupt geht. Ich werde dabei zunächst einmal den aktuellen Stand wiedergeben.

vom Anarchismus her, – den ich einerseits als Männerbewegung begreife und kritisiere, auf dessen Utopie einer nichthierarchischen Gesellschaft von Gleichen (ob Männern oder Frauen) ich mich aber positiv beziehe und seine Kritik an allen hierarchischen, einschränkenden und ausbeuterischen Strukturen aufgreife – sowohl im Bereich der Arbeit, des Warenverkehrs – wie auch im Bereich der sozialen Reproduktion. Der Anarchismus – so wie ich ihn verstehe – bedeutet letztendlich: die immer neue Frage nach den gesellschaftlichen Mechanismen der Verankerung von Herrschaft. Da ich aber bei allem von meiner Situation als Frau ausgehe, davon, daß ich FRAU BIN, mir diese gesellschaftliche Rolle nicht aussuchen konnte und sie daher offensiv angehen will – ist der dritte Aspekt der Feminismus.

Da ich aber bei allem von meiner Situation als Frau ausgehe, davon, daß ich FRAU BIN, mir diese gesellschaftliche Rolle nicht aussuchen konnte und sie daher offensiv angehen will – ist der dritte Aspekt der Feminismus.

Bei allen Diskussionen um Anarchafeminismus möchte ich daher die konkrete Veränderung der Situation von Frauen im Auge behalten – und nicht etwa nur die Erweiterung der theoretischen Perspektive. Την προηγούμενη περίοδο η συνέλευσή μας, μαζί και με άλλες συλλογικότητες και ανθρώπους της Θεσσαλονίκης συντόνισε και προσπάθησε να δώσει ορμή και περιεχόμενο στον αγώνα αλληλεγγύης στα Προσφυγικά, όπως αυτός εξελίχθηκε στην πόλη μας. Το σκεπτικό μας, όπως το βάζαμε και στον δημόσιο λόγο μας, ήταν πως στα Προσφυγικά βρίσκουν έρεισμα όλοι οι αγώνες, γιατί όλοι οι αγώνες πηγάζουν και παίρνουν μορφή στην συλλογική ζωή των από τα κάτω. Μετά την πρώτη νίκη που κατάφερε ο αγώνας αυτός και με την επιθυμία να ανοίξουμε μία σειρά εκδηλώσεων για την αυτοοργάνωση πάνω στις βασικές συλλογικές μας ανάγκες, αποφασίσαμε να πραγματοποιήσουμε αυτήν την εκδήλωση. Στην κοινοτική συγκρότηση και την κοινωνική αυτοοργάνωση εντοπίζουμε την προοπτική συλλογικής επιβίωσης και αξιοπρεπούς ζωής μέσα στην συνθήκη εντεινόμενης καταστολής και μαζικής εξόντωσης που ζούμε σε πλανητικό επίπεδο.


Από τον κοινωνικό αγώνα των εστιακών ενάντια στην πλήρη υποβάθμιση του μοναδικού χώρου με στοιχεία κοινωνικής κατοικίας στην Θεσσαλονίκη, την κινηματική απάντηση σε μισαναπηρικές δολοφονίες και των εγκλεισμό των αναπήρων, την αντίσταση και την πολύμορφη καταστολή της Μεγάλης Παναγίας, ενός ολόκληρου χωριού, και το κοινωνικό μέτωπο που χτίστηκε με αιχμή τις απεργίες πείνας για την υπεράσπιση της Κοινότητας Κατειλημμένων Προσφυγικών, οι συμμετέχουσες συλλογικότητες εκφράζουν μια μεγάλη βεντάλια της αντίστασης των από τα κάτω, με μακρόχρονη εμπειρία απέναντι σε ευρύτατους μηχανισμούς και μεθόδους καταστολής.


Η Κοινότητα Κατειλημμένων Προσφυγικών έχει ξεκινήσει περιοδεία σε διάφορες γεωγραφίες στην ελλάδα και το εξωτερικό με τίτλο “Οι αγώνες νικούν όταν συναντιούνται”, με σκοπό τη σύνδεση και την ενδυνάμωση των αγώνων σε κάθε τοπικότητα. Θα παρουσιαστούν τα σκεπτικά και η θεμελίωση του αγώνα, τα μέσα που επιλέχθηκαν, ο απολογισμός της έκβασής του, καθώς και η προοπτική και οι προτάσεις για την επόμενη μέρα τόσο για την Κοινότητα όσο και ευρύτερα για το κίνημα και την κοινωνία.


Καλούμε τον κόσμο της πόλης να έρθει στην εκδήλωση και να συμμετέχει με τοποθετήσεις στην κουβέντα που θα ακολουθήσει.

content:
Number 114

Acorninfo


1. Defying the zio-global dictatorship

!


by Paul Cudenec, who reads the article 

here


I am sure you don’t need me to tell you that we are heading into a crucial period of history.


Not only is the shadow of a possible world war looming over us, but our freedom is coming under rapidly accelerating assault.


Here in France, for instance, the system started out by simply ignoring schoolkids protesting against the poor condition of their schools and their lives, then went on to

gas

 and

beat

 them,

smear

 their uprising in the media,

team up

 with far-right street gangs to attack the ever-broadening revolt,

ban protests

 in city centres,

pass a law

 to make demonstrators pay for windows they did not break on the basis of some kind of assumed collective responsibility, place protesters under

house arrest

 as “terrorists”, constantly

lie

 about the size of the turn-outs,

manipulate

 social media algorithms so that people did not know about the demos and threaten to pull that communication plug

altogether

.


I should add that there is also the possibility that at least some of the protesters and looters were

agents provocateurs

 working for the system to undermine public support for the youngsters’ cause, although I have not yet seen any hard proof of this.


In an article for

Le Monde diplomatique

 (November 2026 edition), Benoît Bréville describes how politicians were lining up on TV to demand a fascistic response to the protests, with many blaming the left-wing opposition party

La France insoumise

 – president of the French senate Gérard Larcher even suggested the party should be dissolved.


“Others suggested creating thousands of new places in prisons on the model of Nayib Bukele in El Salvador, of removing benefits from the trouble-makers’ families or of hardening the law against minors”.


Bréville notes that curfews were imposed in several cities, policed by drones and helicopters. “Gatherings are banned and in certain neighbourhoods it is even forbidden to walk around with a rucksack or hat”.


He adds that the French railways, SNCF, cancelled trains to prevent some people from attending demos and those arriving by road and rail were subject to police checks.


 “In Paris, the army was mobilised to supervise the demonstrators, along with the brigade of regional intervention, the RAID (

Recherche, assistance, intervention, dissuasion

) and the national gendarmerie’s intervention group (GIGN)”.


But in the face of all that, numbers on the protests across France did not drop away and the uprising is still going strong as I write!


All across Europe protests are

breaking out

 – including against what looks like an attempted

German-backed

 EU

coup d’état

 in Poland – and it seems that policing is increasingly being carried out by

Eurogendfor

 (European Gendarmerie Force), the European mercenary army deployed, as one

X

 user

put it

, “by the EUSSR to crush local uprisings, hijack demonstrations, and stage coups. They have no ties whatsoever to the local population (they don’t even speak the language) and will ruthlessly crush any form of civilian resistance with an iron fist”.


Meanwhile, hitherto unthinkable restrictions are being placed on people’s international travel on the basis of them not being appreciated by the zio-imperialist mafia (ZIM).


Take, for example, the way that veteran anarchist and co-founder of Food not Bombs

Keith McHenry

 was banned from entering Canada essentially on account of the decades of state violence and harassment  he has faced for feeding homeless people (

see below

).


Much of the repression centres, of course, around critics of Israel and its genocidal activities.


Swedish academic Andreas Malm was

refused entry

 to the UK, where he was due to headline an anti-imperialist and pro-Palestinian conference, on the grounds that his presence in the UK “may not be considered to be conducive to the public good”.


New York journalist Jeremy Loffredo has also

revealed

: “The UK is refusing to let me enter the country to report on and investigate the ongoing crackdown against elderly Palestine supporters because my ‘presence in the UK is not conducive to the public good’”.

author: Matt Simmons
title: ‘Not at a distance’: listening and participating as decolonized journalism practice
content:
Stella Caruso records a video of drumming and singing led by Dúqva̓ísḷa William Housty. Photos by Matt Simmons


This story was produced in collaboration with

The Narwhal

.


I reach out to ​’Cúagilákv Jess Housty around the time of the Haíɫzaqv new year, when the wán̓ái (herring) return and harvesting season begins again after the long, dark winter.


We first connected six years ago, when Xenaksiala Elder Wa’xaid Cecil Paul left this world for the next and I was tasked with writing a

tribute

 to his life and legacy. I called ‘Cúagilákv and they told me stories about their interactions with him. Our paths have intersected a few times since — and before, unknowingly, in the neighbourhood I grew up in where they also spent time during their Youth. ‘Cúagilákv’s

poems

 are part of my love story, too, a thread of words and wild mint, mail and ferries. 


This time, I’ve reached out because I’m thinking about a tugboat called the Nathan E. Stewart, which ran aground near the village of Q’vúqvai in Gale Passage 10 years ago. Eight hours after it hit the rocks, it sank, spilling more than 100,000 litres of diesel and other pollutants. Grief and anger and trauma remain.


Much has been done since to protect Haíɫzaqv lands and waters from another tragedy. ‘Cúagilákv tells me how many others, including their brother, Dúqva̓ísḷa William Housty, are working on the technical and policy side of marine protections and stewardship. But ​’Cúagilákv is following a different path to care for Haíɫzaqv territory. 


“I’m going to deepen my commitment to land-based Youth programming so every kid in the community loves the territory and wants to protect it — and eventually they’ll be the system,” they explain.


Allisa Brown watches the other kids in λáλix̌sístala, the Big House at Kvai. Allisa joined me and Veda on the boat with ‘Cúagilákv

when we headed back to Wágḷísḷa the next morning.


Haíɫzaqv youth and camp staff Aria Reid and Norman Paul warm the drums by the fire before the 20th anniversary

celebration.


And they invite me and my daughter to attend the anniversary of the opening of λáλix̌sístala, a Haíɫzaqv Big House which was raised two decades ago on a beach in the Kvai watershed, around two hours by boat from the Haíɫzaqv capital of Wágḷísḷa (Bella Bella, B.C.) . I accept with gratitude, and following the words of Wa’xaid, I listen. I follow the Wedzin Kwa to where it meets K’sien, and from there follow the river to the ocean. 


In his house overlooking the bay at Wágḷísḷa, Ian Reid, a Haíɫzaqv artist and carver, tells me old stories of the animals and people, and some new ones too. We’re sitting together in his living room while our daughters play in the kitchen. Veda, my kiddo, and Hazel, theirs, met at Kvai and became fast friends. Eli, Hazel’s big brother, is in and out of the house, trying out some newfound freedom on his bike. Ian’s partner, Cayce, offers me a coffee. Cayce and I grew up a few blocks from each other and spent a year at the same elementary school — but we’re only meeting now. Ian’s brother, Garney, is outside the house fixing a water line in the street. I sat with Garney and his wife on the boat down to Kvai. We talked about movies.


I brought a blanket for Ian from the Unist’ot’en feast hall, delivering it for a friend. Ian, whose Haíɫzaqv name is ‘Nusi, meaning “Full Moon,” made a frog crest that was used by Dinï ze (Hereditary Chief) Nedïbïs of the C’ihlts’ehkhyu (Big Frog) Clan of the Wet’suwet’en Nation. Ian puts the blanket on “the way they would put it on me in the feast hall” and poses for a photo.


‘Nusi Ian Reid holds his abalone-adorned talking stick, wearing the blanket from the Unist’ot’en feast hall.


Why am I telling you all this? 


Because, as Opaskwayak Cree scholar Shawn Wilson says in

Research is Ceremony,

 “… it is important for storytellers to impart their own life and experience into the telling. When listeners know where the storyteller is coming from and how the story fits into the storyteller’s life, it makes the absorption of the knowledge that much easier.”


In a word: trust. 


I’ve been leaning into participatory journalism as a means of getting closer to stories that centre and prioritize the Indigenous communities where I’ve been welcomed and trusted, letting respect and reciprocity be my guides. In this practice, I’m not only finding deeper truths and more connection — I’m discovering richer, more nuanced stories.


Kim TallBear, in

Standing With and …

author: Nahuel Lag
title: El suelo como espejo de la relación entre humanidad y naturaleza
content:
Por Patricia Fernández y Lourdes Gil Cardeza*


Somos muchas las personas, organizaciones e instituciones que reconocemos estar atravesando una crisis civilizatoria muy profunda. Hay tantísima evidencia que muestra cómo estamos sobrepasando los límites físicos que permiten nuestra existencia en el planeta Tierra. Hay un área específica de la economía que lo estudia: la economía ecológica. El estilo de vida que impone la sociedad occidental implica calentamiento global, una creciente y continua contaminación de suelos y aguas, y el constante despojo de tierras a pueblos indígenas y campesinos debido al avance del modelo económico, que pone en jaque a los procesos biológicos de la vida que han ido coevolucionando desde hace, al menos, 460 millones de años, cuando empezó a desarrollarse la vida fuera del agua.


El suelo es un espejo de los vínculos que lo conforman. Es la resultante de la convivencia evolutiva entre la roca madre, el clima y los seres vivos. En otras palabras, el suelo es parte de los procesos del planeta Tierra, el suelo es vida, el suelo está vivo. Tanto su color oscuro característico como ese olorcito que percibimos corresponden a la materia orgánica (componente fértil y vital del suelo), compuesta por los organismos vivos que lo habitan y por lo muerto en vía de descomposición que nutren de manera espiralada a los organismos y las plantas de las que nos alimentamos. El estilo de vida occidental pone en riesgo esa vitalidad.


El tipo de agricultura que domina al planeta no es un simple conjunto de técnicas para producir alimentos (y muchas veces commodities): es la materialización de una lógica de poder que entrelaza colonialismo, patriarcado y capitalismo. Así lo evidencian las voces críticas de pensadoras que ayer y hoy señalan cómo el avance sobre la tierra y la naturaleza es un reflejo de la misma lógica de dominación ejercida sobre los cuerpos de las mujeres y los territorios. Llegar a comprender la crisis o la degradación del suelo hoy, exige, en principio, desentrañar esta trama histórica y epistemológica que ha convertido a la naturaleza en un objeto de explotación ilimitada. 


Creemos que hacer el intento por desarmar esta trama (o trampa), es condición necesaria en el proceso de deconstrucción que elegimos, como dijo

Audre Lorde

, para transformar la ira en un proceso creativo. Con este texto buscamos traer a la actualidad, y a latinoamérica en particular, a Eve Balfour, una mujer de la aristocracia inglesa quien, con mucha claridad y simpleza, se atrevió a abordar temas invisibilizados en Europa y sus continentes colonizados, al publicar su libro

El Suelo Vivo

 (

The Living Soil

) en 1943. 


Foto: Matías sarlo - Minga


Esta tesis describe de manera sencilla los vínculos entre la salud humana y el cultivo de nuestros alimentos y pone la lupa en el suelo jerarquizando su rol como promotor de la salud toda. En palabras de Eve:

“La evidencia acumulada sobre la interrelación entre la vitalidad del suelo y la salud de las plantas, los animales y el ser humano es de tal importancia y de tan profundas implicancias que ya es hora de que el público en general tenga la oportunidad de estudiar y formarse su propio juicio al respecto”

.


La matriz del despojo


La crítica al modelo agrícola industrial debe partir de la constatación de que su origen no es meramente técnico, sino profundamente político. La antropóloga maya-kaqchikel

Aura Cumes

 sostiene que el patriarcado colonial llega desde Europa y se reconfigura en América para ejercer el sometimiento sobre las mujeres, las poblaciones indígenas y afrodescendientes convirtiéndolas en sujetos despojables y así validar la extracción del territorio y del cuerpo-territorio. Este proceso de dominación tuvo un pilar fundamental: la disociación del hombre respecto de la naturaleza, a la cual se feminizó para legitimar su conquista. "A partir de ello —explica Cumes— se atribuye la potestad de descubrirla, penetrarla, torturarla y convertirla en mercancía." 


Esta visión no es casual, sino que se fundamenta tanto en los textos bíblicos que otorgan al hombre el "señorío" sobre la creación como en el discurso científico que adoptó estos postulados como base de su conocimiento. En esta trama (o trampa), el capitalismo manifiesta la continuidad de las mismas lógicas que motorizaron al colonialismo al implementar la sustitución de ecosistemas enteros por una "biota mixta" europea (trigo, ganado vacuno, cerdos, malezas, microorganismos, personas) …

author: Unknown
title: Indigenous Action - Voting is Not Harm Reduction
content:
Author

: Indigenous Action

Title

: Voting is Not Harm Reduction

Date

: February 5, 2020

Source

: http://www.indigenousaction.org/voting-is-not-harm-reduction-an-indigenous-perspective/


 When proclamations are made that “voting is harm reduction,” it’s never clear how less harm is actually calculated. Do we compare how many millions of undocumented Indigenous Peoples have been deported? Do we add up what political party conducted more drone strikes? Or who had the highest military budget? Do we factor in pipelines, mines, dams, sacred sites desecration? Do we balance incarceration rates? Do we compare sexual violence statistics? Is it in the massive budgets of politicians who spend hundreds of millions of dollars competing for votes?


 Though there are some political distinctions between the two prominent parties in the so-called U.S., they all pledge their allegiance to the same flag. Red or blue, they’re both still stripes on a rag waving over stolen lands that comprise a country built by stolen lives.


 We don’t dismiss the reality that, on the scale of U.S. settler colonial violence, even the slightest degree of harm can mean life or death for those most vulnerable. What we assert here is that the entire notion of “voting as harm reduction” obscures and perpetuates settler-colonial violence, there is nothing “less harmful” about it, and there are more effective ways to intervene in its violences.


 At some point the left in the so-called U.S. realized that convincing people to rally behind a “lesser evil” was a losing strategy. The term “harm reduction” was appropriated to reframe efforts to justify their participation and coerce others to engage in the theater of what is called “democracy” in the U.S.


 Harm reduction was established in the 1980s as a public health strategy for people dealing with substance use issues who struggle with abstinence. According to the Harm Reduction Coalition (HRC) the principles of harm reduction establish that the identified behavior is “part of life” so they “choose not to ignore or condemn but to minimize harmful effects” and work towards breaking social stigmas towards “safer use.” The HRC also states that, “there is no universal definition of or formula for implementing harm reduction.” Overall, harm reduction focuses on reducing adverse impacts associated with harmful behaviors.


 The proposition of “harm reduction” in the context of voting means something entirely different from those organizing to address substance use issues. The assertion is that “since this political system isn’t going away, we’ll support politicians and laws that may do less harm.”


 The idea of a ballot being capable of reducing the harm in a system rooted in colonial domination and exploitation, white supremacy, hetero-patriarchy, and capitalism is an extraordinary exaggeration. There is no person whose life is not impacted every day by these systems of oppression, but instead of coded reformism and coercive “get out the vote” campaigns towards a “safer” form of settler colonialism, we’re asking “what is the real and tragic harm and danger associated with perpetuating colonial power and what can be done to end it?”


 Voting as practiced under U.S. “democracy” is the process with which people (excluding youth under the age of 18, convicted felons, those the state deems “mentally incompetent,” and undocumented folx including permanent legal residents), are coerced to choose narrowly prescribed rules and rulers. The anarchist collective Crimethinc observes, “Voting consolidates the power of a whole society in the hands of a few politicians.” When this process is conducted under colonial authority, there is no option but political death for Indigenous Peoples. In other words, voting can never be a survival strategy under colonial rule. It’s a strategy of defeat and victimhood that protracts the suffering and historical harm induced by ongoing settler colonialism. And while the harm reduction sentiment may be sincere, even hard won marginal reforms gained through popular support can be just as easily reversed by the stroke of a politician’s pen. If voting is the democratic participation in our own oppression, voting as harm reduction is a politics that keeps us at the mercy of our oppressors.


 While so many on the left–including some Indigenous radicals–are concerned with consolidation of power into fascists hands, they fail to recognize how colonial power is already consolidated. There …

author: Arnold Padilla
title: What’s at stake in Trump’s Manila visit?
content:
U.S. President Donald Trump’s upcoming visit to Manila for the ASEAN Summit happens in the wake of intensifying struggle between the U.S. and China for economic, technological, political, and military dominance in Asia. Washington aims to consolidate its strategic position in Southeast Asia, with the Philippines under Ferdinand Marcos Jr. playing an increasingly important role in advancing U.S. imperialist interests.


Trump arrives politically battered. The sweeping Republican defeat in the November 3 midterm elections, which handed both houses of Congress to the Democrats, represents a powerful repudiation of his administration’s policies. Trump’s unpopular U.S. war against Iran and his aggressive tariff policies and their disastrous economic consequences, such as rising living costs, contributed to widespread dissatisfaction among American voters.


The defeat further exposes the political crisis confronting U.S. imperialism. It reflects growing domestic opposition to policies that impose enormous economic and social costs on the American people while sustaining Washington’s aggressive military interventions and global ambitions.


But Trump’s weakened domestic position does not mean that the White House will abandon its imperialist agenda abroad. On the contrary, the administration may seek to demonstrate U.S. power through new military, economic, and diplomatic agreements. Trump could use his visit to Manila to project strength and secure strategic commitments to counter the political setback at home.


The central objective of Washington’s ASEAN agenda is to preserve U.S. supremacy in the face of China’s expanding economic and military power. Southeast Asia occupies a crucial place in this rivalry. It sits astride strategic maritime routes and contains vital manufacturing centers, mineral resources, emerging digital markets, and production networks essential to the world economy.


For U.S. imperialism, maintaining influence over ASEAN means safeguarding its military reach while securing access to markets, technology infrastructure, critical minerals, and industrial supply chains. The U.S. seeks to organize these strategic assets around its own economic and national-security priorities, particularly by reducing dependence on Chinese-controlled production networks.


At the same time, China is expanding its own economic and strategic influence through trade, investment, infrastructure, and military power. This competition between rival great powers seeks to expand their influence over the region’s resources, markets, territory, and political decisions.


Militarizing Southeast Asia 


Washington’s military agenda was made explicit during the ASEAN defense ministers’ meetings in Cebu in October, when Pete Hegseth, Trump’s so-called Secretary of War, proposed a new framework for U.S.–ASEAN defense cooperation.


Under the language of maritime security and interoperability, Washington seeks to deepen military coordination, intelligence sharing, joint exercises, and naval cooperation with Southeast Asian governments. The proposal complements the expanding network of U.S. military alliances and access arrangements across the Indo-Pacific. It aims to strengthen its First Island Chain strategy to encircle and contain China. On the sidelines of the Cebu meeting, U.S. and Japanese defense officials discussed implementing a more effective denial-defense posture along this chain.


With its geographical location, the Philippines has become a crucial platform for this strategy. Under Marcos Jr., U.S. military access under the Enhanced Defense Cooperation Agreement (EDCA) has expanded from five to nine designated Philippine facilities. Washington and Manila are also increasing joint military exercises and deployments of advanced missile and unmanned systems. These arrangements strengthen the capacity of U.S. forces to operate in the South China Sea and potentially respond to a Taiwan Strait conflict. 


So far, only two ASEAN countries have formal defense treaties with the U.S., namely the Philippines and Thailand. But all the other members, except for Myanmar, have various forms of extensive defense or military cooperation arrangements with the U.S. However, unlike its Mutual Defense Treaty (MDT) and related pacts with the Philippines, not all agreements with other ASEAN countries grant U.S. troops access to military installations, allow combat deployments, or entail an obligation to support U.S. military operations.  …

author: Willy Mutunga
title: Book Review: From Mau Mau to Ruto-Must-Go: A Scrapbook of Essays on Kenya’s Struggle Against Imperialism
content:
I recently read a review of the book, 

From MAU MAU to RUTO-MUST-GO: A Scrapbook of Essays on Kenya’s Struggle Against Imperialism,

 

by Teddy Odira, a young lawyer in Nairobi who published in The Platform for Law, Justice, and Society. I shared the review with one of the co-editors of the book, Shiraz Durrani, and asked him what he thought. This is was his response via a WhatsApp text:


It’s a brilliant review, I think. He understands the undercurrents that the book explores and identifies key issues, like land, that have driven resistance. He also sees resistance as an on-going, incomplete struggle. Very well done!


What is well said by another is mine. In this review, I want to glorify the work of the artist movements in Kenya for breathing life into the Constitution of Kenya, 2010, particularly

Article 33

 that decrees freedom of expression. This freedom of expression has limitations. It is the freedom of artistic creativity that is glorified in two of the articles in the book. They glorify cartoonists and Social Justice Theatre (SJCCTT). Freedom of artistic creativity in Kenya is valued by others, including the two mentioned. The others include: poets, spoken word artists, graffiti artists, songwriters, singers, comedians, filmmakers, and others. Freedom of artistic creativity has been a radical site of struggle in the implementation of the Constitution of Kenya, 2010. Freedom of expression under the Constitution has been the subject of a recently published scholarly work.


This Constitution has been described as progressive and transformative because of the process of its making, its texts on objectives, purpose, and vision to reform, by non-reformist reforms, which maintain the status quo in Kenya. While the ruling elite find the Constitution inconvenient and abstract, these sites of struggle have used provisions of the Constitution to craft political demands, breathe life into these sites through uprising, robust public participation, mass action, and public interest litigation. The quest for an authentic patriotic alternative political leadership is a continuous struggle anchored in these constitutional sites of struggle that the ruling elite has refused to implement. It is argued that such an alternative political leadership that is authentic and patriotic will implement the Constitution by consolidating gains made, and rescuing the weaknesses that are encountered during the process of its implementation.


Glorification


A: In Praise of Cartoonists: Ruo Kimani-Ruo


Ruo Kimani-Ruo praises the cartoonists in words that should not be paraphrased:


…,

there has emerged an unprecedented form of political cartoons artwork which has been launched in Kenya with sizzling, scorching, blistering cartoon editorials and other graphics and caricatures of public figures that express the artists’ opinions, with celebrated cartoon artists Celeste and Maddo


being joined by Yoko and others-all freely and fearlessly expressing their opinions on public issues and the individuals in government and thereby shedding light on the public mood on issues.…


With these political cartoons, the artists have had a field day and typically combined artistic skills, hyperbole and satire to question authority. The cartoons have drawn attention to, among other things, corruption, electoral inequalities, political abductions and other social ills including violence- and the Consolidated Fund at Central Bank of Kenya (CBK) where billions of shillings are being ‘siphoned and stashed in offshore accounts in the West; and suspicions of embezzlement.


The genius of the cartoonists that I have encountered over decades lies in the interpretation of their work for the powers that be, and the citizens themselves. They are always armed with many interpretations of their cartoons. They use those interpretations to either stay safe when confronted by elites and their machinery of violence, or to mobilize the citizens around the key messages. They invariably keep their mouths shut and let their work engage both the enemy and the friend. Their work requires great critical thinking, taking ideological and political positions in breathing life into the provisions of the Constitution to energize non-reformist reforms.


B: In Praise of Theatre Artists:


Zachary J Patterson


Zachary J Pattern glorifies the Social Justice Centres Travelling Theatre (SJCTT) in the following paragraphs:


Interactive scenes show an all-too familiar tale of the …

author: Shannia Cabuello
title: Molbog community exposes agenda behind land-use projects
content:
They turned our ancestor’s burial sites into dumping grounds.

“They want to take everything so we insisted on coming here to express ourselves. We will embrace our land even if they harass us. We will not give it even if we get hurt.”

Molbog community member Anjilon Flores from Balabac Palawan stressed this point as Molbog indigenous peoples travelled to Metro Manila ahead of US President Donald Trump’s visit.

They aim to amplify their resistance against the Department of Environmental and Natural Resources’ Enhanced National Greening Program (E-NGP) and the Enhanced Defense Cooperation Agreement (EDCA).

Along with multi-sectoral groups and environmental advocates, they exposed the E-NGP and EDCA as tools of imperialist war and resource plunder, threatening the life, livelihood, culture, and ancestral lands of the Molbog people.

Long before Spanish colonial rule, the Molbog community have been the traditional stewards of Balabac island, depending on coconut farming, shifting cultivation, fishing, and harvesting seaweeds for livelihood.

“Palawan is a key biodiversity area and known to be the last ecological frontier of the Philippines,” Bianca Intia of Kalikasan Timog Katagalugan (TK) said at a press conference on October 26.

It shelters several endemic animal and plant species, including Philippine Mouse-deer which are exclusively found in Balabac and nearby islands.

Flores described their fields as prosperous with cassava, banana, corn, peanuts, and rice, making it their community’s main source of income for decades.

For them, lands are sacred that require ancestral permission before undertaking any activities like when entering the land, performing rituals, planting, harvesting, and cutting trees.

Born in Balabac, Flores cannot accept the prohibitions imposed by the E-NGP in using their resources. “They would restrict us from cutting trees which we use for firewood. This is also the livelihood for most of us. What will happen if they forbid us? Our livelihood will also be gone.”

Bangsa Molbog leader Emmanuel San Esteban lamented the encroachment of Balabac Air Base on their homes, sacred prayer grounds, and burial sites in Barangay Catagupan without any consultation with their tribal officials.

“They turned our ancestor’s burial sites into dumping grounds. The mountains where we do our rituals were flattened,” San Esteban said.

The local authorities said that the remains of their ancestors would be transferred to a different location. However, this is against the principles and culture of the Molbog tribe.

The indigenous residents dread the impact of both projects, as it begins to disrupt their peace, routines, and tradition.

They stressed that access to their land has been restricted, limiting the products they could gather from the forest.

According to DENR, the E-NGP was signed to rehabilitate the estimated 1.2 million hectares of the remaining unproductive, denuded, and degraded forestlands by 2022. It also aimed to maintain and protect existing forests.

This was already implemented by the DENR in several areas in Balabac where trees were planted in Barangay Catagupan, Agutayan, and Indalawan.

The communities worried about fines for damaging plants under E-NGP while clearing farmland. Cutting a tree must also be replaced with a hundred more trees and a Php 6,000 ($94) fine.

Kalikasan TK underscored that E-NGP did not aim to benefit communities but only to carbon offset the Ipilan Nickel Corporation’s deforestation and mining operations in Brooke’s Point, Palawan.

The Molbog people also expressed concerns that monocropping and fast-growing plant species under the E-NGP could affect forest biodiversity and native vegetation.

“The E-NGP is within our ancestral domain, for which we had applied for a Certificate on Ancestral Domain Title (CADT),” said San Esteban, questioning how the project progressed faster than their CADT application.

They first filed their CADT application in 2004 but the National Commission on Indigenous Peoples (NCIP) only certified the application in 2019. To expedite the process, the NCIP required them to pay at least Php 1.6 million ($25,092.33). Their CADT remains pending.

San Esteban said that Balabac Air Base in Barangay Catagupan also pushed through because of the NCIP’s manipulation of the Free, Prior, and Informed Consent (FPIC) process.
