author: anred
title: Trump bombardea Irán en la madrugada de su derrota electoral
content:
Tal como lo descontaban los sondeos electorales y hasta los “mercados”, Trump sufrió una derrota de carácter aplastante en los comicios de este martes. A

 nadie escapa que en el telón de fondo del rechazo electoral a Trump se encuentra la guerra contra Irán y sus consecuencias económicas. Pero al referirse al resultado electoral, los principales voceros del partido Demócrata -y también los de la democracia imperialista europea- han ocultado la cuestión de la guerra por abajo el felpudo. Un largo posteo oficial de Obama ni la menciona, después de varias invocaciones a la “unión nacional”. La guerra imperialista en desarrollo, que comenzó bajo el mandato de Biden, está en el horizonte estratégico de republicanos y demócratas.

Para Trump, la continuidad de la guerra con Irán es también un recurso para prevalecer sobre la Unión Europea, en medio del agravamiento de la guerra entre Ucrania y Rusia y los acuerdos por «separado» entre Putin y el propio Trump.

Un escenario de escalada militar, por un lado, y mayor autoritarismo, por el otro, agravará la crisis política y los estallidos populares al interior de los Estados Unidos, en medio de una crisis financiera en ciernes. El eje de la crisis mundial pasa por el corazón del imperialismo.

Por Marcelo Ramal (Política Obrera).


Tal como lo descontaban los sondeos electorales y hasta los “mercados”, Trump sufrió una derrota de carácter aplastante en los comicios de este martes. La victoria demócrata, que se consideraba segura en Representantes (diputados), también tuvo lugar en el Senado, donde la composición final sería de 52 o 53 escaños demócratas contra 48 o 47 de los republicanos. Los reveses de Trump abarcaron a estados con un dominio histórico de su partido, como Carolina del Norte y del Sur -en este último caso, ganaron los demócratas después de 25 años de mandatos republicanos; también en el bastión petrolero de Texas, donde se impuso un senador demócrata después de 38 años, y lo mismo en Kansas, después de casi un siglo de hegemonía republicana. En Florida, bastión del exilio derechista cubano y venezolano y corazón del movimiento MAGA, la candidata republicana María Salazar había tomado distancias de Trump para salvar el voto migrante. A pesar de ello, sólo se imponía por una diferencia del 0,1%, en un escrutinio voto a voto. En Michigan, la victoria del candidato de origen musulmán Abdul El Sayed lograba prevalecer después de una furiosa campaña en su contra de Trump y del sionismo.


Significado


Ningún observador reconoce un liderazgo o fisonomía política definida en la victoria demócrata: el hilo conductor del resultado electoral es el golpe asestado a Trump -los electores, que concurrieron masivamente a sufragar en un país donde el voto es voluntario- desplegaron una movilización política en rechazo a la carestía desatada por la guerra, la represión política y el “estado de excepción” impuesto por Trump contra la población migrante. Las redadas del ICE llegaron a convertirse en un factor de desorganización económica, al imponer una zozobra que afecta a una parte de la fuerza laboral del capitalismo americano. La tentativa de “reindustrialización” del país a costa de sanciones comerciales extendidas tuvo pobres resultados y acrecentó la inflación. La carestía fue también estimulada por la instalación de los centros de datos para la oligarquía tecnológica de la IA. En sus campañas electorales, los gobernadores electos de Texas, Ohio, Georgia y Pensilvania hicieron de la oposición a la instalación de estas infraestructuras un eje de campaña. 29 jurisdicciones votaron este martes medidas locales de restricción a estas instalaciones, con apoyo abrumador de la población. La política MAGA, en definitiva, sólo hizo grande a los negocios de la camarilla trumpista y la oligarquía tecnológica. Para la población explotada, sólo trajo inflación, salarios a la baja y mayor zozobra en el empleo.


Entre Mr. Veto y los acuerdos


“Con mi nombre en la boleta, ganábamos en todos lados”. Esto posteó Trump después de la derrota, desconociendo u ocultando que él mismo se había puesto al frente de las elecciones que acababa de perder. Pero la alusión a su figura apunta a lo que viene: la pretensión de erigir un régimen de poder personal, a costa de decretazos y de vetos. Las mayorías cosechadas por los demócratas no tienen la contundencia para desconocer esos vetos -tampoco para hacer avanzar hasta el final un juicio político contra Trump. author: LCM-Redaktion
title: Eine Welt zu Gewinnen! – Interview zur Konferenz und dem Anspruch des Internationalismus im 21. Jahrhundert
content:
„

In Zeiten der Zuspitzung der globalen Systemkrise und im Angesicht ihrer direkten Auswirkungen auf uns hierzulande wollen wir eine neue Debatte über internationalistische Praxis und Ausrichtung hier in Deutschland anstoßen. Wir stellen uns die Frage, wie sich unser Anspruch in einer an den konkreten Verhältnissen orientierten Praxis verwirklichen kann.“ – S

o wirbt die Tagung „Eine Welt zu Gewinnen“, die anlässlich des 109. Jahrestages der Oktoberrevolution am kommenden Wochenende in Berlin stattfinden wird.


Wir sprechen mit Ayşe vom Bund der Kommunist:innen

1

 in Berlin und Lena von YUNA – Demokratische Jugend

2

, welche die Konferenz zusammen mit der Akademie der demokratischen Moderne ausrichten.


In Berlin findet ja kommendes Wochenende die Konferenz „Eine Welt zu Gewinnen“ statt. Könnt ihr uns einen Einblick geben, was denn da so geplant ist?


Lena:

 Die Konferenz wird einen ganzen Tag lang gehen und ist in drei Blöcke aufgeteilt: Zu Beginn haben wir Brigitte Studer eingeladen, die ihre Recherchen zur KomIntern vorstellen wird. Dabei werden wir natürlich Publikumsfragen stellen können, um zusammen herauszufinden, welche Lehren wir aus der Vergangenheit ziehen können. Im zweiten Panel teilt dann Torkil Lauesen seine Analyse des globalen Kapitalismus und seine Perspektiven mit uns. Was vor allem im Hinblick auf eine spezifische Praxis in den Zentren des Imperialismus sehr spannend wird.


Ay

ş

e

:

 Das Podium im Anschluss ist ein Ausdruck von dem, was wir mit der gesamten Konferenz versuchen: Wir schauen uns nicht nur die Geschichte der imperialistischen Epoche des Kapitalismus an, sondern auch, was die Bedeutung des Internationalismus in den imperialistischen Krisen war. Wie war unsere internationalistische Praxis in Deutschland in den letzten Jahrzehnten und wie muss eine zukünftige internationalistische Arbeit aussehen? Wir sehen die imperialistische Weltlage einerseits und haben viele internationalistische Erfahrungen. Wenn wir uns zum Beispiel Kurdistan anschauen, vollzieht sich ja ein Umbruch. Deshalb muss die konkrete Analyse, zu der wir gemeinsam an dem Tag kommen, auch dazu führen, dass die Art und Weise, wie unsere Praxis aussieht, sich sozusagen daran anpasst. Und das werden wir eben auf dem Podium gemeinsam, auch aus unseren verschiedenen Erfahrungen und Perspektiven, zusammenbringen.


Worin seht ihr die Herausforderung eines proletarischen bzw. sozialistischen Internationalismus in der heutigen Zeit?


Lena:

 Was wir vielleicht erstmal grundsätzlich zum Verständnis von Internationalismus sagen müssen: Aufgrund des global organisierten Kapitalismus brauchen wir auch eine internationale Strategie. Probleme dabei gibt es viele. Die subjektive Situation, also die Situation von uns organisierten Kräften, müssen wir dabei hervorheben: Auch wenn wir sehen, dass es einen Aufschwung bei den sozialistischen Kräften gibt, sind wir nicht so breit aufgestellt und stabil verankert. Es braucht eine gut organisierte gesellschaftliche Bewegung, um mit einer Relevanz tatsächlich in internationale Beziehungen zu gehen. Ein weiteres Problem ist die Trennung, die wir sowohl als Jugendliche, Frauen, als auch ArbeiterInnen anhand von nationalen Grenzen als auch anderen Machtgrenzen erfahren.


Ay

ş

e:

 Ja, viele Sachen, die Lena genannt hat, würde ich genauso teilen. Ich würde noch hinzufügen, dass, wenn man sich spezifisch die Arbeiterklasse anschaut, das Problem eben die extreme Heterogenität dieser ist. Nicht nur innerhalb der globalen Waren- und Produktionskette, sondern selbst hier in den Betrieben in Deutschland sehen wir: Okay, es gibt eigentlich verschiedene Stellungen in jedem Betrieb, es gibt Festangestellte, Subunternehmer, ganz prekär arbeitende Leute, die ja nicht mal in einem Betrieb ein gemeinsames Interesse formulieren können. Wenn man sich das über nationale Grenzen hinweg anschaut, ist es noch schlimmer.


In Deutschland haben wir das Problem, dass wir es tatsächlich großflächig mit einer Arbeiteraristokratie zu tun hatten. Gerade da, wo eigentlich ganz viel Macht bei der Arbeit liegt: Die Leute, die bei BMW und Mercedes und Volkswagen an den teuren Anlagen sitzen, wo ganz viel Mehrwert in wenigen Sekunden produziert wird, das sind natürlich auch die Leute, die am meisten befriedet sind, weil es einen super Kündigungsschutz gibt, die ein ganz gutes Gehalt bekommen und so weiter und so fort.


Das hat historisch in Deutschland dazu geführt, dass es die Notwendigkeit nach einem Kampf …

title: 25 organizations in Europe seek to strengthen joint struggle and solidarity
content:
25 political and civil society organizations from Turkey and Kurdistan have agreed to establish a joint alliance for struggle and solidarity in Europe. The initiative aims to bring together different political currents and strengthen resistance against the rise of right-wing and fascist forces, imperialist war policies, and state repression. At the same time, the participating organizations intend to support the peace and democratic society process in Turkey and advocate for a democratic solution to the Kurdish question.


The agreement stems from a meeting held on October 17 at the Cologne headquarters of the Federation of Alevi Communities in Europe (AABK). Representatives from various political traditions and social movements gathered at the invitation of eight organizations. In a joint final declaration issued today, the participants reaffirm their determination to preserve their organizational independence while establishing a lasting foundation for joint political action.


Against militarism, fascism and imperialist war policies


In their declaration, the organizations describe a world marked by growing international tensions. They warn that wars and conflicts driven by imperialist centers of power are increasing the risk of a broader military confrontation, potentially escalating into a new global war over the redistribution of power and resources. While ever-greater resources are being devoted to armament and warfare, they say, poverty and social inequality are deepening. The consequences, they argue, are borne primarily by working and oppressed sections of society, women, and the natural environment.


The signatories view the growing strength of right-wing and fascist movements as part of this development. They argue that militarism, racism, sexism, hostility toward refugees and migrants, and the destruction of the natural foundations of life are interconnected. At the same time, social forces opposing these developments are increasingly being criminalized.


The organizations therefore call for stronger international coordination among movements of struggle. They remark that resistance movements from India to France and the United States, as well as Yemen and Rojava, must not remain isolated from one another. “Their experiences must be brought together and transformed into a shared framework of internationalist solidarity. Peace, democracy, and social justice cannot be expected from the very power structures responsible for war, exploitation, and oppression. Instead, the key lies in strengthening ties between working and oppressed populations across national borders.”


Joint resistance against AKP-MHP policies


Another key focus of the declaration is the political situation in Turkey. According to the organizations, the AKP-MHP government is exploiting the international shift to the right to consolidate its authoritarian system of rule on a permanent basis. They point out that repression against the political opposition, arrests, bans, and restrictions on democratic rights are aimed at suppressing social resistance and weakening organized opposition forces.


According to the organizations, those particularly affected include workers, trade unions, democratic organizations, intellectuals, artists, and opposition political groups. At the same time, the collective rights of the Kurdish and Alevi populations continue to be disregarded. Women face patriarchal violence and discrimination, while the protection of children and the right to life of animals, as well as the preservation of nature, are systematically neglected.


The organizations do not regard these policies as an isolated development in Turkey. Rather, they see them as part of a broader authoritarian offensive through which capitalist centers of power and reactionary governments are responding to social crises. This, they argue, makes it necessary to connect democratic and social struggles in Turkey with those in Europe and other regions of the world.


Democratic solution to the Kurdish question as a shared responsibility


The participating organizations explicitly address the peace and democratic society process, stating: “Although Abdullah Öcalan and the PKK have paved the way for political and democratic dialogue through their decisions to end the armed struggle, the AKP-MHP government and the Turkish state continue to refuse to take the necessary steps toward genuine progress.”

author: Kalundi Serumaga
title: The Rise and Fall of Uganda’s Human Rights “Revolution” (1986-2026)
content:
It would not surprise me to see the emergence of a woman-led, woman-centred, or women-only political party in Uganda over the next few years, if not before the next election.


It would surprise me even less if such a party were to then fizzle out, after a brief moment of intense popularity, during which time a whole lot of new neoliberal schemes would be sold to the population as “liberation”.


Neoliberalism is basically the stage of capitalism where it seeks to return completely to its founding work methods. New governments are installed and encouraged to sweep aside all public policy aimed at shielding the vulnerable from the worst effects of those methods, and to instead facilitate a more thorough exploitation of labour and natural resources. Everything becomes a commodity.


Such a political project would simply be a more concentrated distillation of the plastic human rights revolution Uganda has undergone between 1986 and today. Because the performance of a human rights gospel was the thing that enabled the then-incoming National Resistance Movement (NRM) regime to sell and endear itself to a significant section of the Ugandan public after it seized power in 1986.


It would also be an attempt by the elite leadership of the women’s movement to hang onto the place of security and advantage they acquired through their historical strategic alliance with the NRM after it took power.


The plastic revolution grew out of the centring of human rights violations in the years of the political campaigns against the Amin regime, and the truly horrific further such violations meted out on civilians by the second Obote regime during the 1981–1986 civil war. 


Such a focus on human rights violations suited the NRA/M well as it worked to divert political discourse away from the deeper and more critical questions of imperialist domination – and also infantilism politics – by centring on a very emotive issue.


Equally practically, the cohort of feminists did sterling service in helping the NRM regime consolidate itself between 1986 and 1996. Their “gains” were to have the career concerns of elite women hard-wired into national policy at the constitutional level.


It would be the last card played by the imperialists’ hand, and our arrival at the very heart of what has been the success in managing the social damage caused by the neoliberal economic project in Uganda: the Uganda women’s movement.


The revolution was plastic because it relied heavily on external funding; it absorbed external ideas quite uncritically; it was rooted in the understanding and aspirations of the Ugandan middle class; and it was self-contradictory in many aspects, the key contradiction being the idea that there would be prosperity under neoliberalism.


These realizations unfold from the recent drama in which elements of the security forces hunted down, abducted, and detained the celebrated veteran Ugandan feminist Miria Matembe.


This was no small matter. Matembe had been an activist since the days before the current government took power. She had been a parliamentarian for a long time and had even served as a minister in the government whose agents were now inconveniencing her.


Initially denied bail when she was finally brought before the courts, Matembe spent a night in remand prison before being released on bail the following day, leading to a spontaneous, energetic celebration by a gathering of Ugandan women activists singing their English-language “anthem”, while the main character in this drama walked triumphantly from court declaring, “Jesus is king.”


This journey to such a disparate mix of wrong destinations – from illegal detention to an unquestioning court, and thereafter to an eventual release attributed to the god well used by colonialism, all the while as the English-singing cohort of feminists misattribute the initial injustice to the oppression of women, despite there being many more male Ugandans still detained and disappeared – requires a map for sure.


Destination: opportunism


The immediate starting point was the government’s announcement of the intention to create a new law regulating the way in which funds from abroad could be received and spent. This was called the “Sovereignty Bill”. As the arguments behind it rested heavily on the ruling party’s now extremely threadbare “anti-imperialist” credentials, it was said to be about “preserving Uganda’s independence”.

title: La derrota de Bolsonaro es un golpe a los Trump y los Milei
content:
El candidato presidencial brasileño Flávio Bolsonaro, del Partido Liberal (PL), reacciona mientras habla tras perder la segunda vuelta de las elecciones presidenciales, en Brasilia, Brasil. 25 de octubre de 2026. Foto: REUTERS/Adriano Machado


La derrota de Bolsonaro es un golpe político a los Trump, Milei y toda la fracción del imperialismo que había apostado por el mentor de los “milicianos” (parapoliciales) brasileños. Flávio Bolsonaro ha anunciado que impugnará la segunda ronda. Le sirve para la tribuna: la mayor parte de la burguesía mundial ha cerrado filas con la victoria de Lula. El ecológico Lula ya ha anunciado la intención de instalar a Petrobrás en la Amazonía, con la vista puesta en la exportación de carburantes a China. Las empresas chinas de vehículos eléctricos se han asociado a europeas y norteamericanas, para distribuirse el mercado brasileño y las cadenas de exportación. Con el telón de fondo de esta crisis por arriba, la campaña del balotaje fue el escenario de movilizaciones imponentes, que por una simplificación de una situación compleja han sido consideradas de apoyo a la candidatura de Lula. No hay trabajador de a pie en Brasil, sin embargo, que no tenga críticas severas a Lula y a la burocracia política, sindical y educacional del lulismo. La segunda vuelta ha consagrado presidente a Lula, pero la primera vuelta le dio a la derecha el control de parlamentos, gobernaciones y municipios. Es una herencia del PT y de su sucursal política, el Psol, que reúne a la izquierda antisocialista. La victoria de Lula no abre una perspectiva para los trabajadores.

Por Marcelo Ramal y Jorge Altamira (Política Obrera).


Lula ha dado vuelta la elección del primer turno electoral y consiguió una victoria inapelable -más de tres puntos de diferencia- sobre Flávio Bolsonaro. El candidato del Frente Brasil Popular, una coalición con partidos de la gran patronal brasileña, obtuvo nada menos que 10 millones de votos más que hace tres semanas, ocasión en la que había perdido unos 3 millones de votos en relación al balotaje de octubre de 2022. La magnitud de la transferencia de votos de ayer es atribuida a la participación del electorado que no lo había hecho el 4 de octubre pasado y a la mayoría de los que habían votado por los candidatos que no llegaron al segundo turno, pertenecientes a la derecha. La manifestación de apoyo a Lula, en la avenida Paulista de la capital del Estado, habría reunido 1.300.000 asistentes, la mayor, según los entendidos, de la historia de Brasil.


La derrota de Bolsonaro es un golpe político a los Trump, Milei y toda la fracción del imperialismo que había apostado por el mentor de los “milicianos” (parapoliciales) brasileños. En alusión al cuarto mandato de Lula, Trump señaló que “los comunistas se perpetúan en el poder”, a sabiendas de que tiene un gran margen de entendimiento con el ganador. La frase no lo predispone bien frente a Xi Jinping, a quien quiere asociar a su ‘plan de paz’ para Ucrania. Dentro de diez días, Trump perderá distritos que los republicanos han conservado como propios durante los últimos cien años.


La media vuelta de los resultados electorales está asociada a un distanciamiento de la derecha brasileña con respecto a la candidatura de Bolsonaro, que tuvo su expresión en el acogimiento que Diputados y Senado, controlados por ella, dieron a diversos proyectos de ley de Lula para ser votados de inmediato, en el transcurso de la campaña del balotaje. Bolsonaro, en cambio, fue denunciado en la prensa por lo que en Brasil se conoce como “ja ganhou”, en referencia al inmovilismo de quien asegura que no habría una modificación de los resultados previos. Flávio Bolsonaro, cuyo partido pasará a controlar el Senado a partir del 1 de enero próximo, anunció que iniciaría un juicio político y destitución del establishment judicial de Brasil, algo divisorio en la derecha y considerado peligroso para la llamada institucionalidad. Esta amenaza convirtió a Lula en el único defensor del “orden” en Brasil. Flávio Bolsonaro se vio obligado a votar el proyecto de Lula que reduce la semana laboral de 6 a 5 jornadas y a apoyar, en el debate presidencial, las medidas asistenciales de Lula -Bolsa Familia, Sistema de Salud-, las cuales, bajo el propio gobierno del Frente Brasil Popular, se encontraban en la ruina.

title: ÖHD: 10 ayda 116 mahpusun tahliyesi engellendi
content:
Türkiye’deki cezaevlerinde 434 bin 337 tutuklu ve hükümlü bulunurken, cezaevlerinin toplam kapasitesi 304 bin 184 kişiyle sınırlı. Ancak tutuklu, hükümlü sayısı gün geçtikçe artmaya devam ediyor. Ağustos ve Eylül ayında, 817 kişi cezaevine girdi. Bu kapasite beraberinde tedaviye erişim, sağlıklı beslenme gibi pek çok sorunu getiriyor.

Öte yandan siyasi mahpuslar ile diğer tutuklu ve hükümlülerin Cezaevi İdare ve Gözlem Kurulları tarafından “keyfi” gerekçelerle engellenmesi de bu sorunları ortaya çıkaran başka bir neden olarak önümüzde duruyor. Bu kurullar, hukukçular tarafından “ikinci bir mahkeme” olarak tanımlanırken kurullar tahliye engellemelerine dair “çok kitap okuma”, “az kitap okuma”, “spor yapmama”, “suyu fazla kullanma” ve benzeri gerekçeleri öne sürüyor.

Cezaevi İdare ve Gözlem Kurulları; kurum müdürü (kurul başkanı), gözlem ve sınıflandırmadan sorumlu ikinci müdür, idare memuru, cezaevi tabibi, psikiyatrist, psikolog, sosyal çalışmacı, öğretmen, infaz ve koruma baş memuru ile teknik personelden oluşuyor.

İdare ve Gözlem Kurullarının görevi ise infaz süreleri tamamlanan ve denetimli serbestlik hakkı bulunan tutsak ve hükümlüleri çağırarak, onların durumunu değerlendiriyor. Siyasi tutsakların tahliyesini engellemeye yönelik kararlarıyla bilinen İdare ve Gözlem Kurulları, siyasi tutsaklara “Pişman mısın”, “Neden örgüt koğuşundan ayrılıp bağımsız koğuşa geçmiyorsun”, “Neden kitap okuyorsun” gibi sorular sorularak, tutsakların cevaplarına göre tahliye edip edilmeme şeklinde kararını açıklıyor.

İnsan Hakları Derneği (İHD) Hapishane Komisyonu’nun raporlarına göre, Türkiye cezaevlerinde 2021-2024 yılları arasında en az 501, 2025 yılında en az 342 mahpusun tahliyesi ertelendi. Yine Özgürlük İçin Hukukçular Derneği’nin (ÖHD) 2026’nın ilk 10 ayındaki verilerine göre en az 116 mahpusun tahliyesinin ertelendiği kaydedildi.

İdare ve Gözlem Kurulları ve devam eden Barış ve Demokratik Toplum Süreci’nin cezaevlerine yansımasına ilişkin ÖHD üyesi Elif Taşdöğen, değerlendirmelerde bulundu.

Yetersiz gerekçelerle çok sayıda mahpusun tahliyesinin ertelendiğini vurgulayan Elif Taşdöğen, “Her değerlendirme somut, kişiselleştirilmiş, nesnel ve denetlenebilir verilere dayanmalıdır. Özellikle siyasi mahpuslardan ideolojik olarak pişmanlık beklenmesi, infazın hukuki niteliğini aşarak düşünce ve vicdan özgürlüğüne müdahaleye dönüştüğünü, siyasi düşüncelerini değiştirmemesi veya düşüncelerinden vazgeçtiğini beyan etmemesinin tahliye aleyhine yorumlanmasını son süreçlerde çok daha fazla görmekteyiz. Mesela 29 yıldır hapishanede bulunan Mehmet Sait Yıldırım’ın, tek kişilik hücrede olmasına rağmen ‘örgütsel hareket ettiği’ ve ‘düşünce yapısının değişmediği’ yönündeki değerlendirmelerle tahliyesinin ertelendiğine tanıklık ettik ne yazık ki” dedi.

İdare ve Gözlem Kurulu’nun yeni bir cezalandırma sistemine döndüğünü, infaz süresinin mahkeme kararı ve kanunlara dayanmasını gerektiğinin altını çizen Elif Taşdöğen, yaşanan hak ihlallerine değinerek, 7 Kasım’da hayatını kaybeden hasta mahpus Tuncer Sağlam’ı işaret etti. Elif Taşdöğen, “Tuncer Sağlam'ın tedavi gördüğü hastanede yaşamını yitirmesi, hapishanelerde hasta mahpusların yaşam hakkı ve sağlık hizmetlerine erişimi konusundaki sorunları bir kez daha gündeme getirmiştir. Tedavi hakkına erişimde yaşanan engeller ve sağlık durumunun gerektirdiği koşulların sağlanmaması, mahpuslar açısından telafisi mümkün olmayan sonuçlar doğurabilmektedir. Hiç kimse cezaevinde hastalığıyla, tedaviye erişememekle ve yaşam hakkı mücadelesiyle baş başa bırakılmamalıdır” diye belirtti.

Barış ve Demokratik Toplum Süreci’nin yalnızca siyasi aktörler üzerinden değerlendirilmemesi gerektiğini ifade eden Elif Taşdöğen, “Sürecin toplumsal karşılık bulabilmesi için hapishanelerinde yaşanan hak ihlallerinin de ortadan kaldırılması gerekir” dedi.

Elif Taşdöğen, sözlerini şöyle sürdürdü: “Demokratikleşmenin tartışıldığı bir dönemde, hapishanelerde mahpusların düşüncelerinden dolayı tahliyelerinin engellenmesi ciddi bir çelişkidir. Bununla ilgili olarak; barış sürecinin hapishanelere yansıması için öncelikle infaz hukukundaki ayrımcı ve keyfi uygulamalar sonlandırılmalı, İdare ve Gözlem Kurullarının yetkileri yeniden düzenlenmeli, infazda eşitlik ilkesi güvence altına alınmalı, infaz mevzuatı barış ve demokratikleşme perspektifiyle yeniden ele alınmalı, tutsakların tahliye hakkı idarenin takdirine bırakılmamalıdır. title: MED TUHAD-FED: Son iki yılda 15 hasta mahpus yaşamını yitirdi
content:
MED Tutuklu ve Hükümlü Aileleri ile Hukuki ve Dayanışma Dernekleri Federasyonu (MED TUHAD-FED), son iki yılda cezaevlerinde 15 hasta mahpusun yaşamını yitirdiğini açıkladı. Federasyon, ağır hasta mahpusların sağlık durumlarına rağmen tahliye edilmediğini belirterek Adalet Bakanlığına çağrıda bulundu.


Hasta mahpus Tuncer Sağlam toprağa verildi


8 Kasım 2026


Mezopotamya Ajansının haberine göre, cezaevinde bulunduğu sırada ağır sağlık sorunları yaşayan ve tedavi gördüğü hastanede hayatını kaybeden Tuncer Sağlam'ın ardından federasyon temsilcileri cezaevlerindeki hak ihlallerini değerlendirdi.


MED TUHAD-FED Eşbaşkanı Kerem Canpolat ile yönetim kurulu üyeleri Mahsum Oruç ve Şafi Hayme, Barış ve Demokratik Toplum Süreci kapsamında cezaevlerindeki koşulların iyileştirilmesi ve hasta tutukluların tahliyesi için somut adımlar atılmasını istedi.


“Cezaevlerinde yüzlerce hasta mahpus var”


Federasyon Eşbaşkanı Kerem Canpolat, devam eden siyasi sürecin toplumda umut yarattığını ancak cezaevlerindeki koşullara olumlu bir etkisinin olmadığını söyledi.


Cezaevlerinde sağlık sorunları nedeniyle günlük ihtiyaçlarını tek başına karşılayamayan yüzlerce mahpus bulunduğunu belirten Canpolat, kanser ve kronik hastalıkları olan kişilerin uygun tedavi koşullarına erişemediğini ifade etti.


Canpolat, bazı mahpusların cezaevinde kalamayacaklarına ilişkin sağlık raporlarına rağmen tahliye edilmediklerini söyledi.


Cezaevlerinde hem adli hem de siyasi mahpusların hak ihlallerine maruz kaldığını söyleyen Canpolat, devletin tutukluların yaşamını ve sağlığını koruma yükümlülüğünü hatırlattı.


73 yaşındaki hasta tutuklu Abdullah Tırpan yaşamını yitirdi


26 Ekim 2026


“Her ölüm toplumdaki güveni zedeliyor”


Barış ve Demokratik Toplum Süreci'nin başlamasından bu yana cezaevlerinde 15 hasta mahpusun yaşamını yitirdiğini belirten Canpolat, sağlık hakkına erişim ve tahliye uygulamalarının yeniden düzenlenmesi gerektiğini söyledi.


Canpolat, cezaevlerindeki ölümlerin toplumsal güveni de olumsuz etkilediğini belirterek sürecin ilerleyebilmesi için devletin somut adımlar atması gerektiğini ifade etti.


Avrupa İnsan Hakları Mahkemesi (AİHM) kararlarının uygulanmamasını da eleştiren Canpolat, hasta tutukluların tedavilerinin cezaevi dışında, ailelerinin yanında sürdürülmesini talep etti.


İzmir Barosu, hasta mahpus Yıldırım'ı ziyaret etti: "Zamana yayılmış idam cezası"


27 Ağustos 2026


“400 ila 500 ağır hasta mahpus bulunuyor”


MED TUHAD-FED Yönetim Kurulu Üyesi Mahsum Oruç, cezaevlerinde 400 ila 500 arasında ağır hasta tutuklu bulunduğunu belirtti.


Oruç, sağlık sorunları nedeniyle cezaevinde kalamayacak durumda olan kişilerin tahliyesinin çeşitli idari ve hukuki uygulamalarla engellendiğini söyledi.


Yaklaşık dört ay önce TBMM'de kabul edilen yasal düzenlemeye işaret eden Oruç, düzenlemenin uygulanmasının çeşitli kurulların değerlendirmelerine bağlı tutulduğunu ve bu nedenle tahliyelerin gerçekleşmediğini söyledi.


Oruç, söz konusu düzenlemenin etkili biçimde uygulanması halinde Tuncer Sağlam'ın yaşamını yitirmemiş olabileceğini ifade etti.


Tuncer Sağlam'ın ölümü


Federasyon temsilcileri, Tuncer Sağlam'ın sağlık durumunun ağır olmasına rağmen tahliye edilmediğini belirtti.


Sağlam'ın avukatı tarafından 23 Eylül'de yapılan tahliye başvurusunda, vücudunda 10 santimetrelik kitle bulunduğu, damar invazyonu ve olası metastaz bulgularının tespit edildiği aktarıldı. Sağlam, 7 Kasım'da tedavi gördüğü hastanede yaşamını yitirdi.


Mahsum Oruç, Sağlam'ın yaklaşık iki yıldır cezaevinde bulunduğunu ve sağlık durumunun yetkililer tarafından bilindiğini belirterek gerekli tedavinin sağlanmadığını savundu.


TAHLİYESİ ÜÇÜNCÜ KEZ ERTELENDİ


Hasta mahpus Mehmet Sait Yıldırım kalp krizi geçirdi


25 Ağustos 2026


“Tahliyeler için mekanizmalar oluşturulmalı”

author: anred
title: ¿Qué pasó en Guernica?, el gobierno de Alberto y la represión a la última ola de tomas de tierras
content:
Sergio Berni, entonces ministro de Seguridad bonaerense, se jactaba de desalojar cinco tomas de tierra por semana. Era plena pandemia, cientos de miles de familias que no podían pagar alquileres o vivían hacinadas buscaron una salida en la ocupación de terrenos. Ocurría la última gran ola de “tomas de tierras” durante el gobierno de Alberto Fernández que terminó marcada por la represión, las promesas incumplidas y el abandono. Guernica se convirtió en el caso visible y emblemático de aquella crisis: la organización de más de 2 mil familias en tierras “compradas” en dictadura destinadas a un country, la resistencia al desalojo y la exposición mediática obligaron al gobierno provincial a abrir una negociación que estuvo atravesada por titubeos, dilaciones y propuestas que no resolvían el problema habitacional. Por ANRed | Imagen: German Romeo Pena


Primero es necesario contar que la “ocupación de tierras “ tras la dictadura fue una modalidad habitual de las clases trabajadoras más empobrecidas para adquirir sus viviendas ante la sucesiva falta de respuesta habitacional que dieron las democracias posteriores, es decir ni el Estado y menos el mercado resolvieron la crisis habitacional. Para aquel entonces los últimos datos eran delCenso Nacional de 2010, el déficit habitacional alcanzaba 3,5 millones de vivienda entre ellas 1,3 millones de viviendas faltantes y 2,2 millones de viviendas que no proveían  las condiciones mínimas para mantener un nivel de vida digno. 9 millones de personas que eran inquilinos, cifras que actualmente se han agravado en el último censo del 2022.


Luego el desenlace del conflicto en Guernica, disputa que estuvo atravesado por la crisis política y económica que sacudía al gobierno de Alberto Fernández. En septiembre de 2020, la disparada de los dólares paralelos, la presión empresaria y la preocupación oficial por la inestabilidad económica habilitaron una ofensiva política contra las tomas de tierras. Sergio Massa, junto con la intendenta de Presidente Perón, Blanca Cantero, impulsaron una posición de endurecimiento frente a las ocupaciones. Cantero convocó a intendentes del conurbano que reclamaban una respuesta judicial y policial, mientras se consolidaba un bloque político que exigía terminar con la toma y enviar una señal contra nuevas recuperaciones. Guernica comenzaba a ser presentada como un antecedente peligroso que debía clausurarse para evitar que se multiplicara.


14 intendentes piden desalojar tomas de tierras y Berni se publicita defendiendo la «propiedad privada»


La tensión se agravó en octubre con la ocupación de la estancia Casa Nueva, perteneciente a la familia Etchevehere, en Entre Ríos. La iniciativa fue impulsada por Dolores Etchevehere junto al Proyecto Artigas, con el acompañamiento de Juan Grabois y militantes vinculados del Movimiento de Trabajadores Excluidos (MTE), que proponía desarrollar un proyecto agroecológico en esas tierras. La reacción de empresarios y la derecha política que venía presionando por desalojar Guernica reaccionó de inmediato: el conflicto se convirtió en una bandera contra las recuperaciones de tierras y en una supuesta amenaza generalizada a la propiedad privada. La disputa con los Etchevehere intensificó la presión política y mediática sobre el gobierno nacional. Dentro del Frente de Todos también se profundizaron las diferencias: mientras un sector intentaba sostener la negociación y encontrar una salida habitacional, Massa, Berni y los intendentes reclamaban hacer cumplir la orden judicial. Las negociaciones impulsadas inicialmente desde Nación, con participación de funcionarios vinculados al Movimiento Evita, contemplaron una posible relocalización colectiva, pero naufragaron en medio de las disputas internas entre el Movimiento Evita y La Cámpora. Desde septiembre, Andrés Larroque quedó al frente de las conversaciones provinciales, cada vez más condicionadas por la presión judicial y política.


Finalmente, el 28 de octubre, cuando todavía se discutía una última prórroga y existían conversaciones para evitar una intervención violenta, la Justicia rechazó el pedido de postergación y la gobernación cancelo las negociaciones inventando justificaciones. En la madrugada del 29, unos 4.000 efectivos de la Policía Bonaerense.. La decisión terminó imponiendo la línea de Berni y de los intendentes: el desalojo como respuesta disciplinadora frente a las recuperaciones de tierras, antes que una solución de fondo a la emergencia habitacional. Dossier

Uns bleiben nur Schulden und Sorgen, während die Aussicht auf eine bessere Zukunft schwindet.

Coimbra bleibt nicht außen vor! Wir rufen alle dazu auf, sich am kommenden *Mittwoch (14.) ab 17:30 Uhr auf der Praça da República* zu einer Malaktion sowie zum Anbringen eines Transparents und anderer Materialien zu versammeln

.“ portug.

Aufruf zur Demo am 10. Oktober


 der Instagram-Plattform „Não dá mais para viver assim“ („So kann man nicht mehr leben“) und mehr dazu:


In Portugal schließen sich die Kämpfe gegen Lebenshaltungskosten und für öffentliche Infrastuktur zusammen – ein Generalstreik spätestens am 24. November nicht ausgeschlossen 


Portugal: Nach der gewaltsamen Räumung kämpfen neue Protestlager gegen Wohnungsnot und Mietengesetz in Lissabon und Porto auch fürs Demonstrationsrecht


Wohnungskrise in Portugal: Protestcamp oder Weihnachtsmarkt?


„

In Portugal hat die Aktivistin Renata Cambra vor Gericht einen symbolischen Sieg errungen: Ihr Zelt auf einem zentralen Platz in Lissabon darf aufgebaut bleiben. Aber genau dort soll bald der Weihnachtsmarkt stehen. Sie ist zur Symbolfigur der Proteste gegen die Wohnungskrise in Portugal geworden. Die Aktivistin Renata Cambra verbucht einen juristischen Erfolg, denn ihr Zelt auf der Praça do Rossio in Lissabon darf aufgebaut bleiben. Genug Solidarität für ein neues Protestlager gab es zunächst aber nicht. Das Gericht entschied, ihr Zelt sei keine illegale Besetzung des öffentlichen Raums, sondern ein symbolisches Element des Protests. Die Entscheidung beschränkte die Erlaubnis jedoch auf die Demonstrantin, die den Antrag gestellt hat. In dem Verfahren prüfte das Gericht nicht die „Rechtmäßigkeit einer kollektiven Besetzung“ des Rossio oder das Bestehen eines allgemeinen Rechts, „Zelte im öffentlichen Raum durch eine unbestimmte Zahl von Teilnehmern“ zu errichten.


Protestzelt darf auch nachts stehenbleiben


Das Gericht stellte außerdem fest, dass ein Ende der Demonstrationen um 0 Uhr 30 „nicht absolut und automatisch“ ist, und erlaubte Renata Cambra, mit einem Zelt die Nacht über auf der Praça do Rossio zu bleiben.  Der Protest kann dem Gerichtsentscheid zufolge bis zum 24. November 2026 fortgesetzt werden. Das ist der geplante Termin für die Schlussabstimmung über den Staatshaushalt für 2027.


Renata Cambra und die Bewegung „Acampada de Lisboa“ sehen darin einen Sieg für das Demonstrationsrecht in Portugal. (…)


Nach einer gewalttätigen Nacht zum Sonntag, in der es in Lissabon und Porto erneut zu Polizeieinsätzen mit Schlagstöcken kam, blieb die Lage ruhig. Das gewaltsame Vorgehen der Polizei am Wochenende veranlasste den Präsidenten der Republik, António José Seguro, die Regierung und die Ombudsfrau um Aufklärung zu bitten. Ein Anwalt kündigte außerdem eine Strafanzeige wegen Amtsmissbrauchs gegen den Innenminister und den verantwortlichen Polizeidirektor an.


Das Innenministerium (MAI) unterstrich, dass die Entscheidung des Verwaltungsgerichts zu den Wohnungsprotesten die Rechtmäßigkeit der Polizeieinsätze nicht bewerte und kein Recht auf das Aufstellen von Zelten im öffentlichen Raum anerkenne

…“

Artikel von Joana Mourão Carvalho vom 3. November 2026 auf Euronews


 mit Video


Proteste gegen die Wohnungsnot in Portugal


„

Like, not to be all “in my dayyyy” about it, but… at 16, my friends and I were expected to be broadly responsible for our presence in the world. Most of us had jobs, we navigated public transport, looked after younger siblings. We were expected to make informed decisions about our future careers and our sexual partners. We were allowed to leave education and work full time (this was not necessarily good thing - I think increasing the school leaving age to 18 was broadly for the best). Most of us were smoking, or drinking, or both - again, not good things, but just facts - and many of us were sexually active. Many of the AFAB people I knew were on the pill. Legally, we could live independently, or get married with adult consent.

Legally (I live in the UK) we were not minors, although we inhabited an odd legal limbo until we turned 18, and we were certainly not “children”. Intellectually, socially, though, we were considered (young) adults, or at the most “older teenagers.” We were expected to read mostly adult books (rather than middle grade or YA), watch the news/read papers, watch mostly adult television.

author: Daron Letts
title: Dialogue about Inuit-specific housing funding underway, says Indigenous Services Minister
content:
Inuit-Nunangat’s share of billions of dollars in federal housing and infrastructure funding announced in

Thursday

‘s budget

 remains undetermined, but that could change soon, Indigenous Services Minister Mandy Gull-Masty said Saturday in Iqaluit.


“I think that we’ll have greater clarity in the next few days,” Gull-Masty said during a news conference at the Inuusirvik Community Wellness Hub. It marked the start of a two-day visit to the territory, her first trip to the eastern Arctic. In addition to her role as Indigenous Services minister, Gull-Masty is the Liberal MP for Abitibi—Baie-James—Nunavik—Eeyou, the sprawling Quebec riding that includes Nunavik.


The Liberal government’s budget allocated $30 billion for First Nations housing and infrastructure as part of Prime Minister Mark Carney’s new commitment to eliminate homelessness within a decade.


But the budget did not mention comparable investments for Inuit communities.


However, discussions with Inuit organizations about how to fund housing and infrastructure in Inuit communities are ongoing, Gull-Masty said.


“It’s imperative that we take the time, that we take that space and really have that conversation to reflect the uniqueness of the North,” she said. “It’s important for us if we want to reach that target in the North that we shape it according to the realities of what it means to live here and deliver services.”


She met with representatives from Nunavut Tunngavik Inc., the organization that represents Inuit beneficiaries under the Nunavut Agreement, on Saturday.


On Thursday, she met with Inuit Tapiriit Kanatami president Natan Obed, the head of the national organization for Inuit in Canada.


Gull-Masty said the dialogue about Inuit-specific funding for housing and infrastructure will continue later this year during a meeting of the Inuit-Crown Partnership Committee, a bilateral forum that brings together Inuit leaders and federal cabinet ministers to advance shared priorities.


Nunavut MP Lori Idlout and Iqaluit Mayor Solomon Awa also met with Gull-Masty on Saturday.


Idlout said she is confident Nunavut will be included in Carney’s commitment to eliminate homelessness across Canada within a decade.


“What this government will need to do is make sure that it works respectfully with the Inuit organizations to ensure that Nunavut’s needs are being met,” Idlout said.


Awa shares Idlout’s optimism.


“It can be done if we work really hard,” he said.

author: Emma Honeybun
title: Prime minister announces $1B for housing, new hospital to ‘tackle’ homelessness in Winnipeg
content:
Prime Minister Mark Carney joined Manitoba Premier Wab Kinew and the mayor of Winnipeg to announce a joint funding venture to build more than 2,000 new homes and an addictions treatment centre in the middle province’s capital.

The federal government will be allocating $1 billion overall, with $800 million going to the homes and the remaining $200 million going to the proposed Winnipeg Mental Health and Addictions Centre, as well as the refurbishment of similar facilities.

“There’s no simple answer,” Carney said. “This is a hard problem. And hard problems demand the humility to learn from previous well-intentioned efforts that have fallen short.”

Funds will also go to supporting local, grassroots organizations that are already involved in addressing the homelessness crisis, including End Homelessness Winnipeg, the North End Women’s Centre, and Chalmers Neighbourhood Renewal Corporation.

Carney said the partnership is one project in an “unprecedented” $30 billion allocation in the 2026 budget, with the end goal of ending homelessness in Canada in 10 years.

“Help works,” he said, which extends to housing and healthcare.

Alongside federal, provincial and municipal governments, funding for these Winnipeg-based projects will also be provided by First Nation governments such as the Southern Chiefs’ Organization (SCO), as well as private funders such as True North Sports and Entertainment, owner of the Winnipeg Jets and the primary investor in several major infrastructure projects downtown.

“It’s the first time in our country’s history where every level of government has come together to tackle homelessness,” Kinew said. “Including First Nations and Métis governments.”

“The reality is that a huge part of what we see is that [in the past] failed policies like residential schools left a disproportionate number of Indigenous people vulnerable to the ravages of addictions. And the only way for us to find a solution is to have the full participation and engagement of the leaders of those people.”

He said, “A challenge for Indigenous Peoples in Canada has never been that Indigenous Peoples don’t know the solutions. Absolutely we do. The challenge has been that we didn’t have access to the resources and to the decision-making tables to make that happen.”

Carney said that previous government and community efforts to address homelessness have been “inadequately resourced, poorly co-ordinated, and not sustained.”

He said it’s “imperative” that this new strategy succeeds.”

“In Canada, we know we’re not perfect, but we always strive to be good,” Carney said. “We do things because they’re right, not because they’re easy. Ending homelessness is hard; it’s good, and it’s right. And it will require more than compassion.

“It will require ambition, execution, and partnership amongst all levels of government with contributions from philanthropy and business,” Carney added.

There was no determined answer when it came to where most of the 2,000 planned units will be built, but the first 373 are currently being developed inside of Wehwehneh Bahgahkinahgohn, formerly known as the Hudson’s Bay Building, just down the street from the Manitoba Legislature.

The building was acquired by the SCO in 2022, and is scheduled to be complete in 2028. Funding is supported through a partnership with True North.

Jamil Mahmood, the executive director of Main Street Project, a major non-profit addictions treatment centre and homeless shelter, said that additional housing would be useful anywhere in the downtown core.

The organization’s emergency shelter on Main Street has been affected by several fires in 2026, beginning in January. The most recent was on Oct. 31.

Money from this announcement will help refurbish the building, which housed over 2,900 people in 2025, according to its annual report.

“We know that’s where people are, we know that’s where the resources are, so the more you can put housing up where resources are is great,” he said.

“I think over time we can definitely expand that … from the core area to different areas, but then you also need to move resources to those places,” he added. “So we believe a decentralized model would work over time, but right now we have resources downtown.”

Mahmood said “the big thing,” however, is the inclusion of wrap-around support on-site, and staff who can remain there to help.

“I think that helps a lot of people really feel more comfortable with this housing,” he said. “And also, the reverse …

author: CMI Argentina
title: Misiones: intimidación policial a la comunidad Mbya Guaraní Kuaray Amba
content:
Denuncian un accionar continuo de hostigamiento de la fuerza policial sobre la comunidad del pueblo Mbya Guaraní Kuaray Amba, en Puerto Iguazú, y advierten que puede ser la preparatoria de un nuevo desalojo ilegal como el que sufrió Puente Quemado II, en la misma provincia.


Compartimos el comunicado del Equipo Misiones de Pastoral Aborigen (EMiPA):


Kuaray Amba: la intimidación como mecanismo de control


La persecución a Kuaray Amba, en Puerto Iguazú, sumó este martes un nuevo capítulo. Alrededor de 15 efectivos policiales llegaron a la Comunidad, bajo la misma modalidad que en las ocasiones anteriores: sin previo aviso y solicitando información.


Resulta llamativo el despliegue de tantos efectivos policiales si lo que necesitan es solamente recabar algunos datos. ¿O será que buscan intimidar a la Comunidad y preparar el terreno para un posible desalojo forzado, como ocurrió en Puente Quemado II?


https://argentina.indymedia.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/Intimidacion-policial.mp4


Video: EMiPA


“Trajeron una nota, pero no estaba dirigida a la Comunidad ni a mí”, explicó Lidio Rivarola, mburuvicha. El documento que exhibieron era un oficio judicial dirigido al jefe de la Comisaría Seccional Primera de Puerto Iguazú. Allí se hace referencia a una denuncia por una presunta intrusión en terrenos del Estado provincial y se ordena realizar una inspección policial para relevar la ocupación actual e histórica del territorio.


“Querían datos de la gente, pero se los negamos. ¿Para qué los quieren? Dicen que es para llevar al juez. Nos amenazan con el desalojo”, aseguró Lidio.


Hasta el momento, no existe una orden de desalojo ni una imputación contra integrantes de la Comunidad. Además, ya se presentó un escrito ante la Dirección de Asuntos Guaraníes, en el que la Comunidad dejó clara su postura: no va a abandonar el territorio.

title: „Shut Elbit Down“: Proteste gegen Niederlassung des israelischen Rüstungskonzerns „Elbit Systems Deutschland“
content:
Dossier


„

Vor der Niederlassung des israelischen Rüstungskonzerns „Elbit Systems“ haben Demonstranten ein Protestcamp aufgeschlagen. Was sie damit bewirken wollen und wie die Firma reagiert. Seit Dienstag besetzen knapp 30 Anhänger der Gruppe „Shut Elbit Down“ eine Grünfläche am Safranberg in Ulm. Angereist aus dem gesamten Bundesgebiet, haben sie ihre Zelte unmittelbar vor der Niederlassung des israelischen Rüstungskonzerns „Elbit Systems Deutschland“ aufgeschlagen. Wie lange sie dort verharren werden, lassen die Aktivisten bewusst offen. „Wenn es sein muss, bleiben wir einen Monat“, kündigt eine Teilnehmerin an. Das Ziel der Demonstranten: die Schließung der Ansiedlung des Großkonzerns in Ulm

…“

Bericht von Dennis Bacher vom 25.04.2025 in schwaebische.de


 („„Wenn es sein muss, bleiben wir einen Monat“: Demonstranten belagern israelisches Unternehmen“) mit Video und Fotos – siehe mehr zu den Protesten und deren Folgen:


Grundrechtekomitee beobachtet den Prozess gegen „Ulm 5“ wegen Sabotage gegen Elbit: Vorsitzende Richterin verweigert den Angeklagten grundlegendes


RAV zum Prozess gegen die »Ulm 5«: Unabhängige Beobachtung erheblich erschwert


„

Der Republikanische Anwältinnen- und Anwälteverein e.V. (RAV) kritisiert nach Prozessbeobachtung das Verbot handschriftlicher Notizen sowie Einschränkungen der Kommunikation zwischen Angeklagten und Verteidigung. Eine unabhängige Beobachtung der Verhandlungsführung werde erheblich erschwert.


Der RAV hat am 25.09.2026 die Hauptverhandlung gegen die sogenannten »Ulm 5« vor der 18. Großen Strafkammer des Landgerichts Stuttgart beobachtet. Nach Einschätzung des Prozessbeobachters Rechtsanwalt Yunus Ziyal erschweren die Bedingungen im Hochsicherheitssaal des OLG-Prozessgebäudes in Stuttgart-Stammheim sowohl eine unabhängige Dokumentation des Verfahrens als auch die effektive Wahrnehmung von Verteidigungsrechten. (…)


Kritisch bewertet der RAV zudem, dass eine von der Verteidigung auf eigene Kosten beschäftigte Protokollkraft nicht zugelassen wurde. Gerade in umfangreichen Strafverfahren könne eine solche Unterstützung wesentlich für eine effektive Verteidigungsarbeit sein. Ein pauschaler Ausschluss bedürfe daher einer konkreten und nachvollziehbaren Begründung.


Kommunikation mit der Verteidigung erheblich erschwert


Besonders problematisch ist aus Sicht des RAV die räumliche Situation der Angeklagten. Diese saßen während der Hauptverhandlung getrennt von ihren Verteidiger*innen in einem Glaskasten. Eine Kommunikation war lediglich über Telefonhörer möglich. Da Teile der Verhandlung verdolmetscht wurden, mussten sich die Angeklagten nach den Beobachtungen von Ziyal zeitweise entscheiden, ob sie über Kopfhörer der Übersetzung folgen oder über den Telefonhörer mit ihrer Verteidigung kommunizieren wollten. Beides gleichzeitig war technisch nicht möglich. (…)


»Was in Stammheim vor sich geht, ist zutiefst besorgniserregend. Es ist sehr fraglich, ob diese Prozesssituation noch mit rechtsstaatlichen Grundsätzen zu vereinbaren ist«, resümiert Rechtsanwalt Ziyal.


Der RAV fordert deshalb:


– eine verhältnismäßige Ausgestaltung sitzungspolizeilicher Maßnahmen


– die Zulassung handschriftlicher Notizen für Prozessbeobachter*innen


– eine konkrete Prüfung der Zulassung von Protokollkräften sowie


– technische und räumliche Bedingungen, die es den Angeklagten ermöglichen, der Verdolmetschung zu folgen und zugleich vertraulich mit ihrer Verteidigung zu kommunizieren

…“

Pressemitteilung vom 10.11.2026


des RAV


 zur Prozessbeobachtung der „Ulm 5“ in Stammheim


Sabotage gegen Elbit: Prozessauftakt gegen »Ulm 5« endet im Eklat


„… Zum Auftakt des Prozesses der »Ulm 5« in Stuttgart-Stammheim gab es am Montag Tumult. Den Aktivist*innen wird unter anderem vorgeworfen, im September 2024 Sabotage beim deutschen Ableger des israelischen Rüstungskonzerns Elbit Systems in Ulm betrieben zu haben. Ziel ihrer Aktion war es, Aufmerksamkeit für Elbits Verantwortung im Gaza-Genozid zu erzeugen – und diesen durch direkte Aktion zu erschweren. Die fünf Freund*innen befinden sich seit ihrer Festnahme unter erschwerten Bedingungen in Untersuchungshaft. Dutzende Menschen waren hauptsächlich aus Berlin angereist, um die Aktivist*innen zu unterstützen, vor Ort schlossen sich ihnen auch Gruppen aus Stuttgart an. Vor dem Gebäude gab es über den ganzen Tag eine Kundgebung, die Gefangenen wurden aus der Gruppe heraus bei ihrer Ankunft mit Rufen wie »Freiheit für alle politischen Gefangenen« …

author: anno
title: Kundgebung für Maja & Zaid
content:
+++Kundgebung vor dem Bundesjustizministerium am 13.11. um 13:00 Uhr in der Anton-Wilhelm-Amo-Str. 37.+++


Am 25.11. soll das Gericht in Paris über Zaids Auslieferung nach Ungarn entscheiden.


Trotz des Machtwechsels in Ungarn können wir aus Majas, Tobis und Ilarias Erfahrungen erahnen, was ihn dort erwartet: Isolation, Gewalt und Willkür, sowie ein politisches Verfahren.


Zudem sind die ungarischen Behörden und das Knastsystem für ihren gewaltvollen Rassismus bekannt.


Wir gehen zusätzlich davon aus, dass Zaid eine Abschiebung von Ungarn nach Syrien drohen würde.


Währenddessen sitzt Maja seit über 2 Jahren in Ungarn im Knast. Zuletzt wurde Majas Urteil zu 7 Jahren Haft unter strengsten Bedingungen rechtskräftig.


Maja wurde eine Rücküberstellung nach Deutschland zugesichert.


Während eine rechtswidrige Auslieferung nur wenige Stunden dauert, schieben sich die deutschen Behörden die Zuständigkeit für die Rücküberstellung hin und her. Es kann sein, dass Maja noch ein weiteres Jahr in ungarischer Haft überstehen muss – und das, obwohl sich Majas Haftbedingungen in der Strafhaft weiter verschlechtert haben!


Wir werden weder das noch eine weitere Auslieferung nach Ungarn hinnehmen!


Deshalb rufen wir für den 13. und 14. November dazu auf, den Druck auf alle verantwortlichen Behörden zu erhöhen!


Besonders wichtig aus deutscher Sicht sind dabei französische Konsulate, das Justizministerium und das Auswärtige Amt.


Gemeinsam wollen wir am Freitag, dem 13.11. möglichst vielen französischen Konsulaten in Deutschland einen offenen Brief übergeben, in dem unsere Forderung klar werden: keine Auslieferung von Zaid nach Ungarn!


Dafür brauchen wir Euch! Organisiert eigene Briefübergaben in Euren Städten!


Am Ende des Aufrufs findet ihr den Brief als Druckvorlage und eine Liste der Konsulate.


Noch ein kleiner Hinweis: Wenn ihr zu den Botschaften geht, kündigt die Übergabe am besten vorher per Mail bei den Konsulaten an!


Am selben Tag wird es auch eine Kundgebung vor dem Justizministerium in Berlin geben, um deutlich zu machen, dass Maja jetzt nach Deutschland rücküberstellt werden muss! Kommt und supportet am 13.11. um 13:00 Uhr in der Anton-Wilhelm-Amo-Str. 37.


passiert am 13.11.2026

İstanbul Kadıköy Kaymakamlığı, TOBB ETÜ yurdunda yaşamını yitiren 19 yaşındaki trans kadın Arya için adalet talebiyle yapılmak istenen eylemi yasakladı.


“Arya’ya Ne Oldu?” İnisiyatifi’nin bugün Kadıköy Süreyya Operası önünde düzenlemek istediği eylem öncesinde polis, LGBTİ+’ların etrafını sardı.


Gazeteci Yusuf Çelik'in aktardığı bilgilere göre, bir süre polisle görüşen LGBTİ+’lar, eylemi gerçekleştirmeden alandan ayrıldı.

Kadıköy Kaymakamlığı, TOBB ETÜ yurdunda yaşamını yitiren 19 yaşındaki trans kadın Arya için adalet arayan "Arya'ya Ne Oldu?" İnisiyatifi'nin bugün Kadıköy'de yapacağı eylemi yasakladı. Video: @21yusufcelk https://t.co/Of4HXkLOAP


— bianet (@bianetorg_)

November 8, 2026


Çelik'in aktardığı bilgiye göre, Kadıköy Kaymakamlığı, yasak kararını 2911 Sayılı Toplantı ve Gösteri Yürüyüşleri Kanunu ile 5442 Sayılı İl İdaresi Kanunu’na dayandırdı.


Kaymakamlığın açıklamasında, “İntihar değil cinayet! 19 yaşında TOBB ETÜ yurdunda intihara sürüklenerek katledilen Arya’nın hesabını sormak için sokaklardayız!” sloganıyla yapılması planlanan eylemin toplumda infial uyandırabileceği ve “toplumsal iç barışı tehdit edebileceği” öne sürüldü.


Açıklamada ayrıca eyleme katılacak gruplarla yurttaşlar arasında provokatif olaylar yaşanabileceği iddia edildi.


Kaymakamlık, 8 Kasım saat 00.00’dan itibaren bir gün süreyle ilçe genelindeki tüm açık alanlarda basın açıklaması, yürüyüş, oturma eylemi, miting ve benzeri etkinliklerin yanı sıra bu etkinliklere yönelik çağrı yapılmasını, bildiri dağıtılmasını ve stant açılmasını da yasakladı.


Yasak kararı, bugün saat 16.50’de kamuoyuna duyuruldu.


Ne olmuştu?


TOBB Ekonomi ve Teknoloji Üniversitesi (TOBB ETÜ) İngiliz Dili ve Edebiyatı Bölümü öğrencisi 19 yaşındaki trans kadın Arya, 13 Nisan’da üniversitenin yurdunda yaşamını yitirmişti.


Arya’nın ölümünün ardından arkadaşları ve üniversiteli LGBTİ+ toplulukları, olayın tüm yönleriyle aydınlatılması talebiyle “Arya’ya Ne Oldu İnisiyatifi”ni kurdu. İnisiyatif, Arya’nın eğitim ve yurt yaşamı boyunca sözlü, fiziksel ve dijital şiddete maruz bırakıldığını, yurt yönetimi ve bazı öğrenciler tarafından hedef gösterildiğini açıklamıştı.


Soruşturmada Arya’nın telefon ve bilgisayar gibi temel dijital materyallerinin henüz incelenmediğine dikkat çeken inisiyatif, ölümün yalnızca bireysel bir karar olarak değerlendirilmemesi gerektiğini vurgulamıştı. İnisiyatif, sistematik transfobinin ve kurumsal ihmallerin de soruşturulmasını talep etmişti.

author: Kate Sharpley
title: We Have Fed You All for a Thousand Years : Travels of a Protest Poem
content:
As ‘We Have Fed You All for a Thousand Years’ this poem is possibly the most widely reprinted item from Freedom.

In September 1893 the London anarchist newspaper Freedom : A Journal of Anarchist Communism published a poem called ‘A Humble Reminder : To the Propertied Classes’, credited to ‘N.’[1] It’s an anti-capitalist protest, lamenting the ‘workers’ dead’ whose deaths enriched those ‘propertied classes’. It rails at the rich ‘We have fed you all for a thousand years, / And you hail us still unfed’. I do not know who ‘N.’ was, though they seem to be connected to the Freedom milieu. Freedom had published another poem by them, ‘The Pet Voter’, in August 1892.[2] Max Nettlau used the same initial when writing in Freedom in June 1891; the Fabian socialist Edith Nesbit had a poem ‘A Word For The Children’ in Freedom in February 1891 (‘The right to give help is your own, / The right to claim it theirs.’) Neither seems a convincing candidate for the authorship of this poem. The Kipling connection

‘N.’ introduced their poem by saying it was ‘slightly altered from Rudyard Kipling’s Ode in praise of English Enterprise.’ That’s a reference to Kipling’s ‘Song of the Dead’ published four months earlier in The English Illustrated Magazine (May 1893). ‘N.’s address to the propertied classes ‘For if blood be the price of England’s wealth, / Good God, we ha’ paid in full’ rewrites Kipling’s address to the sea ‘If blood be the price of admiralty, / Lord God, we ha’ paid in full!’.[3] The ‘Humble Reminder’ changes Kipling’s poem – but leans heavily upon it. Mark Leier said ‘strictly speaking the poem is not a parody of Kipling’s poem but a re-working of the words based on the original verse and meter.’[4] It reminds me of Utah Philips’ comment on IWW songmaking: ‘The Wobblies liked to steal the hymn tunes ‘cos they were pretty and change the words so they made more sense.’[5]

The connection to Kipling persisted. He was credited in many of the reprints (inevitable, perhaps, given that the author remained unknown and their debt to Kipling was clear). There were even articles discussing what it would mean if the poem were by Kipling.[6] Reprinted and recited

Once printed, it was always possible for the poem to reappear, and this one spread beyond the anarchist press, becoming a standard of labour movement papers. The title often changed, varying from ‘The Cry of Toil’ to ‘The Capitalist’. Just as the connection to Kipling is sometimes there and sometimes not, the text varies between the poetic ‘ha’’ to the everyday ‘have’.

Apparently a version was published in Wilkes-Barre, Pennsylvania in 1895.[7] The Portland anarchist newspaper The Firebrand reprinted the poem (anonymously) as ‘The Workers Outcry’ in 1897.[8] Changes had been made to Americanise the text: instead of pounds the third line talks of ‘there’s never a dollar of all your wealth’.

Sometimes you can read about the poem’s life off the printed page. In May 1897 Miss Olive Keep recited ‘We have fed you all for a thousand years’ at a gathering of the Socialist Labor Party. [9]. In August 1899, The Carpenter, a union journal for ‘Carpenters, Stair Builders, Machine Wood Workers, Planing Mill Men, and Kindred Interests’ reprinted the ‘Firebrand version’ (with credit).[10] In 1904 the poem reappeared as ‘The Price of England’s Wealth’ in Glasgow’s The Voice of Labour.[11] This version talks of ‘sovereigns’ rather than ‘pounds’ or ‘dollars’ but there are other changes: I can’t tell if it’s rewritten from the Freedom or Firebrand version.

The anarchist journal Mother Earth (‘published every 15th of the month’) reprinted ‘The Cry of Toil’ (credited to Kipling) in April 1908.[12] On April 18, 1908 it appeared in the IWW’s Industrial Union Bulletin (also credited to Kipling).[13] Once the poem was reprinted in the IWW songbook, and was later put to music (‘about 1916’ by Rudolf von Liebich), it was firmly established as a classic of working class protest.

In November 1913 strikers in Auckland used a line from the poem on their banner during the 1913 Waterfront Strike: ‘If blood be the price of your cursed wealth, good God we have bought it fair’.[14] It’s not often we get the names of people who helped circulate the text but ‘Gordon’ suggested it (as ‘The Workers’ Answer’) in the 1917 compilation New songs for Butte Mining Camp.[15]

As ‘We Have Fed You All for a Thousand Years’ this poem is possibly the most widely reprinted item from Freedom. In March 1969 it was reprinted …

author: Anne Marxze Umil
title: Trump out! | Progressive groups launch 12 days of protest
content:
Photo by Emman Capones/Pinoy Weekly

We don’t want this lunatic to come to our country. He is a mass murderer who has initiated wars around the world, led by and benefiting the US.

Progressive groups launch 12 days of protest as the visit of US President Donald Trump to the Philippines approaches.

“Trump is not welcome here in the Philippines, he is not welcome anywhere in the world,” said International League of Peoples’ Struggles-Philippines Secretary General Arnold Padilla in a press conference on Wednesday, November 4.

Trump is scheduled to visit the Philippines on November 16 to sign the Pax Silica initiative also in time for the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) Summit.

“Under the banner of Trump Out, we shall hold daily actions ranging from rallies, indoor assemblies, public forums, pickets, concerts, teach-ins, camp-outs, and vigils aimed to express the Filipino people’s strong objection to Trump’s visit,” Bagong Alyansang Makabayan (Bayan) Chairperson Teddy Casiño said.

Casiño added in Filipino, “Trump represents the largest imperialist power, which sows war, terror, oppression, and plunder across the world. This includes military aggression against Iran, support for genocide, the imposition of economic sanctions and intervention in Venezuela, Cuba, and other countries; military escalation in the Philippines and across the Asia-Pacific; and brutal repression of immigrants and critics within his own country.”

For Ana Marie Nemenzo of the Network Opposed to Pax Silica, Trump should be declared as persona non grata and barred from entering the country.

“We don’t want this lunatic to come to our country. He is a mass murderer who has initiated wars around the world, led by and benefiting the US. This shows that imperialism remains very much alive and must be opposed because it poses a major threat to the planet and endangers the lives of ordinary people around the world,” she added.

Nemenzo said the Philippines has not been truly free. She said since the so-called independence in 1946, the Americans have kept the Philippines tied to the U.S. economy. She also criticized the presence of soldiers and its equipment in the country and urged the public to join the movement to drive U.S. military forces out of the country.

Nemenzo also added that Pax Silica will only further tie the Philippines “to an economic framework that primarily benefits powerful countries seeking access to our critical resources.”

“We know that the Philippines is among the most vulnerable countries. The loss of people’s livelihoods must be a paramount concern,” she added, saying that her organization, Women’s Health is one in the campaign against Pax Silica.

For Pastor Allan Sarte, secretary general of Philippines-Palestine Friendship Association, Trump is the number one enabler of (then Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin) Netanyahu that killed 70,000 citizens of Gaza, more than 20,000 of which are children. “We cannot in conscience welcome Trump in the Philippines,” he said.

Not only the Filipinos are rejecting Trump, Bayan said the glaring defeat of Trump’s party in the U.S. midterm elections is a powerful boost to the Trump Out campaign.

“The Democratic Party’s landslide victory, wresting control of both Houses of Congress and defeating Republicans even in traditional strongholds like Texas, Kansas, and South Carolina, is a resounding repudiation of Trump and his rule,” the group said in a statement.

The group said the results of the election is a reflection of the growing disgust and rejection by the American people of Trump’s corrupt, authoritarian, war mongering, racist, anti-immigrant and over all anti-people policies. “They show that even in his own country, Trump faces mounting opposition to his disastrous leadership,” Bayan said.

The group expressed their solidarity with the American people who are resisting Trump’s attacks on their democratic rights, livelihoods, and welfare.

“They see through his collusion with his big corporate backers to enrich himself. They oppose his war on Iran and belligerence towards other countries’ sovereignty,” Bayan said. (RVO)

author: Vinil Kumar
title: Western Sydney Airport is a gift to business
content:
It’s rare for aviation executives and prime ministers to party in Western Sydney. But the opening of Sydney’s second airport, Western Sydney International (WSI), was an unmissable photo opportunity. Attendees included Prime Minister Anthony Albanese, his predecessors Tony Abbott and Scott Morrison, Jetstar CEO Stephanie Tully and NSW Premier Chris Minns. 

After the first passenger flight departed, the exodus back to the leafy Eastern Suburbs began, leaving behind the roar of turbo-fan engines that will only grow more frequent once the fanfare around the airport subsides.

The new airport is a monument to twenty-first century capitalism: a feat of human ingenuity, subordinated to corporate interests, with working-class people paying the price.

Background

Sections of business have long campaigned for a second major airport in Sydney. 

The established Sydney Kingsford Smith Airport at Mascot is boxed in by residential suburbs and Botany Bay. A third runway was opened in 1994, but community protests won a night-time curfew and hourly flight limits. 

Aviation is central to supply chains and corporate Australia wanted a new airport with minimal restrictions on its use.

After 60 years of 

proposals, disputes and false starts

, the project was revived in 2012, with the release of the Joint Study on Aviation Capacity in the Sydney Region by the federal and New South Wales governments. Its co-authors included the incoming Business Council of Australia head, Jennifer Westacott. 

The 

report

 warned Kingsford Smith airport would reach capacity by 2027 and unmet passenger and freight demand could cost as much as $60 billion by 2060. It argued the curfew “creates impediments for night-time movements of freight”, but that “an opportunity exists for a 24-hour freight facility to be established at a secondary airport”. Proximity to future warehousing and distribution centres made Western Sydney an enticing option.

Although the proposal for an airport at Badgerys Creek was rejected by the state and federal governments at the time, the 

Daily Telegraph

 immediately launched a 

renewed campaign

 for one. It was joined in its 

lobbying

 by the National Australia Bank, Harvey Norman, Crown Resorts, Channel 7 and executives from Western Sydney University. Backing was also 

secured

 from the peak body of local councils in Sydney. 

The Sydney Business Chamber, Western Sydney, led by former Labor state minister and member for Granville David Borger, 

established the Western Sydney Airport Alliance

 to cohere a local campaign for the airport.

In 2014, Liberal Prime Minister Tony Abbott’s federal cabinet approved the proposal for an airport at Badgerys Creek.  

Local residents objected. “Well, it’s going to make Western Sydney a nightmare to live in”, Geoff Brown, a 40-year resident of Penrith and member of the Western Sydney Conservation alliance, 

told the ABC

 at the time. “Growth and a fair go for Western Sydney doesn’t mean trashing the place, doesn't mean turning it into a wasteland of factories and industrial sites”, he said.

Abbott’s successor, Malcolm Turnbull 

manoeuvred

 to make the new airport a government-run project. The state and federal governments provided 

$29 billion in public funding

. Meanwhile Western Sydney’s hospitals, schools and public housing continued to crumble.

Government control enabled a grander development plan, including the construction of a new CBD around the airport, 

Bradfield City

. Part of Bradfield City’s purpose is military support, by “strengthening the defence industrial base through advanced manufacturing and semiconductor packaging”. 

The government ensured businesses had direct input. “It’s not often you get to help design an airport from scratch,” former Qantas CEO Alan Joyce 

celebrated

 in 2019. WSI’s then-CEO 

warmly welcomed

 the freight industry: “Tell us what size facility you need, tell us what technology you want in it and how you want it designed to optimise your productivity”. Construction company Lendlease was another big winner, scoring a 

$644 million contract

 for the airport’s earth works.

Careful messaging trumpeted WSI’s economic benefits to a dubious public, while noise and environmental concerns were addressed through non-binding consultation. Naming the airport after Australia’s youngest female pilot, Nancy Bird Walton, and highlighting Indigenous culture and sustainability in its design, represented an attempt to further head off …

title: Muratakan: Lack of concrete steps undermines public trust in the process
content:
Yunus Muratakan, Co-Chair of the Peoples' Equality and Democracy Party (DEM Party) in Diyarbakır (Amed), spoke about the resolution of the Kurdish question and the ongoing peace process, drawing attention to its historical background, legal guarantees, participation in democratic politics and the importance of social reckoning. Muratakan said that the Kurdish question could not be addressed solely through security-oriented policies, emphasizing that a lasting solution would only be possible through the recognition of democratic rights and the establishment of constitutional guarantees.


 


Muratakan discussed the historical development of the Kurdish question, saying that the centralized and uniform approach to governance that emerged with the founding of the Republic restricted the rights of different identities, languages and cultures. He stated that this approach, institutionalized through the 1924 Constitution, paved the way for policies of denial and repression targeting Kurdish identity and cultural rights. Muratakan added that restrictions on democratic expression, organization and political participation contributed to the emergence of the armed conflict.


'A process without a legal framework cannot become permanent'


Muratakan said that the period of armed conflict had imposed heavy human, economic and social costs on Turkey, recalling that tens of thousands of people had lost their lives, villages had been burned and evacuated, and forced displacement and serious human rights violations had occurred.


Muratakan also discussed peace and dialogue initiatives that emerged from the 1990s onwards, noting that the peace process launched in 2013 had received significant public support. He described the work of the Wise Persons Committee, the participation of political parties in discussions and public support as important achievements of the process. Muratakan said that Turkey had entered another period of intense conflict following the collapse of the process in 2015.


Muratakan stressed that past experiences offered important lessons, saying, "A process may begin through political will, but it cannot become permanent without legal guarantees. Any process that lacks a legal framework remains vulnerable to provocations and political interference."


'The process must move towards building positive peace'


Muratakan described the developments following the 27 February call as the beginning of a new era, saying that the declaration of a ceasefire, the decision to dissolve the organization and steps towards disarmament were significant. He also noted that the legal regulation introduced in Parliament represented an important beginning but contained shortcomings in its scope and content.


Muratakan said, "At this point, attention must be drawn to the DDR mechanism used in international conflict resolution experiences. Disarmament, demobilization and reintegration must be addressed as an integrated process. It is crucial to establish legal and institutional arrangements that enable people who have participated in armed struggle to reintegrate into social life and democratic politics. Negative peace means the end of armed conflict. Positive peace, however, requires addressing the structural problems that caused the conflict, guaranteeing rights and freedoms, and establishing a democratic social order. What we need today is a process that does not remain limited to negative peace but also builds positive peace."


Muratakan also criticized the scope of the legal regulation introduced in Parliament, saying that a step, albeit limited, had been taken towards seeking a solution through legal means with an organization that had waged an armed struggle against the government in Turkey's history.


Muratakan drew attention to shortcomings in the regulation's scope, saying, "For the first time in the history of the Republic of Turkey, a very small step has been taken towards recognizing through law an organization that has engaged in armed struggle, an insurgent organization, and resolving the rebellion through legal means. The fact that the law covers only a particular group involved in armed struggle, while excluding intentional homicide and related offenses, as well as people who were investigated before 2005, is a serious shortcoming. This process is also not entirely consistent with the conventional DDR processes implemented around the world."

author: webdev@democracynow.org (Democracy Now!)
title: "We Have to Be Brave": Palestinian Journalist Abed Abu Shehadeh Speaks Out After Israeli Detention
content:
The prominent journalist Abed Abu Shehadeh, a Palestinian citizen of Israel, has been released from Israeli custody after five days in detention. He was arrested on Wednesday by armed police and Shin Bet agents who conducted a nighttime raid on his home in the Israeli city of Jaffa. Abu Shehadeh’s detention was related to his reporting on the October 27 Israeli election and the role of Palestinian political parties. Ahead of the election, he interviewed Azmi Bishara, a Palestinian intellectual and former member of the Israeli Knesset who has lived in exile in Qatar since fleeing Israel amid allegations that he aided Hezbollah during the 2006 Lebanon war. Israeli authorities detained Abu Shehadeh on suspicion of “contacting a foreign agent,” in connection to his interview with Bishara.


“Men with ski masks knock on your door at 11 at night. They tell you that they have an arrest warrant. They raid the house. They wake your wife, your children,” says Shehadeh. “It tells how messianic and dangerous the extreme right in Israel has become, willing to use this unprecedented power against journalists.”
