author: Unknown
title: Kayyım gölgesinde belediye sözleşmeleri: İşçiler nasıl seyirciye çevrildi?
content:
Genel İşler iş kolunda yerel hizmetleri ve belediyeleri kapsayan sözleşmeler sırayla imzalanırken, sözleşmelerin seyrine ve işçiler arasında öne çıkan eğilimlere dair birkaç not düşmenin önümüzdeki tartışmalar açısından önemli olacağını düşünüyoruz. İBB’de peş peşe imzalanan ve zam oranları gerçekte yüzde 20’yi aşmayan sözleşmelerin ardından sırasıyla Ataşehir, Kartal ve Maltepe belediyelerinde de sözleşmeler imzalandı. Sırada Kadıköy sözleşmesi var. Bu notları iki yazıda ele alacağız.

Geçen sözleşme döneminde, başta Kartal Belediyesi dış şantiyesi olmak üzere belediye işçileri imzalanan zam oranlarına karşı lokal iş durdurmalar yapmıştı; ancak bu karşı çıkış yenilgiyle sonuçlanmıştı. Belediye yönetimlerinin baskısına, sendika genel merkezlerinin işçiye sormadan, şubelerin inisiyatifini ellerinden alarak sözleşmeleri üstten imzalamasına dair geçmiş deneyimler eklendi; bu tutumun şubeler üzerinde yarattığı baskı ve şube yönetimlerinin ortak tutum almaktan kaçınması bu sonuçta belirleyici oldu. İşçilerin bu karşı çıkışını ve ortak hareket etmek için gösterdikleri inisiyatifi bir kazanım olarak hanemize yazsak da bu deneyimden olumlu sonuçlar çıkarmaları engellendi. Birçok işçinin dile getirdiği “İş durduruyoruz, kaybeden biz oluyoruz, yevmiyemiz kesiliyor, grev bittikten sonra daha çok çöp topluyoruz” serzenişinin altında biraz da sonuçsuz kalan bu eylemler yattı. Grevlerin ortasında işçinin beklentilerine yanıt vermeden imzalanan sözleşmeler, işçiler arasında “Biz greve çıkıyoruz, 3. gün aniden imzalanıyor, biz niye 3 gün yevmiyemizden oluyoruz?” gibi sözlere zemin hazırladı. İşçilerin bu grev ve iş durdurmalardan neler kazandığına ayrıca bir parantez açmak gerekiyor; ama önce, sürekli yarıda kalan bu mücadelelerin işçileri TİS süreçlerinde izleyici konumuna ittiğini söyleyebiliriz. “Zaten ne kazanacağımızı belirleyemiyoruz, şube ne alabiliyorsa alsın işte” düşüncesi hakim eğilimlerden biri oldu.

İzmir’de belediye işçilerinin hedef gösterilmesiyle örgütlenen linç kampanyası, işçilerin birbirini izleyen eylemleri sayesinde onları kolayca teslim alamadı. Ama bu süreçte işçileri tehdit eden, onları bir gider kalemi olarak gösterip halka şikayet eden, belediyelerde gerçekleştiremedikleri her şeyi işçilerin sırtına yıkan ve belediye işçilerinin ücretlerinin neden açlık sınırının üzerinde olduğunu tartıştıran bir anlayışla, Saray rejiminin sermaye programına bağlanan bir ucuz iş gücü rejimi uygulandı. AKP’nin kayyım saldırısının yarattığı iş güvencesizliği ortamını kendi saldırılarına dayanak yapan belediyeler, beğenmeyene kapıyı göstermekte ve kayyım sopasını işaret etmekte cesaretlendi. Ayrıca kayyım tehlikesinin halkta belediyeleri sahiplenme duygusu yarattığını bilen belediye yönetimleri, mağduru oynayarak işçilerin sözleşmelerini süzgece çevirdi. Bizi takip eden okurlarımız, 2025 sonu ile 2026 başında onlarca belediyede aynı anda ücretlerin geciktirildiğini, maaş ve mesailerin ödenmediğini, işçilere ne zaman ödeneceğine dair bir açıklama bile yapılmadığını hatırlayacaktır. Ödemeler yapıldığında ise işçilerin deyimiyle para “pul” olmuştu: Geriye dönük alacaklar, ödenmesi gereken tarihten neredeyse 8-9 ay sonra taksitlerle ödendi ve enflasyon marifetiyle eritildi. Henüz kayyım gelmemiş ama “Kayyım yönetse böyle yönetirdi” dediğimiz belediyeler bir yandan sosyal belediyecilik rüzgarları estirdi, öte yandan en çarpıcı örneği İzmir’de görüldüğü gibi on binlerce işçinin ekmeğiyle oynadı, işçileri havuz sisteminde boğmaya kalktı. İşte işçiler, sözleşmelerindeki ücretlerin bile ödenmediği bu koşullarda yeni TİS’ten daha az umutlu hale geldi.

Bu umutsuzluğun bir ayağı da sendikacılar. Belediye işçileri, geçmiş sözleşme dönemlerinde Hizmet-İş, Belediye-İş ve Genel-İş’ten bekledikleri desteği ve önderliği göremedi. Yine lokal diyebileceğimiz bazı belediyelerde Genel-İş’e bağlı kimi şubeler ya da şubelerden bağımsız tutum alan bazı temsilciler ve işçi grupları bu eylemlere önderlik etmeye, en azından önlerini kesmemeye çalıştı. Ama genel olarak “Sendikamız bizim arkamızda durmaz” eğiliminin son 3 sözleşme döneminde (6 yıl) güçlendiği, işçilerin üzerinde uzlaştığı bir tespittir.

Bilindiği gibi AKP’li belediyeler hem ücret politikasında hem de sosyal haklarda CHP’li ve Yeni Partili belediyelerin gerisinde. İşçilerin örgütlenmemesi için de her yolu deniyorlar. Ancak aynı tutum, başka söylemlerle CHP’li, şimdilerde Yeni Partili belediyelerde de var; üstelik buralarda işçiler daha örgütlü olduğu için daha hızlı açığa çıkıyor …

author: Unknown
title: Gastronominin vitrini şeflik, mutfağın gerçeği bol kepçe sömürü
content:
Televizyon programları, MasterChef gibi yarışmalar ve sosyal medyanın büyüttüğü Michelin yıldızlı şeflik hayali gençleri gastronomi eğitiminin olduğu bölümlere yöneltirken, mutfakların arkasında taşeronlaşma, düşük ücret, meslek hastalıkları, iş kazaları, yetersiz beslenme ve güvencesizlik büyüyor.

Gastronomi bölümlerinde şeflik hayali kuran, yarışmalarda şampiyon olup restoran açmayı hedefleyen gençlerin bulunduğu sektörün diğer tarafında ise binlerce kişilik yemek üretimini düşük ücret, uzun çalışma saatleri ve ağır koşullar altında gerçekleştiren mutfak işçileri bulunuyor. Gastronomi dünyasında restoranlara müşteri ve gelir sağlayan ödüllerin arkasındaki mutfakta görünmeyen emeği aşçılarla ve sektörde örgütlü sendika başkanları ile konuştuk.

DİSK/Gıda-İş Genel Başkanı Olcay Ozak, gastronomiye yönelik ilginin televizyon, internet ve sosyal medyanın etkisiyle büyüdüğünü belirterek, gençlerin kendilerini başarılı birer şef olarak yetiştirme hayaliyle bu bölümlere yöneldiğini söyledi. Michelin yıldızı gibi derecelendirmelerin restoranlara müşteri ve gelir sağladığını, ancak bu değeri yaratan mutfak çalışanlarına aynı ölçüde yansımadığını ifade eden Ozak, “Bunların arkasındaki şefler, aşçıbaşılar emeğin asıl sahibidir ama ödül restoran sahibine gider” dedi. “Gastronomi okuyan öğrencilerin çoğu staj adı altında aslında müthiş bir sömürü çarkının içerisine itiliyorlar” diyen Ozak, stajyerlerin denetim ve koruma mekanizmalarından yoksun bırakılmasının sorunları ağırlaştırdığını dile getirdi. Gençlerin ücret ve çalışma süresiyle, mobbing ve tacizle karşı karşıya kaldığını aktardı. TBMM lokantasında stajyer olarak çalışan kız çocuklarının Meclis personeli tarafından taciz edildiği ortaya çıkmış, haklarında 16 yıl 6 aya kadar hapis cezası istenen 4’ü tutuklu 5 sanığın davasında mahkeme, tutuklu sanıkların tahliyelerine karar vermişti.

2026 verilerine göre gastronomi ve mutfak sanatları bölümlerinin taban puanları yükseldi. Özyeğin Üniversitesi İngilizce burslu programı 460.30 puan ve 1178 başarı sırasıyla ilk sırada yer aldı. Devlet üniversitelerinde ise Akdeniz Üniversitesi 403.18, (10 bin 885 başarı sırası), Anadolu Üniversitesi 393.77 (15 bin 613 başarı sırası), Eskişehir Osmangazi Üniversitesi 381.53 (24 bin 225 başarı sırası) puanla öğrenci kabul etti.

Kendisi de aşçı olarak çalışan DİSK’e bağlı Dev Turizm-İş Genel Başkanı Turgay Özdemir, “Tamamen insan bedeni ve insan emeğiyle üretilen, insan emeğinin artı değere çevrildiği bir iş kolu bizim iş kolumuz. Çok uzun çalışma saatlerinin, yorucu ve atmosferik ortamın sıcaklığın, çalışma koşulları ve mevcut çalışma yerlerinin iyileştirilmemesiyle ilgili ciddi bir problem var. O şaşaalı, büyük otellerin görünmeyen alanlardaki dinlenme alanları ya yok ya da aynı standartta değil. Aşçıların mola yapabileceği, çay içebileceği bir alan yok çoğu işletmede, işçi sağlığı öncelenmiyor” dedi.

Catering sektöründe çalışan Aşçı Başaran benzer bir tabloyu yemek üretiminin yoğunluğu üzerinden anlattı. Catering mutfaklarını “inşaat şantiyesi”ne benzeten Başaran “Burada inşaat işçisi gibisin, öyle bir tabak iki tabak ya da on kişilik, yirmi kişilik yapmıyorsun; burada yaptığın zaman en düşük yaptığın yer 2 bin kişilik, 3 bin kişilik” dedi. Mutfak işçisinin işinin yemek pişirmekle sınırlı kalmadığını, taşıma, indirme, kaldırma ve yükleme gibi işlerin de aşçılara yaptırıldığını anlatan Başaran, mutfaklarda çalışanların kendilerine ayrılmış bir dinlenme alanı dahi olmadığını dile getirdi: “Koridorda bir yer bulursa ya da beş-on dakika dışarı çıkıp hava alabilirse dinleniyor. Başka türlü yok.”

Binlerce kişiye yemek üreten mutfaklarda yoğunluk, işçinin yalnızca iş yerinde geçirdiği süreyi değil, işe ulaşım için harcadığı zamanı da artırıyor. Evden çıkıp eve dönene kadar geçen sürenin 16 saate ulaşabildiğini belirten bir diğer aşçı, “Sabah 5.20’de servise bindim, 5 çeyrek gibi evden çıktım, işe saat 07.00’de başlıyorum, 15.00’te iş bitiyor, fazla mesai başlıyor ve düşünmeye başlıyorum şu an geri eve ne zaman döneceğim. Akşam 9’da evde oluyorum. Çoğu zaman uykudan uykuya gidiyorum eve” dedi.

Yemeğin zamanında yetiştirilmesi, beğenilmesi ve belirlenen maliyet içerisinde hazırlanması da çalışanların üzerindeki baskıyı artırıyor. Başaran, “En ucuz malzemeyle en iyi yemeği çıkarmamızı istiyorlar” diye anlatıyor bu durumu.

Catering sektöründe çalışan bir başka aşçı ise personel için hazırlanan yemeklerin çoğu zaman üretimde kullanılan ürünlerden farklı olduğunu, protein yerine karbonhidrat …

title: ABD’de tsunami, bölgede temkinli bekleyiş
content:
Arap basını ABD ara seçimlerinde ABD Başkanı Donald Trump ve Cumhuriyetçilerin yaşadığı ağır yenilgiyi “mavi tsunami” olarak gördü. Trump’ın ve Cumhuriyetçilerin yaşadığı bu yenilgi, İran savaşının ve İsrail’e verilen sınırsız desteğin bedeli olarak değerlendirildi. Trump’ın dış politikada geniş yetkilerini koruduğuna işaret edilen analizlerde, Demokratların Senatoda ve Temsilciler Meclisinde sağladıkları çoğunlukla Trump’ın yasama alanındaki hedeflerinin ve önerdiği bütçelerin önüne kalın bir set çekebileceklerine dikkat çekildi. Ancak ABD’nin dış politikasında köklü bir değişikliğin olacağına kimse ihtimal vermiyor.

Öte yandan, Middle East Online’da Semir Adel imzasıyla yayımlanan makalede, Trump ve Trumpçılığın yenilgisinin izlenen ekonomik ve toplumsal politikaların bir sonucu olduğu vurgulanıyor. Iraklı Yazar ve Siyasetçi Adel, bu yenilgiyi aynı zamanda Avrupa ve ABD’de işçi sınıfının öncülük ettiği insancıl ve ilerici toplumsal hareketlerin sanılandan çok daha güçlü olduğunun bir göstergesi olarak değerlendiriyor. Adel, “Trump ve Trumpçılığın yenilgisi; yaşam, sağlık ve eğitim koşullarının iyileştirilmesini talep eden, Filistin halkıyla dayanışmayı ve kadın haklarını savunan, ırkçılığa ve düşünce ve ifade özgürlüğüne yönelik baskılara karşı çıkan gösteri ve protestoların bir kazanımıdır” ifadelerini kullanıyor.

3 Kasım’da yapılan seçimlerin ortaya çıkardığı sonuç, Trump’ı tamamen yeni ve farklı bir denklemle karşı karşıya bıraktı. Kongreyi kaybetti ancak silahlı kuvvetlerin başkomutanı sıfatıyla sahip olduğu yetkileri koruyor. Anayasal açıdan hâlâ Kongrenin iznini beklemeden askeri saldırı emri verebilir. Ayrıca hareket alanını kısıtlayan herhangi bir yasayı veto etme yetkisine de sahip. Buna karşılık, yeni bir savaş artık siyasi destekten ve güvence altına alınmış finansmandan yoksun olacak. Üstelik Trump, denetim yetkilerini kullanabilecek ve 60 günlük yetkilendirme süresi olmaksızın yürütülen askeri operasyonları sınırlandıran Savaş Yetkileri Yasası’nı devreye sokabilecek muhalif bir Kongrenin baskısı altında kalacak. Bütün bu araçlar, yeni Kongre ile birlikte Trump yönetiminin İran savaşını yürütmesinin önünde bir baskı ve engelleme mekanizmasına dönüşebilir.

Ancak ABD dış politikasının, iç politikadaki parti rekabetinden büyük ölçüde bağımsız bir süreklilik taşıdığını da unutmamak gerekir. Demokratlar ve Cumhuriyetçiler iç politikada farklı programları savunsalar da özellikle İsrail ve Ortadoğu politikası söz konusu olduğunda aralarındaki görüş ayrılıkları büyük ölçüde ortadan kalkabiliyor. İsrail’in Gazze’ye yönelik katliamlarına Demokratlar döneminde başladığını ve Başkan Biden’ın İsrail’e her türlü desteği sağladığını hatırlayalım. Trump Biden’ın bıraktığı yerden İsrail’e destek olmaya devam etti. Dolayısıyla Trump’ın bir çılgınlık yapıp İran’a yönelik kapsamlı bir saldırı başlatması halinde Demokratların ne yapacağını bugünden kestirmek zor.

Arap basınında, İran’ın Trump’ın seçim yenilgisine duyulan memnuniyete işaret ediliyor. Nitekim İran Meclis Başkanı Muhammed Bakır Kalibaf, “ABD seçmeni savaşa hayır dedi ve biz bunu destekliyoruz” açıklamasında bulundu. Ancak Tahran, seçim sonuçlarının ABD’nin yeni bir saldırı düzenleme ihtimalini ortadan kaldırdığı kanaatinde değil. Bu nedenle İranlı yetkililer, olası bir ABD saldırısına karşı her cephede hazır olduklarını vurgularken, aynı zamanda müzakereye açık oldukları mesajını veriyor. Dini Lider Mücteba Hamaney de ABD’de iktidardaki partinin değişmesinin Washington’ın İran’a yönelik tutumunu değiştirmeyeceğini belirtiyor. Arap basınındaki değerlendirmelerde, İran’ın şu ana kadar geri adım atmadığı, yaptırımların kaldırılması, deniz ablukasının sona erdirilmesi, dondurulmuş fonlarının serbest bırakılması ve Hürmüz Boğazı üzerindeki kontrolünün kabul edilmesi koşulları karşılığında anlaşmaya hazır olduğu da aktarılıyor.

Ara seçimlerde alınan ağır yenilginin Trump’ı siyasi açıdan “topal ördek” konumuna düşürmesinin ardından, İran savaşının, ortaya çıkan yeni siyasi dengelerin ilk ve en önemli sınavı olacağına dikkat çekiliyor. Cumhuriyetçi Parti içinde bu konuda, Başkan Yardımcısı JD Vance ile Dışişleri Bakanı Marco Rubio’nun öncülük ettiği iki farklı yaklaşımın bulunduğu belirtiliyor. Her iki ismin de 2028 başkanlık seçimlerinde Cumhuriyetçilerin adayı olabilmek için şimdiden siyasi pozisyon almaya hazırlandığına işaret ediliyor.

title: More Pressure Needed to STOP the Trump EGO Arch
content:
By U.S. Army Colonel (Ret) Ann Wright, World BEYOND War, November 8, 2026


Despite

9.5 hours of citizen testimony from 131 persons

Over 100,000 written comments opposing the Arch have been sent to the NCPC. The plan to build it was rushed and skirted legal procedures and funding requirements under Title 40 U.S.C. § 8106.


Immediately after the vote that took place after 10pm on November 5, 2026, the Trump administration filed a notification with the federal court that construction would begin immediately.


That notification was followed within minutes by a

33-page injunction

Judge Chutkan wrote, “[T]he District and Virginia have offered enough proof ‘indicating that the harm is certain to occur in the near future’ to show irreparable harm.” She also wrote that “the most straightforward of Congress’s planning directives,” remains in force today. Now codified at 40 U.S.C. § 8106, the statute provides in full: “A building or structure shall not be erected on any reservation, park, or public grounds of the Federal Government in the District of Columbia without express authority of Congress.”

author: By Sean Summers, Unicorn Riot
title: Twin Cities Demand Justice For Kohen Wiley Killing
content:
St. Paul, MN – When one-year-old Kohen Wiley was shot by police in Mississippi this summer, residents in the Twin Cities felt the pain of a life lost to police violence. In late October, when the body-worn camera footage of the shooting was released and the officer’s use of force ruled justified, they knew they needed to respond.


So on Oct. 25, local Black women, many of whom have experienced losing a loved one to police violence themselves, rallied residents to show up and march in hopes of raising awareness and demanding accountability for the one-year-old infant shot by police in June.


The march was spurred by the Mississippi Attorney General ruling that the officer who fired the shots that killed Wiley and struck another woman in the car, was justified in using deadly force. Protests have taken place across the country, including last month’s march in St. Paul.


On October 25, a crowd gathered in front of the Governor’s mansion where speakers addressed attendees. Though Wiley was killed in Mississippi, organizers saw a direct connection to his killing and the many police shootings that have burdened their community.


“When a murder happens to any one of us, it happens to all of us,” Toshira Garraway Allen, founder of

Families Supporting Families Against Police Violence

, told the crowd.


Garraway, whose work centers around supporting families who have lost loved ones at the hands of the police, drove that point home. The burden, she said, of demanding justice and picking up the pieces after police kill or jail a loved one falls largely on the shoulders of the Black women who raised and cared for the victims.


“It’s Black women that are standing up and fighting these injustices,” Garraway said.


The Oct. 25 march embodied that. After listening to several Black women speak about their experiences of losing family members and seeking justice in the aftermath, the crowd marched in the street to the Center for Black Empowerment and rallied to demand justice for Wiley.


On June 18, police in Senatobia, Mississippi responded to a report of shoplifting at a local Walmart. Among the responding officers was Sergeant Hunter Foster.


Body-worn camera footage from that day shows a group of police gathered in an office at the Walmart talking with an employee. After seeing people on a surveillance camera leaving the store’s front doors, the police rushed out of the office and pursued the Wiley family across the parking lot.


Moments later, police confronted the family in their car. After the driver backed up into another car, they pulled forward toward the police. That’s when Foster fired through the car’s window, hitting and killing one-year-old infant Kohen Wiley.


Foster and the city’s interim police chief have both resigned following the shooting.


After the state investigated the shooting, Mississippi Attorney General Lynn Fitch stated the use of force that resulted in Wiley’s killing was justified as the car had been driven toward officers.


But critics point out that Hunter shot through the passenger window of the sedan, refuting the claim that he was at risk of being hit by the car.

author: Unknown
title: Kurdish political prisoner in Iran denied urgent treatment
content:
The Tehran Prosecutor’s Office continues to block Kurdish political prisoner Motalleb Ahmadian’s transfer outside Evin Prison for urgent medical treatment, despite repeated medical warnings over his deteriorating health and serious complications from a cancerous tumour.


Ahmadian, from Baneh, Kurdistan Province, is in his 17th year of imprisonment and suffers from multiple illnesses.


An informed source told the Kurdistan Human Rights Network (KHRN): “The Legal Medicine Organisation has repeatedly informed the judge overseeing the prison and the Tehran Prosecutor’s Office that, given the deterioration in Motalleb Ahmadian’s health, he must be transferred outside prison as soon as possible so that he can receive treatment for his multiple illnesses, undergo the necessary medical procedures and recover in suitable conditions.”


The source said the prosecutor’s office had nevertheless refused to approve the transfer, heightening concerns about irreversible harm to Ahmadian’s health and the risk to his life.


Ahmadian has undergone several operations to treat complications caused by the cancerous tumour. During these procedures, his gallbladder was completely emptied, and surgeons also operated on parts of his liver and intestines, the source said.


Repeated operations and damage to his digestive system have severely limited the options for further surgery and increased the risks, including the possible loss of bowel control.


The surgery he currently needs is intended to treat complications caused by the tumour and is not directly related to the main tumour operation, said the source, adding that it required urgent medical attention.


In previous years, Ahmadian’s hospital transfers have repeatedly been cancelled, including at least three scheduled transfers. He has also been denied adequate access to medication and specialist care.


The source expressed concern that his history of multiple operations, damage to internal organs, limited surgical options and urgent treatment needs, combined with the prosecutor’s continued refusal to approve his transfer, placed his health and life at increasing risk.


Sources following his case warned that continued denial of timely treatment could lead to his gradual death.


Ahmadian went on hunger strike on 5 May 2025 to protest the Tehran prosecutor’s refusal to suspend his sentence and the denial of medical treatment.


His continued denial of access to specialised medical care has caused him to lose more than 35 kg, leaving him in a critical and alarming condition.


Ahmadian has long highlighted the impact of medical neglect on his deteriorating health. In a letter written in January 2020, he described his worsening health condition, attributing it to the denial of timely medical care. He noted infections in the testicular region and fractures in three vertebrae caused by torture during detention.


He wrote: “Unfortunately, the prison authorities refused to cover the costs of my surgeries and medications. According to the Prisons Organisation’s regulations, these expenses should be borne by the prison, but I had to pay all costs myself. Due to financial constraints, I stopped seeking further treatment.”


Ahmadian was born in Baneh in 1983 and arrested on 5 October 2010.


After eight months in security detention facilities in Sardasht, Saqqez and Sanandaj, where he says he was held in harsh solitary confinement and subjected to severe physical torture, he was sentenced to 30 years in prison and exile to Minab Prison on charges of “enmity against God” (moharebeh).


Over more than 16 years in custody, Ahmadian has been held in prisons in Saqqez and Sanandaj, Rajaei Shahr Prison in Karaj, Evin Prison and Greater Tehran Central Penitentiary. He is currently held in Evin Prison.

author: Unknown
title: Four Kurdish citizens remain detained in Iran, whereabouts unknown
content:
Four Kurdish citizens arrested by security forces in Bukan, Miandoab and Piranshahr in West Azerbaijan Province between 2 and 4 November remain detained with their exact whereabouts and condition unknown.


The detainees – Diyar Abroun, Jamileh (Mina) Mohammadamin-Azar, Saadi Karimi, and Mahmoud Pileh – have been denied access to legal counsel and family visits since their arrests.


The Kurdistan Human Rights Network (KHRN) has learned that security forces violently arrested Abroun, from Piranshahr, on 2 November.


On 3 November, Ministry of Intelligence forces raided Mohammadamin-Azar’s family home in Bukan and arrested her and her husband, Khoshnaw Azizpour, without a warrant.


Azizpour was released after several hours of interrogation, while Mohammadamin-Azar was reportedly transferred to a security detention facility in Orumiyeh, the provincial capital, with her exact place of detention remaining unknown.


Security forces also arrested Karimi, another citizen from Bukan, on the same day.


On 4 November, security forces arrested Pileh, from the village of Gug Jalu in Miandoab County.

title: Eğitim Sen Bolu'dan öğretmen görevlendirmelerine tepki: Hatalı atamalar gözden geçirilsin
content:
Eğitim Sen Bolu Şubesi, norm kadro fazlası öğretmenlere yönelik resen atama kararlarına ve il genelindeki hatalı görevlendirmelere tepki gösterdi. Öğretmenlerin kendi branşları dışında görevlendirilmesine, rehber öğretmenlerin ikinci okullarda çalıştırılmasına ve sınıfların birleştirilmesine dikkat çeken sendika, Millî Eğitim Bakanlığına uygulamaları gözden geçirme çağrısı yaptı.

Eğitim Sen Bolu Şubesi, il genelinde norm kadro fazlası öğretmenlere yönelik uygulamalar ve öğretmen görevlendirmelerinde yaşanan sorunlara ilişkin açıklama yaptı. Şube Yürütme Kurulu adına açıklamayı yapan Şube Başkanı Dilek Çakman, Millî Eğitim Bakanlığını (MEB) resen atama kararlarını ve hatalı görevlendirmeleri gözden geçirmeye çağırdı.

Açıklamada, norm kadro uygulamaları, plansız atamalar ve okul dönüşümlerinin öğretmenler ile öğrencileri mağdur ettiği belirtildi. Okulların birleştirilmesi ve kapatılması sonucunda çok sayıda öğretmenin görev yaptığı okulda norm kadro fazlası durumuna düşürüldüğünü ifade eden Çakman, ders çizelgelerindeki değişikliklerin, okul dönüşümlerinin ve istihdam politikalarının sonuçlarının öğretmenlere yüklenmesine tepki gösterdi.

Açıklamada, şubelerin birleştirilmesiyle sınıf mevcutlarının arttığına, ikili eğitimin yaygınlaştığına ve öğretmen değişikliklerinin eğitimde sürekliliği olumsuz etkilediğine dikkat çekildi.

Sınıflara ilişkin kararların yalnızca öğrenci sayısı ve bina kapasitesi dikkate alınarak değil, öğrencilerin öğrenme ihtiyaçları ve pedagojik koşullar gözetilerek alınması gerektiği vurgulandı. Eğitimde verimliliğin sınıf mevcutlarının azaltılması ve her öğrencinin eşit, kamusal ve nitelikli eğitime erişiminin sağlanmasıyla mümkün olabileceği belirtildi.

MEB'in 19 Ağustos 2026 tarihli 2026/70 sayılı Genelgesi kapsamında norm kadro fazlası öğretmenlerin belirli bir takvime bağlı kalmaksızın ihtiyaç bulunan okullara atanmasının öngörüldüğünü hatırlatan Eğitim Sen Bolu Şubesi, uygulamanın öğretmenler açısından belirsizliği artırdığını savundu.

Öğretmenlerin eğitim aldıkları branşlar dışında görevlendirilmesine de tepki gösteren sendika, öğretmen açığının kadrolu atamalarla giderilmesi gerektiğini ifade etti.

Çakman, Bolu genelinde norm kadro fazlası öğretmenlere yönelik hatalı görevlendirmeler yapıldığını belirtti. Açıklamada, öğretmenlerin kendi alanları dışında görevlendirilmesi, rehber öğretmenlerin ilgili genelgeye aykırı biçimde ikinci okullarda görevlendirilmesi ve destek eğitiminde öğretmen görevlendirmelerine ilişkin ortak bir standardın bulunmaması eleştirildi.

İl Millî Eğitim Müdürlüğünün ilgili birimleriyle yapılan görüşmelere rağmen sorunların çözümü için somut bir adım atılmadığını savunan sendika, öğrencilerin üstün yararını gözeten kesintisiz ve nitelikli bir eğitim için öğretmenlerin güvenli ve istikrarlı çalışma koşullarına sahip olması gerektiğini kaydetti.

Açıklamanın sonunda norm kadro fazlası sorununun sorumlusunun öğretmenler olmadığı vurgulandı. Eğitim Sen Bolu Şubesi, resen atama kararlarının ve hatalı görevlendirmelerin derhâl gözden geçirilmesini, norm kadro planlamasının okulların gerçek ihtiyaçları ve öğrencilerin üstün yararı doğrultusunda yapılmasını istedi.

Eğitim politikalarının kamusal, bilimsel ve pedagojik ilkeler doğrultusunda yürütülmesi gerektiğini belirten sendika, norm kadro fazlası ilan edilerek görev yerleri değiştirilen öğretmenlerle dayanışmayı sürdüreceğini ve yaşanan mağduriyetler giderilene kadar mücadele edeceğini duyurdu.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

Hunderte von Lieferfahrern protestieren in der Innenstadt und fordern von den Unternehmen Würde und faire Bezahlung


„

Uber Canada erklärte, dass das Unternehmen für Lohntransparenz sorge und die Mindestlohnstandards der Provinzen einhalte


Hunderte von Lieferfahrern versammelten sich am Montag bei einer Protestkundgebung in der Innenstadt von Toronto, um von ihren Arbeitgebern faire Bezahlung, sichere Arbeitsbedingungen und Würde am Arbeitsplatz zu fordern.


Eine neu gegründete Gruppe namens „Delivery Drivers United“ organisierte die Protestkundgebung auf dem Nathan Phillips Square. Die Gruppe besteht aus mehr als 900 Beschäftigten, die für Plattformen wie Uber Eats, Skip und DoorDash arbeiten.


Ameer Ali, der unter anderem als Lieferfahrer für Uber Eats und DoorDash tätig ist, sagte, es sei schwierig, mit dem Ausliefern von Essen seinen Lebensunterhalt zu bestreiten. Die Arbeit sei mit langen Arbeitszeiten, viel Verkehr und unsicheren Bedingungen verbunden, erklärte er. „Wir arbeiten rund um die Uhr. Wir setzen unser Leben auf den Straßen aufs Spiel … Wir riskieren unser Leben, um den Kunden etwas Gutes zu liefern“, sagte Ali. „Ich habe eine Bestellung im Wert von 3 Dollar ausgeliefert, die über eine Strecke von sechs Kilometern ging, und dafür habe ich 45 Minuten gebraucht“, sagte Ali.


Nachdem sie den Rednern zugehört hatten, machten sich die Fahrer auf den Weg zur Zentrale von Uber Canada an der Ecke Bloor Street und Church Street, um dort einen Brief mit ihren Forderungen zu übergeben. Die Gruppe berichtete, dass die Fahrer zwar das Gebäude betreten durften, ihnen jedoch der Zugang zur Hauptverwaltung verwehrt wurde. Sie übergaben ihren Forderungsbrief dem Sicherheitspersonal von Uber. In dem Brief erklärten die Fahrer, dass ihrer Organisation Hunderte von Uber-Eats-Mitarbeitern angehören.


Der Brief fordert einen existenzsichernden Lohn, ein faires und transparentes Verfahren zur Berechnung des Grundtarifs vor Trinkgeldern sowie eine Erläuterung, wie unerwartete Wartezeiten im Grundlohn berücksichtigt werden. Außerdem werden ein erweiterter Krankenversicherungsschutz, auch bei Arbeitsunfällen, sowie garantierter Zugang zu Toiletten und Wartebereichen in Restaurants gefordert

…“ engl.

title: EMEP Bursa Kongresi'nde birleşik mücadele çağrısı: Genel eylem, genel halk direnişi
content:
Emek Partisi Bursa İl Örgütü 11. Olağan Kongresi’nde konuşan EMEP Genel Başkan Yardımcısı İstanbul Milletvekili İskender Bayhan’ın katılımıyla gerçekleştirildi.

Emek Partisi (EMEP) Bursa İl Örgütü 11. Olağan Kongresi, Merinos Atatürk Kongre Kültür Merkezi’nde gerçekleştirildi. Kongreye EMEP Genel Başkan Yardımcısı İstanbul Milletvekili İskender Bayhan’ın yanı sıra siyasi parti ve sendika temsilcileri katıldı. Kongreye Taymes Tekstil’de patron şiddetine maruz kalan kadın işçi ve Korteks fabrikasında TEKSİF’in satış sözleşmesine karşı çıktıkları için işten atılan tekstil işçileri katılarak bir konuşma yaptı.

Kongreye ayrıca metal, gıda, tekstil iş kolları olmak üzere farklı sektörde çalışan işçiler de katıldı.

Kongrede konuşan EMEP Genel Başkan Yardımcısı İstanbul Milletvekili İskender Bayhan, dünyada yaşanan son gelişmelere değinerek, “Bütün dünyada egemen olan sermaye düzeni ne yazık ki bütün dünya halklarını yeni ve daha büyük savaşlara sürükleyecek olan iktisadi ve politik programlar uyguluyorlar. Bütün dünyada savaş ve sömürü politikası büyüdükçe halkların mücadelesi de büyüyor” dedi.

Sarayda oturan bir avuç sermayedar ve oligarşinin temsilcileri, var olan savaş politikalarının içinde aktif olarak yer alıp buradan pay almalıyız yaklaşımında olduğunu söyleyen Bayhan, “Bölge politikaları bize savaşsız bir bölge değil, savaşın bölgede yayılması ve oradan pay kapmaya dönük. Mekke anlaşması da bu zincirin bir halkasıdır. Onların gözünde bu ülkenin işçilerinin, emekçilerinin mutlak yoksullaşması, gençlerin geleceğinin olmaması önemli değil. Onlar için tek önemli olan bu coğrafyada yeniden paylaşımdan güçlü bir pozisyon alıp yüksek kârlarla, rantlarla bu yeniden paylaşımdan çıkmak.”

Fedakarlık yapın, dişinizi sıkın diyenler oturdukları yerden milyarları götürüyor diyen Bayhan, “Partimizin yeni anayasa konusundaki tutumu açıktır. Bu parlamentonun ve Cumhur İttifakı'nın bu ülkenin halkının, emekçilerinin çıkarına demokratik bir anayasa yazma ihtimali bir toplu iğnenin ucu kadar yoktur. Böyle bir niyeti de yoktur. Bunu her vesileyle dile getiriyoruz. Seçimler konusuna gelince ise partimizin tutumu açık. Geçmişte saray oligarşisinin son bulması için biz iki seçim üst üste burjuva muhalefetini eleştirmemize, düzen içi muhalefet dememize rağmen destekledik. Önümüzdeki dönem ortak mücadelenin, birleşik mücadelenin temel hedefi bir genel eylem, genel halk direnişi hattı olmalıdır. Seçimlerde bunun parçası olmalıdır. Bu yolu ortak yürüme noktasında hiçbir tereddüdümüz yoktur. Bunun olmamasının sorumlusu kimse de hesap vermeli” dedi.

Kongrede söz alan KESK Bursa Dönem Sözcüsü Eğitim Sen Şube Başkanı Derviş Erdem, “Hem siyasal hem de sendikal mücadeleyi yürütme noktasında zor bir dönemdeyiz. Adalete kimse inanmıyor. Siz kimi seçerseniz seçin, ben istediğimle yol yürüyeceğim diyen bir iktidar var. Doğa her gün talan ediliyor. Eğitimde parası olmayan nitelikli bir eğitim alamaz duruma geldi. Sağlıkta durum aynı. Bizden toplanan 100 liralık vergiden 20 lirası faize gidiyor, yüzde 17’si silahlanmaya ve yüzde 5’i de asla bizim kadar vergi vermeyen, devletten ballı ihaleler alan ve vergi borçları silinen o büyük şirketlere teşvik olarak veriliyor. Siyasi iktidar tercihini asla işçiden emekçiden yana kullanmıyor” dedi.

AKP’nin iktidara geldiği günden bugüne mücadeleci örgütleri ele geçirdiğini söyleyen Birleşik Metal Bursa Şube Başkanı Gökhan Aydın, “İşçilerin mücadeleleri iktidarın desteği ile sarı sendikalar tarafından bastırıldı. Bugün bütçe görüşmeleri var ve asgari ücretin düşük kalması için çalışmalar yapılırken vergi dilimleriyle soyuluyoruz. DİSK’e bağlı 11 sendika 29 Kasım'da İstanbul’da bir miting gerçekleştireceğiz. author: Julius Gavroche
title: Giorgio Agamben: Political elections or opinion polls?
content:
Auguste Couder,

Le Serment du Jeu de Paume, 20 juin 1789

. 1848


The fact that what we continue to call democracy has lost its meaning is demonstrated by the indiscriminate use of opinion polls, which lay bare the already obvious fact that elections are merely a survey of public opinion rather than an expression of political will. Opinion polls, by showing day by day—through fluctuations in respondents’ views—the numerical standing of the parties, carry out a sort of continuous election, which nobody controls and which can therefore, as indeed happens, be manipulated to in turn influence the very opinion it is supposed to reflect. We call democracy a government of public opinion; that is to say, of something politically entirely insubstantial, which has no reality other than the polls, which, at the very moment they appear to record it, create, alter and manipulate it incessantly. The process by which Rousseau’s

volonté générale

 [general will]—which cannot be quantified—has gradually been transformed into public opinion, which is merely a matter of numbers, defines the fate of Western democracies.

title: Yıldız Çakar’s poetry wins international award in the US
content:
The poem “Mohra Reş” (The Dark Seal) by Kurdish poet and novelist Yıldız Çakar has won the Special International Honorable Mention at the Julia Vive Feminist Poetry Festival, held in Philadelphia, USA. The award, presented in the category of “Poetry, Memory and Resistance,” recognizes Çakar’s distinctive literary treatment of women’s struggle, collective memory and resistance.


Organized by the Madre Tierra Women’s Center (CIMMT), the Julia Vive Feminist Poetry Festival will take place on November 13 at the Taller Puertorriqueño Cultural Center in Philadelphia. Bringing together 100 poets from different parts of the world, the festival selected Yıldız Çakar’s poem “Mohra Reş” (The Dark Seal) for the Special International Honorable Mention in the “Poetry, Memory and Resistance” category.


The award committee informed Yıldız Çakar of its decision in a special letter. Highlighting the poet’s literary strength, the letter noted that she explores themes including violence against women, femicide, collective memory, land, loss and women’s resistance through a distinctive Kurdish perspective.


The letter also emphasized that Çakar’s poem expands the festival’s literary horizons beyond Latin America and the Caribbean, giving it a global dimension. It highlighted the work’s powerful connection to women’s struggles for freedom and dignity.


As one of the festival’s participants living outside the United States, Yıldız Çakar will have her poem presented to audiences through a video recording during the official award ceremony.


10 books published


Yıldız Çakar, who has worked in journalism and literature for many years, has published 10 books across the genres of poetry, fiction and research. Her first poetry collection, “Goristana Stêrkan,” was published in 2004.


Her book “Mohra Reş,” which contains the poem selected for the award, was published in 2024. The collection’s central poem was later adapted into a digital theatre project titled “Lockedown Locked In.” The project won the Best Original Screenplay award at the Athens International Art Films Festival.


In her work, Yıldız Çakar focuses primarily on themes of death, exile, identity and oppression. Rather than relying on conventional poetic forms, her style draws on profound expression and the oral memory of Kurdish history.


Yıldız Çakar, who migrated to Germany in 2018 and has lived in Berlin for the past eight years, was detained at Istanbul Airport in May of this year while traveling to Turkey. She was released after being questioned.

content:
Members of Koma Berxwedan and other artists issued a statement to draw attention to the situation of Kurdish artist Nûdem Durak, who has been in prison for 11.5 years and is reportedly battling serious illnesses.


Reacting to the 19-year-and-6-month prison sentence handed down to Nûdem Durak, the artists said that her health had deteriorated and that her life was in danger. They called for the release of all sick prisoners, particularly Nûdem Durak.


Criticising the continued imprisonment of sick prisoners at a time when the Peace and Democratic Society Process is being discussed, the artists called on human rights organisations, intellectuals, politicians and the public to intensify their efforts and raise their voices.


 


Freedom of ill prisoners must be our top priority


Speaking on behalf of Koma Berxwedan, Hekim Sefkan said that, at a time when hopes for peace were growing, decisions continued to be made that contradicted human rights and the spirit of the process. Reacting to the prison sentence imposed on Nûdem Durak, Sefkan said it was unacceptable that the artist was being kept behind bars despite her serious health problems.


Sefkan said: “At a time when hopes for peace are growing, decisions and actions that contradict human rights and the spirit of the process are also continuing. One such decision is the 19.5-year prison sentence imposed on artist Nûdem Durak. She has been in prison for 11.5 years. She is ill. Keeping her in prison for another 19.5 years at such a time goes against both the spirit of the process and human rights.


We call on all intellectuals, artists, human rights defenders and our people to raise their voices against this injustice. We want people to take a stand against this unlawful treatment, to speak out for all sick prisoners, and to make this our number one priority. All ill prisoners, beginning with our artist Nûdem Durak, must be released as soon as possible so that they can continue their treatment in humane conditions. On this issue, we call on everyone, particularly human rights organisations, to increase pressure on the state institutions responsible for these decisions. All relevant institutions must intensify their struggle against these decisions, which disregard human rights.”


The peace process is, above all, a test of sincerity


Artist Seyda Perinçek also criticised the prison sentence imposed on Nûdem Durak, drawing attention to the increasingly serious health conditions of sick prisoners. Stating that the release of sick prisoners would be an important step in the Peace and Democratic Society Process, Perinçek emphasised that the state must take concrete action on this matter.


Perinçek said: “The condition of sick prisoners is becoming increasingly serious. One of them is artist Nûdem Durak who has been in prison for 11.5 years because of her work for Kurdish art and Kurdish culture. She is trying to survive under extremely difficult conditions while battling illness.


We must struggle for all sick prisoners, with Nûdem as a particular example. We must take a stand against this torture and this inhumane situation, because our friends are being left to die in prison. The peace process is, above all, a test of sincerity. Addressing the situation of sick prisoners must be the starting point for demonstrating good faith. In particular, our friends who are ill and have been imprisoned for many years must be released.”


Nûdem is in prison for her dedication to Kurdish culture and art


Bermal Çem, speaking on behalf of Hünera Mizgîn, said that Nûdem Durak had been punished for her contributions to Kurdish culture and art. Çem said that Durak had been held in prison for years and was struggling with serious health problems. She added that her illness was progressing and that she was at risk of losing her voice. Emphasising that the situation of sick prisoners is not merely a concern for their families and loved ones, but a matter for society as a whole, Çem appealed to intellectuals, human rights defenders and politicians.


Çem added: “Nûdem was arrested despite being innocent and has been held in prison for years. Her only ‘crime’ was contributing to Kurdish culture and art and keeping them alive. Today, she is fighting for her life in prison while suffering from cancer. Despite this serious illness, she was sentenced to 19.5 years in prison. Her condition is deteriorating, and she could even lose her voice.

title: A border built with water: Six dams in succession
content:
There are six dams along a stretch of just 45–50 kilometers on the Ortasu (Rubozik) Stream, located on the border between Northern Kurdistan (Bakur) and Southern Kurdistan (Başur). Under normal circumstances, dams should either not be built because of the damage they cause to the ecological balance, or should only be constructed following an Environmental Impact Assessment for irrigation, flood prevention and electricity generation. However, these six dams serve a somewhat different purpose. The 2007 activity report of the State Hydraulic Works (DSI) states that their function is entirely security-related. This represents an unprecedented category worldwide, a new type of dam.


A look at the map reveals that all six dams have been built along a single stream. Each has its own tender, dam structure and reservoir. Yet for those living in the valley, they are all part of the same story: villages whose roads have been cut off, whose pastures and farmland have been lost, and whose residents face the winter fearing landslides and floods.


The fundamental question that needs to be asked is: Why does the Turkish state use dams so extensively as a security instrument in Kurdistan?


'Security dams': A new category


A report published in the newspaper Hürriyet on 26 October 2011 clearly revealed why these six dams were being constructed. The report emphasized that the dams were intended to "solve the problem" by flooding caves used by guerrillas and people engaged in cross-border trade. The deep valleys of Aynatepe, Gürbül Mountain, Bezenik Mountain and Düğün Mountain, which form the border stretching from the Qilaban (Uludere) district of Şırnak (Şirnex) to the Çelê (Çukurca) district of Hakkari (Colemêrg), contained strategic locations. Guerrilla transit routes also passed through these valleys.


A project tendered in 2008 and prepared by the DSI for "energy storage" along the borders with Iraq and Iran included a total of 11 dams. Seven were located in Şırnak (Silopi, Şırnak, Uludere, Ballı, Kavşaktepe, Musatepe and Çetintepe), while four were in Hakkari (Gölgeliyamaç, Çocuktepe, Beyyurdu and Aslandağ).


Reports based on a DSI map obtained by the press in July 2009 stated that the reservoirs would flood hundreds of caves and crossing points used by the Kurdistan Workers' Party (PKK), cut off logistical support and prevent infiltration and smuggling.


The military and strategic function of the dams


The primary rationale behind the construction of these dams was a strategy of territorial control. The deep valleys along the border formed natural corridors for the PKK's logistical and shelter networks. By filling these valleys, the reservoirs physically block transit routes while also restricting military movement in the region.


This represents a concrete shift from the tactics of the 1990s, characterized by "burn the villages, dry up the water," toward an approach based on "transforming the terrain to prevent operations." The dams reinforce the border with a natural barrier while simultaneously reshaping the region's socioeconomic structure. However, the long-term ecological and social costs of this strategy have not been adequately discussed in public.


Reshaping geography in the name of 'securitization'


Rather than resolving the Kurdish question through peaceful means, the state sees no problem with reshaping the region's geography and ecosystem and displacing its inhabitants through securitization policies. Dams built in succession are turning artificial borders into natural barriers.


The term "security dam" appeared in the DSI's 2007 report, although officials later stated that these dams were being constructed for irrigation and energy production. While official discourse presents them as "energy and irrigation investments," the experiences of villagers in the region do not correspond to this narrative.


It has been reported that the canals and distribution networks required for irrigation have largely not been constructed, while electricity generation remains limited to a total installed capacity of 15 megawatts. This capacity reportedly represents just 0.044 percent of the total installed capacity of hydroelectric power plants in Turkey.


Meanwhile, the risks of landslides, water leakage and flooding caused by the dams pose serious dangers to local communities. This situation reinforces criticism that the dams' primary function is not "development" but "keeping the region under control."

title: Akın: Policies destroying nature and society must end for ecological peace
content:
The Conference of the Parties (COP), held annually under the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) to combat climate change, brings together countries from around the world. The 31st conference (COP31), which will address critical issues such as climate finance, reducing greenhouse gas emissions and the energy transition, will take place in Antalya from 9 to 20 November 2026.


However, the deepening ecological crisis despite nearly 30 years of conferences has reignited debate over the role of these summits in combating climate change. Ecologists are questioning whether these meetings offer genuine solutions for protecting nature and the climate.


Ibrahim Akın, Co-Deputy Chair of the Peoples' Equality and Democracy Party (DEM Party) responsible for Ecology and Agriculture, spoke about the importance of ecological peace in the context of the Peace and Democratic Society Process, the background of the summit and the People's Climate Summit, which has emerged as an alternative gathering ahead of COP31.


'Ecological destruction impoverishes and displaces peoples'


Ibrahim Akın defined ecological peace as restoring balance in the relationship between humanity and nature and freeing nature and living environments from exploitation. He drew attention to the impact of ecological destruction on peoples and said: "Under capitalism, nature has been transformed into a source of capital accumulation. Our land, water and air have been turned into commodities. The exploitation of nature has been added to the exploitation of labor. Peoples who resist this plunder have often been confronted by state security forces, the judiciary and mechanisms of repression. Therefore, attacks on nature do not merely cause ecological destruction. They also impoverish peoples, displace them and sever their ties with their history and culture. In this respect, ecological destruction is part of the war being waged against the people."


'

Ecocide is also a devastating attack on the future of societies'


Akın said that ecological peace carries a meaning beyond the silencing of weapons in the context of the Peace and Democratic Society Process, emphasizing that it requires an end to policies that destroy nature and society. He continued: "Social peace cannot be achieved without guaranteeing peoples' right to have a say and make decisions over their lands, waters and living environments. To achieve this, the commodification of nature must end, the will of local communities must be recognized and acts of ecocide must be stopped. Ecocide is a devastating attack not only on nature but also on the future of societies that live in harmony with it. A system that continues to wage war against nature cannot promise genuine peace to humanity.


Ecological peace means taking steps to heal nature wounded by war and enabling humanity and nature to establish an egalitarian, free and sustainable relationship."


'The deepening ecological destruction despite more than 30 years of summits is no coincidence'


Ibrahim Akın said that the deepening ecological destruction, despite more than 30 years of summits, signed agreements and announced targets, was no coincidence. He explained the reasons as follows: "This is because the climate crisis is the product of a capitalist system of production and consumption that regards nature as an unlimited reservoir of raw materials, labor as a cheap input for production and every aspect of life as a source of profit. We cannot overcome this crisis by relying solely on technological solutions, carbon markets and international commitments without questioning capital's need for unlimited growth or confronting the interests of fossil fuel companies and major monopolies.


This does not, of course, mean that international cooperation or COP summits are unimportant. However, we must also acknowledge the limitations of these platforms, whose interests they serve and what their decisions actually change in real life. Nevertheless, I see COP summits as platforms that make it possible to bring the climate crisis onto the international agenda."


Turkey's insincere and contradictory approach


Akın drew attention to what he described as Turkey's insincere approach to preparations for COP31, saying that the summit was being treated as an international promotional event rather than an opportunity to confront the root causes of the climate crisis. 


Akın said: "Instead of confronting the causes of the climate crisis …

title: DEM Party: Workplace deaths are consequence of a system of impunity that protects capital
content:
In a written statement, the Labour Commission recalled that on 8 November 2025, a fire broke out at a perfume-filling factory belonging to Ravive Kozmetik in the Dilovası district of Kocaeli. Seven workers, three of them children, lost their lives and six others were injured. “A year has passed. Yet, just as the pain of the families of the seven workers we lost has not subsided, their search for justice has still not yielded results,” the statement said.


The statement continued: “What happened in Dilovası was not a workplace accident, but the result of a model of production that disregards workers’ health and their right to life, of a lack of inspections, and of the capital’s insatiable pursuit of profit. This tragedy, which occurred at a workplace where children were allegedly employed under precarious conditions and where occupational safety measures were reportedly absent, has once again exposed the scale of exploitation in working life and the serious problems with regulatory and inspection mechanisms.”


The DEM Party underlined that “the demands of families who have lost their loved ones are clear, everyone bearing responsibility must be brought to trial, no defendant must receive preferential treatment, and justice must be delivered in every respect. This case is not only about employers. It must also establish how a workplace reportedly operating without a licence was able to continue its activities, as well as the responsibility of the public institutions and officials charged with carrying out inspections. Responsibility cannot be confined to just a few individuals.”


The statement also called for an end to precarious and unregistered employment, the removal of barriers to trade union organisation, and the establishment of independent and effective inspection mechanisms.


Commemorating the seven workers who lost their lives in Dilovası and expressing its support for their families’ struggle for justice, the DEM Party concluded: “We want a legal system that eases the families’ suffering through justice, rather than deepening it through releases from custody. We will continue to follow this case through to the very end.”

title: Apoist prisoners: Fulfil the requirements of the process
content:
Apoist prisoners said in a statement: “Do not leave the Peace and Democratic Society Process at the level of rhetoric; fulfil its requirements! The physical freedom of our Leadership, along with the immediate release of all sick prisoners, is an issue on the agenda of this process that cannot be postponed.”


The statement added: “We, as political prisoners who have been held behind bars for years because of our ideas, our political identity and our commitment to our people's struggle for freedom, address our people and the public today.


The Peace and Democratic Society Process, initiated by our Leadership, represents a strategic shift and transformation aimed at rebuilding social life, political relations and approaches to struggle on democratic foundations. The transition from a strategy of armed struggle to one of democratic society and democratic politics places historical responsibilities on all social and political actors, above all the state and those in power. Concrete steps in keeping with the spirit of this process must be taken, the conflict-ridden conditions of the past must be overcome, and the way must be opened for a democratic solution.”


The statement continued: “However, the failure to take the democratic and legal steps required by the process, together with the government's delaying tactics and its tendency to drag things out, is having severe and potentially irreversible consequences, particularly for political prisoners behind bars. While there is talk of making peace part of social life and opening the way for democratic politics, prisons continue to be treated as places of isolation, punishment, the imposition of repentance and the breaking of prisoners' will. This is in clear contradiction with the very essence of the process.


Today, hundreds of our comrades are facing serious health problems, progressive illnesses and conditions that threaten their lives. Delays in hospital transfers, the obstruction of medical treatment and the failure to provide humane conditions appropriate to their health needs are unacceptable. When the right to life and the right to health are at stake, no political, administrative or security-related justification can absolve the authorities of their responsibility. Continuing to hold seriously ill prisoners in prison means openly putting their lives at risk.”


Condolences to the family of Tuncer Sağlam


The statement recalled that “most recently, the death of our comrade

Tuncer Sağlam

, who had been battling advanced cancer and who, despite all the conditions of imprisonment, never wavered in his commitment to the struggle for freedom and a democratic society, is a painful expression of this reality. His death has once again demonstrated that the right of sick prisoners to healthcare and medical treatment is an urgent matter of the right to life that cannot be postponed.


We remember our comrade Tuncer Sağlam for his commitment to the free Kurdish will, his people and the struggle for a democratic society. In his person, we also remember with respect and gratitude all our comrades who have fallen as martyrs in prison. We extend our condolences to our patriotic people, particularly his family and loved ones, and reaffirm our pledge to keep his struggle and memory alive through the construction of a democratic society and a free life. The Peace and Democratic Society Process requires that the issue of political prisoners currently held in prisons be addressed from the perspective of a democratic solution. For peace to take root in social life, concrete steps must be taken in those areas where the most serious human rights violations occur.”


The statement underlined that “the arbitrary implementation of sentence enforcement provisions established within the existing legal framework, and the continued deprivation of freedom of political prisoners who have completed their sentences on various administrative pretexts, are unacceptable. Allowing political considerations to determine release procedures, imposing demands for expressions of repentance and pursuing policies of pressure intended to break prisoners' will are incompatible with any claim to democratisation. No one should be imprisoned because of their ideas, political identity or stance in the struggle for democracy.


In this regard, seriously ill prisoners must be released immediately and granted unconditional access to medical treatment and healthcare services. Our comrades who have completed their …

title: Whereabouts of KJAR members detained in Urmia unknown since June
content:
The Kurdistan Free Women’s Community (KJAR) announced that it has been unable to obtain any information about two of its members detained by Iranian security forces in Urmia.


In its statement on Sunday, KJAR reported that its member Zahra Pirdehghan (32) was detained by Iranian state forces on June 25, while another member, Parvin Rasegh Qizilbash (33), was detained on June 28. The organization described the detentions as a clear violation of human rights.


According to the statement, the families reported that despite the considerable time that had passed since the two women activists were detained, they had received no information about where they were being held, their health conditions, or their fate. Neither the security authorities nor judicial institutions provided any information regarding their situation.


KJAR warned that depriving its members of their rights to legal representation, regular communication, and contact with their families, as well as subjecting them to enforced disappearance, constituted violations of international law.


The organization demanded that the fate of its members be disclosed immediately and called for their fundamental rights, including access to medical examinations and communication, to be guaranteed.

title: ‘We cannot envision peace independently of any people or culture’
content:
As the Peace and Democratic Society Process continues, women came together to discuss the process and share their experiences of peacebuilding. Hundreds of women gathered at the “Women Side by Side, Discussing the Future” conference to address cultural, political, and social issues. Attended by women from various cities across Kurdistan and Turkey, the conference in Ankara explored women’s roles in peace processes and their ongoing efforts, as well as issues related to ecology and mother-tongue rights.


Painter Neşe Toprak, who attended the conference as a representative of the cultural sector, reflected on its atmosphere and outcomes. Emphasizing that efforts to embed peace in society must encompass all peoples and social groups, Toprak highlighted the importance of women, culture, ecology, and the struggle for mother-tongue rights in the process.


Toprak explained that the conference was organized to give concrete expression to women’s role as active participants in the process. Following nearly two months of preparation, it was held under the leadership of 82 organizing groups. The conference brought together participants from numerous cities across Turkey and from Europe, including women working to ensure that peoples can freely preserve and express their own languages, cultures, and civilizations.


https://video.anf-news2.com/live/firat/21711330_20261107194045_2026-11-08-amed-nese-toprak-barisin-toplumsallasmasi-kadinlarin-ortak-mucadelesiyle-mumkun_1.mp4


‘Peace must encompass all peoples’


Describing the conference as a highly attended event with an exciting atmosphere, Neşe Toprak said that hopes for an end to the policies of assimilation and war that the Kurdish people had faced for years generated optimism about the new process. Highlighting the significance of discussions resuming after an interruption of nearly ten years, Toprak said that extensive assessments had been made on what it means to embed peace in society, what kinds of initiatives could be undertaken in different areas, and how peace could be brought into everyday social life.


Toprak noted that the conference featured sessions and panels attended by women politicians, where participants discussed how political peace could be built and reflected in society. Women from different areas of struggle shared their experiences, emphasizing that culture and ecology were also fundamental components of efforts to embed peace in society.


Stating that ecology was another major topic on the conference agenda, Toprak said discussions had taken place within the framework of the democratic, ecological, and women’s liberation paradigm. Drawing attention to the exploitation of nature and ecological destruction in Kurdistan, Toprak said:


“We cannot consider ecology separately from social peace. What we mean by bringing peace into society encompasses every aspect of life. Culture, ecology, and women’s freedom are all integral parts of life. We depend on the land we live on, so we must take responsibility for it and protect nature.


At the conference, we focused particularly on the exploitation of nature in Kurdistan, ecological problems, and how to combat them. We discussed how to build a better life, protect nature, and develop an ecological way of living.”


‘Every people should have the right to education in their mother tongue’


Emphasizing the important role of culture in embedding peace in society, Neşe Toprak said that mother-tongue rights and the right to education in one’s mother tongue were among the key issues discussed at the conference.


Noting that they were working in the field of Kurdish culture and art, Neşe Toprak said, “We see ourselves not merely as artists but, more importantly, as people working to preserve and promote culture. For this reason, we cannot consider culture separately from peace and its integration into society. There was extensive discussion, particularly about mother-tongue rights and the right to education in one’s mother tongue. We emphasized that every people should be able to receive education in their own mother tongue.”


Stressing that the Kurdish people’s struggle could not be viewed separately from the struggles of other peoples for their languages and cultures, Toprak concluded: “We are not struggling solely for the Kurdish people. We attach importance to the struggles of all peoples whose languages, cultures, and very existence have been denied and who have been subjected to assimilation. The demands …

title: Bayındır: The Turkish state must now take concrete steps
content:
The co-chair of the Democratic Regions Party (DBP), Keskin Bayındır, called on the Turkish government to finally take concrete legal and political measures in the ongoing peace process. “The end of the armed struggle does not mean that the Kurdish question has been resolved,” Bayındır said at an event in Götzis, Austria. Following the dissolution of the PKK and the decision to withdraw guerrilla forces, the Turkish state must now fulfill its responsibilities, he stated.


Murat Sarısaç, co-spokesperson of the DBP’s Diplomacy Commission, also attended the meeting at the Sara Cultural Association in the Austrian state of Vorarlberg. Discussions focused on the Peace and Democratic Society Process in Turkey and political developments in South and West Kurdistan.


https://video.anf-news2.com/live/firat/e11beaa9_20261107200749_2026-11-07-gotzis-keskin-bayindir-ve-murat-sarisac-surece-iliskin-konustular_1.mp4


Democratic integration instead of assimilation


At the beginning of the event, Sarısaç recalled the Kurdish people’s decades-long struggle for political and cultural rights. He emphasized that the democratic integration of Kurds into Turkey’s state structures must not entail either subjugation or assimilation.


“The identity, language, and political existence of the Kurdish people must be recognized. Kurdish national unity must be strengthened, and the organizing efforts of women and young people must be further developed,” Sarısaç stated.


Bayındır described the Kurdish freedom movement’s decision to end the armed struggle as historic steps. He said that Kurdish leader Abdullah Öcalan had advocated a peaceful solution at various stages in the past. Ankara must now create the conditions for democratic restructuring, he underlined.


According to Bayındır, this would require constitutional recognition of Kurdish identity, education in the mother tongue, guarantees for political participation and freedom of organization, and stronger municipal self-governance. Legal provisions underpinning the denial of Kurdish rights must also be amended, he said.


Öcalan’s messages to the KDP and PUK


Addressing the political crisis in South Kurdistan, Bayındır warned that disputes between Kurdish parties could jeopardize the achievements of the Kurdistan Autonomous Region. He stressed that existing differences must be resolved through dialogue.


In this context, he reported on diplomatic contacts undertaken on behalf of Abdullah Öcalan. According to Bayındır, Öcalan sent letters to political parties in South Kurdistan, which were delivered by DBP representatives. Meetings were held with both Nechirvan Barzani of the Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP) and Bafel Talabani of the Patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK).


Bayındır said Öcalan had particularly emphasized the need to strengthen Kurdish national unity and restructure the Peshmerga forces. He stated that these forces should be removed from the control of individual parties and brought together under a unified defense structure. He stressed that political tensions in South Kurdistan affected the entire Kurdish population and must not be allowed to escalate further.


Constitutional guarantees for Rojava


The political future of Rojava was also discussed at the meeting. Bayındır called for the rights of the Kurdish population, their language and culture, and the democratic achievements of the autonomous administration to be enshrined in the Syrian constitution.


He referred to the diplomatic efforts of Mazlum Abdi and Ilham Ehmed, who are involved in negotiations over Rojava’s future. According to Bayındır, progress has already been made. “The crucial task now is to translate the outcomes of these negotiations into binding constitutional provisions,” he added.


Following the speeches, Bayındır and Sarısaç answered questions from participants.

title: Culture and arts festival in Rome commemorates Nagihan Akarsel
content:
The 'Voce Arcaica' (Ancient Voice) Art and Culture Festival, organised annually in Italy by the Jineolojî Academy, was held in memory of Nagihan Akarsel, a member of the Jineolojî Research Centre, writer and journalist who was assassinated in an armed attack outside her home in Sulaymaniyah (Silêmanî) on 4 October 2022.


The festival took place on November 7 at the Teatro Biblioteca Quarticciolo in Rome. The morning program featured performances and sound and rhythm workshops focusing on the ancient voices of women. The activities, attended by Italian, Kurdish, and migrant women, explored women’s experiences of transforming sorrow, grief, and emotions into artistic expression.


https://video.anf-news2.com/live/firat/128d852f_20261108112548_2026-11-08-roma-jineoloji-avrupa-akademisi-onculugunde-nagihan-akarsel-kultur-ve-sanat-festivali-ile-anildi-1.mp4


Women’s voices and solidarity brought to the stage


The evening arts program featured music, dance, film, and theater performances. Inspired by the mulberry tree that Nagihan Akarsel loved, the stage was designed around a forest theme, conveying the message: “When one tree is cut down, we become a forest of ‘Jin, Jiyan, Azadî’.”


Performers at the festival included Rachele Andrioli and the musical group Coro a Coro, Kurdish artist Deniz Deman, Controchiave Theater, the Le Coeur choir, Acab Coro, and the Jineolojî Choir. Through their songs and performances, the women artists explored themes of women’s struggle, intergenerational solidarity, resistance against patriarchy, and respect for nature.


Festival held in different cities across Italy


The festival preparations, which began in Reggio Calabria in September, concluded in Rome following a series of traveling events in Turin and Bologna. Throughout the festival, panels, readings, and knitting workshops focusing on Nagihan Akarsel and women’s identity were held.


Organizations and institutions including Rete Jin, Oltretorino, Donne che intrecciano il futuro, Quarticciolo Ribelle, Non Una di Meno Roma, and Quarticciolo Theater also contributed to organizing the festival.


The organizers emphasized that art and culture are integral parts of everyday life, serving not only to preserve memory and give meaning to life but also as means of resisting social crises.


Nagihan Akarsel, a prominent figure in the Kurdish women’s movement, was killed in a Turkish attack in Sulaymaniyah on October 4, 2022. The festival aims to keep Akarsel’s memory alive and strengthen women’s cultural production and struggle for freedom.


'Voce Arcaica' Festival in memory of Nagihan Akarsel to take place in Rome on 7 November

title: Ex-Financial Insider: ‘I Predicted 2008. This Will Be WORSE’.
content:
In 2007, Richard Murphy, a chartered accountant and tax justice campaigner, accurately foresaw the global financial crisis. His insights into that crisis caught the attention of leaders from David Cameron to Barack Obama, and led to global tax evasion reform.


Today, in 2026, Richard warns that we are heading for an even greater crash. And if the AI bubble bursting coincides with escalating war in West Asia, and the impacts of climate change turbocharged by El Niño, he warns the results could be ‘cataclysmic’.


On Downstream this week, Aaron Bastani sits down with the rogue accountant, campaigner, university professor, whistleblower and, latterly, YouTuber, to discuss the coming poly-crisis. Will the AI bubble bursting be more like the dot com bubble or the 2008 crash? Why are governments including Britain’s telling us to stock up on water and food supplies? And are the Treasury’s claims that there are limits to spending based in truth, or just an excuse for cowardly leadership?

author: Daniel Aloc
title: #TrumpOut: Sampung awiting Pilipino laban sa imperyalismong US at Pax Silica
content:
Nakatakdang bumisita sa Pilipinas si United States President Donald Trump para sa ika-49 na Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) Summit na gaganapin sa Metro Manila sa Nobyembre 16–18, 2026. Ngunit sa halip na salubungin nang pagdiriwang, naghahanda ang mga progresibo at makabayang organisasyon sa malawakang pagkilos upang ipahayag ang pagtutol sa patuloy na panghihimasok at dominasyon ng Estados Unidos sa bansa.

Bitbit ang mga panawagang “Trump Out” at “Reject Pax Silica,” tinututulan ng mga mamamayan ang mga patakarang lalong magtatali sa Pilipinas sa pang-ekonomiyang interes ng US. Kabilang dito ang planong pagtatayo ng Pax Silica industrial hub sa Tarlac.

Kaugnay nito, mahalagang pakinggan ang mga awiting Pilipinong tumatalakay sa imperyalismo, panghihimasok ng dayuhan, at pandarambong sa likas na yaman. Narito ang sampung kantang dapat pakinggan at muling balikan sa pagbisita ni Trump.

Ang title track ng compilation album na inilabas sa kasagsagan ng kampanya para sa pagpapalayas sa mga base militar ng US sa Pilipinas.

Binibigyang-diin ng kanta ang panganib na dulot ng presensiya ng mga base militar, na maaaring maglagay sa Pilipinas bilang target ng mga bansang kaaway ng US.

Sa gitna ng tumitinding tensiyon sa rehiyon, partikular sa pagitan ng Pilipinas at China, nararapat lamang itanong: seguridad ba ng mamamayang Pilipino ang pangunahing pinangangalagaan ng US, o ang sarili nitong estratehikong interes sa rehiyon?

Sabi nga ni Chickoy Pura: “Paalam na, paalam na sa’yo Uncle Sam / Sa inyo ka na maglaro ng baril-barilan!”

Totoong cute ang mga tuta, aspin man o may lahi. Ngunit kapag ginagamit ang salitang “tuta” upang ilarawan ang isang lider na sunud-sunuran sa dikta ng dayuhan, nagiging matalim itong pampulitikang insulto.

Madalas makita sa mga plakard tuwing rali ang katagang “Tuta ng Kano” bilsng pagpuna sa pangulong inuuna ang interes ng imperyalistang US kaysa sa kapakanan at soberanya ng mamamayang Pilipino. Tumpak na tumpak ang paglalarawang ito sa administrasyong Marcos Jr., na sagad-sagaring tuta ng Kano.

Sa mahabang kasaysayan ng bansa, paulit-ulit nang nagpalit ng mga pangulo, ngunit nanatiling nakatali ang Pilipinas sa Estados Unidos. Umaasa pa rin ang gobyerno sa suporta ng Washington sa gitna ng sigalot sa West Philippine Sea, sa ilusyon ng Mutual Defense Treaty, habang patuloy na ipinapatupad ang mga polisiyang pang-ekonomiyang nakasandig sa interes ng dayuhang kapital.

Isang satirikong alegorya tungkol sa historikal na relasyon ng Pilipinas at Estados Unidos ang Pinggan. Bahagi ng compilation album na Karapatang Pantao, ginagamit ng kanta ang kuwento nina Juan at Sam upang ilarawan ang di-pantay at mapagsamantalang ugnayan ng dalawang bansa.

Mahalagang balikan ang mensahe ng Pinggan: hindi tunay na pagkakaibigan ang isang relasyong ang makapangyarihan lamang ang nakikinabang habang patuloy na pinagsasamantalahan ang mahina. Hindi maituturing na patas ang ugnayan kung ang isang panig lamang ang nagdidikta ng mga tuntunin at ang kabila ang kailangang sumunod.

Isinulat nina Ed Formoso at Joey Ayala para sa album na Ikalawang Yugto ng supergroup na Lokal Brown, tinatalakay ng Pay U ang isang mahalagang suliranin ng ekonomiya ng Pilipinas: ang pagiging import-dependent at export-oriented nito.

Sa kabila ng likas na yaman at lakas-paggawa ng bansa, nananatiling nakasandig ang malaking bahagi ng ekonomiya sa pag-aangkat ng mga yaring produkto at pagluluwas ng mga hilaw na materyales. Sa ilalim ng neoliberal na balangkas, napahihina ang kakayahan ng Pilipinas na paunlarin ang sariling industriya, palakasin ang agrikultura, at makamit ang tunay na pagsasarili sa ekonomiya.

Ngunit sa halip na paunlarin ang sariling kakayahan sa produksyon, patuloy na itinatali ang bansa sa pandaigdigang sistemang pang-ekonomiya kung saan nananatiling nakikinabang ang malalaking dayuhang korporasyon.

Tampok ang tinig ni Bayang Barrios at isinulat ni Danny Fabella, inilalahad ng Igpaw, Mindanao ang mapaminsalang epekto ng malawakang pagmimina sa mga mamamayan ng Mindanao.

Sa ngalan ng tubo, napipilitang lumikas ang mga katutubo mula sa kanilang mga lupang ninuno upang bigyang-daan ang mga dambuhalang minahan. Kaakibat ng mga proyektong ito ang pagkasira ng kagubatan at mga ilog, gayundin ang pagkitil sa kabuhayan at karapatan ng mga komunidad na matagal nang nangangalaga sa kanilang mga lupain.

title: DA TORINO ALLA CALABRIA NESSUNO PUÒ FERMARCI!Ferdinando libero, tutti e tutte libere.
content:
La zelante procura di Torino ha emesso in questi giorni una serie di misure cautelari, tra cui arresti domiciliari e carcere, per colpire e criminalizzare le migliaia di persone che lo scorso gennaio si sono mobilitate dopo lo sgombero del centro sociale Askatasuna.


È evidente che si tratta di una vera e propria vendetta da parte di un governo che, incapace di dare risposte al Paese reale sul carovita e sulle conseguenze di un’economia di guerra, decide di arginare il dissenso con la repressione.

Ma il tentativo è fallito ancora prima di cominciare, come dimostrano le piazze piene delle ultime settimane e come dimostreranno quelle che verranno.

A gennaio, nelle strade di Torino, eravamo oltre 50.000, arrivati da tutta Italia. E c’eravamo anche noi.

Perché quella mobilitazione era un ulteriore, importante momento di risposta all’attacco contro le lotte sociali, dopo la sollevazione di massa dello scorso autunno per la Palestina e contro il genocidio.

Quella giornata ha avuto il merito di essere una tappa necessaria tra il “Blocchiamo tutto” e le proteste che nell’ultimo mese, da Nord a Sud, hanno immobilizzato il Paese, in un’onda lunga di contestazione e opposizione a scelte politiche scellerate.

Sfidare Meloni e i suoi tentativi di silenziare il conflitto sociale era e resta urgente e necessario.

È l’impegno comune che abbiamo assunto anche in Calabria, contro chi vorrebbe la nostra terra relegata al silenzio, alla povertà e all’emigrazione forzata.

Il tentativo di fermare compagni e compagne, colpevoli di essersi opposti e opposte con generosità alla volontà di silenziare la voce di Askatasuna, è fallito, e non saranno le misere vendette di questi giorni a cambiare la storia.

Tra le persone private della libertà c’è anche Ferdinando, da sempre in prima linea nelle lotte sociali, attualmente agli arresti domiciliari.

La solidarietà è lo strumento che abbiamo a disposizione, quello che impedisce a qualunque governo di pensare di poter fermare o silenziare l’opposizione sociale, a qualsiasi latitudine.

Oggi solidarietà significa continuare la lotta, rafforzare le mobilitazioni contro il governo della guerra e del carovita, continuare a spenderci per una trasformazione radicale del presente.

Noi non lasciamo indietro nessuno, e già dai prossimi giorni organizzeremo la solidarietà ai nostri compagni e alle nostre compagne.

Ci vediamo dove bisogna stare, in piazza, di nuovo il 20 novembre!


La Base Cosenza
